## BACKLOG G anchor search: outcome [2026-09-28, branch backlog-g, read-only]
TARGET CLAIM searched for (stated precisely, not "load transfer in
general"): a construction attributing per-axle lateral force using
measured/known vertical axle load -- axle Fy in proportion to, or as a
stated function of, its normal load. Context: Module 4a computes
Fy_f = m*ay*front_fraction + Iz*psidd/L, Fy_r = m*ay - Fy_f (rigid-body
force + yaw-moment balance, no Fz); BACKLOG G asks whether measured Fz
should inform that split.
VERDICT: NO DIRECT ANCHOR in any of the five available texts. BACKLOG G
is BLOCKED ON LITERATURE per CLAUDE.md's stop-and-ask rule (Tier A, no
anchor -> stop). Every text that constructs an axle Fy split does so from
force and moment equilibrium with the CG-to-axle distances; none brings
measured normal load into that split. Physical reading (mine, stated as
reasoning, not a quote): the moment balance is exact for the rigid body,
so a load-proportional split would contradict it whenever axle load
fractions differ from b/L (longitudinal transfer, aero), unless a further
modelled force/moment is added -- which no text supplies.
READABILITY: Milliken & Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics
(docs/literature/Racecar_vehicle_dynamics.pdf, 928 pp.) has NO text
layer; read visually from pymupdf renders, locators are PRINTED page
numbers read off each page (PDF index offset drifts: +31 in ch.5, +33 in
ch.7/18). Kiencke & Nielsen has a garbled text layer (broken font
encoding) -> read visually (offset +10 in ch.9). Rajamani, Segers,
Werner (German) have usable text layers; Rajamani equations read from
renders. This corrects the WP-ELICIT note that the non-Segers texts were
"not searchable": a tool gap (no PDF library in the venv), since fixed by
installing pymupdf into the venv for this package.
PER-TEXT RECORD (verbatim; [DIRECT]/[NEAR-MISS]/[CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR]):
1. Milliken RCVD.
 - Sec. 5.4, p.130 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR, steady state]: "The centrifugal
   force effectively pulling sideways on the vehicle must be reacted in
   a steady turn by the front and rear tire cornering forces which in
   this case are obviously equal. In general, the vehicle acts as a
   horizontal beam in lateral force and moment equilibrium" -- "Force
   Equilibrium: CF = Y_F + Y_R" / "Moment Equilibrium: C_F a_F a =
   C_R a_R b (also called yaw moment balance)".
 - Sec. 5.5, p.135 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR; the closest wording to the
   target, and it states the lever, not the load]: "The vehicle acts as
   a horizontal beam or lever. The side force must be reacted at the
   individual tracks in inverse proportion to the CG to track distances
   (in ratio to the wheelbase). Thus the front track takes 2/3 of the
   cornering force and the rear 1/3." Same page: "The static load on the
   front wheels is now 2/3 W and that on the rear 1/3 W". The split
   equals the STATIC load fraction only because both follow from the
   same CG position; the stated mechanism is the lever.
 - Sec. 5.7, p.144 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR, transient]: "N = I_z dr/dt",
   "Y = ma_y", "where N and Y are the resultant yawing moment and
   lateral force that the tires apply to the vehicle (aerodynamic forces
   are not included in the elementary vehicle)." p.149, Eq. 5.6:
   "N = N_F + N_R = Y_F a - Y_R b". Solving gives exactly Module 4a's
   Fy_f = (m*ay*b + Iz*r_dot)/l.
 - Sec. 5.7, p.146 [stated limit]: "The so-called unbalanced forces and
   moments causing acceleration arise totally from the tires in this
   simple model. Since load transfer, camber and aerodynamic effects are
   omitted, only slip angle effects need to be included at the
   appropriate static loads." Footnote 26: "An extension of this model
   could include constant aerodynamic downforce at the front and rear
   and also longitudinal load transfer effects associated with constant
   longitudinal acceleration." -- load enters the TIRE characteristics,
   not the force/moment split; no such extension is given there.
 - Ch.7 intro, p.280 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR]: "the yawing moment on the
   vehicle is simply the difference between the total lateral forces at
   the front and the rear, times their respective distances from the
   CG." / "The total lateral tire force is the sum of the lateral track
   forces."
 - Sec. 7.1, pp.283-285 [NEAR-MISS, capacity/normalisation]: "Any
   calculation of this type assumes the availability of tire data."
   (p.283); "In the general case, W_a should take into account any
   changes in static wheel loads plus longitudinal load transfer if the
   situation of interest involves longitudinal acceleration." (p.284);
   "The lateral track force is the sum of the lateral forces of the two
   wheels ... This force divided by W_a is the lateral acceleration of
   the track (A_Y)_a." (p.285). Load is the NORMALISER of a forward,
   tire-data-driven axle capacity ("lateral force potential diagram"),
   not an attribution of measured Fy. Supports load-normalised axle
   force (the existing fy_*_norm_N display), not G.
 - Sec. 18.4, pp.678-679 and 18.5, p.684 [NEAR-MISS, reverse
   direction]: loads computed FROM lateral/longitudinal acceleration
   ("Total lateral load transfer", "Delta W_X = (h/l) W A_X"). Stated
   limit, p.679: "The information in this section applies only to steady
   turns, no consideration is given to combined lateral and longitudinal
   accelerations or other dynamic situations (i.e., power on/off,
   braking, or rough roads)."
 - Not read this session: ch.2 (tire lateral force vs load), 8.5 (limit
   behavior), 18.3/18.8. These would be "load changes tire capacity"
   material, insufficient for G by the work order's own rule.
2. Rajamani, Vehicle Dynamics and Control.
 - Sec. 2.3, p.28 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR]: Eq. 2.21 "m(y_dd + psi_d V_x)
   = F_yf + F_yr"; "Moment balance about the z axis yields the equation
   for the yaw dynamics as" Eq. 2.22 "I_z psi_dd = l_f F_yf - l_r F_yr".
 - Ch.3, p.55 [CURRENT-CODE ANCHOR, steady state]: "Steady state force
   and moment equilibrium equations for the vehicle yield" Eq. 3.17
   "F_yf + F_yr = m V_x^2/R", Eq. 3.18 "F_yf l_f - F_yr l_r = 0",
   Eq. 3.19 "F_yf = (l_r/l_f) F_yr".
 - Sec. 4.1.5, p.97 [NOTHING for G]: normal loads from pitch balance
   ("The normal force distribution on the tires can be determined by
   assuming that the net pitch torque on the vehicle is zero.").
3. Segers, Analysis Techniques for Racecar Data Acquisition.
 - Ch.10 sec. 10.1, pp.221-222 [NEAR-MISS, reverse direction]:
   Eq. 10.1 "F = W . Glat", Eq. 10.2 "Delta W_Lat = W . Glat . h_COG /
   T" -- loads from lateral acceleration.
 - Ch.15 (Simulation Tools, tire-model subsection before 15.3.5),
   pp.412-415 [NEAR-MISS, capacity model]: "In this equation the lateral
   tire force is dependent of the tire slip angle and the normal load on
   the tire." (Eq. 15.18, Fy = f(alpha) . f(F_N)); "f(FN) is what
   describes the maximum lateral tire force the tire can produce for a
   given vertical tire load." (p.413); "Equations 15.20 and 15.21
   estimate the total lateral tire force of both front and rear wheels,
   respectively, by applying a force equilibrium around the front and
   rear axles." (p.414). A peak-capacity fit for a lap-time-simulation
   tire model from max-load snapshots, not a time-series split of
   measured Fy.
4. Kiencke & Nielsen, Automotive Control Systems.
 - Sec. 9.5, p.387 [NEAR-MISS, model-based]: "One of the most important
   tasks of the identification is to obtain the forces acting upon the
   wheels, which are very difficult to obtain in terms of measurement
   techniques. The longitudinal and lateral wheel forces, F_X and F_Y can
   be determined from the friction co-efficients mu_S, mu_L and the
   wheel ground contact forces F_Zij (Section 8.3.4)."
 - Sec. 9.5.1, pp.388-389: wheel loads from a_X/a_Y (Eqs. 9.47-9.54);
   "During cornering the lateral acceleration causes a roll torque as
   shown in Figure 9.34, whose distribution over the front and rear axle
   depends on the axle load."
 - Sec. 9.5.2, pp.391-392 [NEAR-MISS, the closest in kind]: Eq. 9.57
   "F_Sij = k_red,ij (k1 - F_Zij/k2) . F_Zij . arctan(k3 . alpha_ij)";
   "Equation 9.57 considers the influence of varying wheel loads F_Zij
   (see Section 9.5.1) on the lateral wheel forces." "Based on the
   lateral wheel forces in Equation 9.57 the tire side slip constants
   are recalculated in every time step." (Eq. 9.58 c_ij = F_Sij/alpha_ij).
   Fz-dependent per-wheel Fy, but produced by a TIRE MODEL fed with slip
   angle -- adopting it would make Module 4b's model-free CS estimate
   (dFy/dalpha from measured Fy) circular in alpha and in the tire curve,
   i.e. it runs straight into the documented beta/tire-curve
   identifiability wall. Not a licence for G.
5. Werner 2021 (MA, German).
 - Sec. 4.5.2, p.56 [NEAR-MISS, different consumer]: "Um die effektiven
   Schraeglaufsteifigkeiten mithilfe des Reifenmodells zu jedem Zeitpunkt
   zu berechnen, sind neben den Schraeglaeufen Informationen zur Radlast
   Fz erforderlich. Aufgrund fehlender Sensoren zur Ermittlung der
   Radlasten stehen diese Daten nicht zur Verfuegung, was die Berechnung
   des gierdaempfungsabhaengigen Teils des Giermoments verhindert."
   (umlauts transliterated). Fz is needed for C_alpha,eff inside D_psi
   (Eq. 4.3/4.4) -- the separate "Completing Werner Eq. 4.3" item, not
   the Fy split. ~~Measured Fz is thus better placed as a D_psi input than
   as a split input; that remains its own Tier A question.~~ [SUPERSEDED
   2026-09-29: Werner needed Fz only for his tyre-model route to the
   effective stiffness; this project measures effective stiffness
   directly (Module 4b, model-free), so Eq. 4.3 completes WITHOUT Fz --
   see "Werner Eq. 4.3 completion: anchor check".]
WHAT THE TEXTS DO NOT SUPPORT: attributing measured total Fy (m*ay) to
the axles by measured axle-load fractions; replacing front_fraction
with Fz_f/(Fz_f+Fz_r) in the moment-balance split; any time-series Fy
attribution that uses Fz without a tire model and slip angle.

## BACKLOG G close-out [2026-09-28, branch backlog-g]
BACKLOG G (Fy split from measured axle loads) is BLOCKED ON LITERATURE.
Evidence: the five-text anchor search (entry "BACKLOG G anchor search:
outcome" above) -- Milliken RCVD, Rajamani, Segers, Kiencke & Nielsen,
Werner 2021 all anchor the current moment-balance split (Milliken sec.
5.7; Rajamani Eqs. 2.21/2.22); none splits axle Fy by measured normal
load.
REASONING that makes the negative result structural, not a gap in the
search: m*ay and Iz*psidd give exactly two independent equations for the
two unknown axle lateral forces, so the moment-balance split is the
unique solution given those inputs (verified numerically in the WP-N2
pass 0 record: a*Fy_f - b*Fy_r = Iz*psidd to a max deviation of 7.3e-12
Nm). A measured Fz measures what an axle CAN carry (capacity), not the
lateral force actually flowing through it. Forcing Fy proportional to Fz
would bake into the CS_ratio input exactly the front/rear imbalance that
CS_ratio exists to detect -- the estimator would lose its signal by
construction.
REOPEN CONDITION: a real literature anchor for a load-informed split.

yaw-damping (D_psi) item. Werner sec. 4.5.2 (p.56) needs Fz exactly
there, to evaluate the tyre model's effective cornering stiffness; he
could not complete D_psi because his car lacked wheel-load sensors. That
is its own future Tier A package, proposal-first.~~ [SUPERSEDED
2026-09-29: Werner needed Fz only for his tyre-model route to the
effective stiffness; this project measures effective stiffness directly
(Module 4b, model-free), so Eq. 4.3 completes WITHOUT Fz. The measured-Fz
question therefore has no destination at present; Eq. 4.3 proceeds as
its own package without it.]
CONSEQUENCE: no estimator input changed, so there is no CS threshold
re-derivation and no full-suite G boundary. The gated-kinematic

## Milliken RCVD ch. 2 read: D = mu*Fz citation check [2026-09-28, branch backlog-g]
Read visually from renders (printed pp.13-27, sec. 2.1; no text layer).
SUPPORTED, sec. 2.1 "Tire Load Sensitivity", pp.25-27 (verbatim):
 - p.26: "concept of a friction coefficient defined as mu = Frictional
   force between two bodies / Normal force between two bodies. This
   suggests normalizing (also referred to as nondimensionalizing) the
   lateral force vs. slip angle curve by dividing by the load to give a
   dimensionless measure of the amount of lateral force obtained in
   relation to the load: Lateral force / Load on tire = Lateral Force
   Coefficient, F_y/F_z".
 - p.27: "If they all reached exactly the same value, the peak lateral
   force for any load would be simply (lateral force coefficient) x
   (load on tire)."
 - p.27, the stated LIMIT: "Actually, the peak lateral force coefficient
   (or lateral friction coefficient) is normally higher for the lighter
   loads or, conversely, falls off as the load increases. This effect is
   called the tire load sensitivity." and "For a current Grand Prix tire
   the coefficient may run as high as 1.8 at light load."
 - p.25: "When a particular tire is tested at a series of loads, the
   lateral force curves appear as in Figure 2.8. It will be noted that as
   the load increases, the peak lateral force occurs at a somewhat higher
   slip angle. Also, the cornering stiffness (slope in the elastic range)
   increases."
So D = mu*Fz is anchored as the DEFINITION of the peak lateral friction
coefficient, with Milliken's own caveat that mu is not load-independent
-- which is exactly the load-sensitivity signature the Fz-integration
Phase 2/3 mu-fit found in real data (thesis_notes.md "Fz-integration
Phase 2/3"). The citation now carries its limit.
POINTERS UPDATED (comment-only): modules/tyre_fit_auto.py (two
docstrings) and config/parameters.json _comment_load_normalised ->
"Milliken RCVD ch. 2 (sec. 2.1)".
STILL TO VERIFY, deliberately left untouched:
 - config/parameters.json _comment_mu_plausibility_band cites "Milliken
   RCVD, tyre chapter" for a GT3-slick peak-mu band of 1.2-2.0. Sec. 2.1
   supports the D = mu*Fz definition but gives no GT3 band; its only
   number is "as high as 1.8 at light load" for a Grand Prix tire. The
   band values are not from this text.
 - config/parameters.json _comment_cs_fallback cites "Milliken RCVD, GT3
   slick" for C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 (diagnostics-only consumer). Not
   looked for this session (sec. 2.1 shows cornering stiffness rising

## Gated-kinematic sideslip diagnostic [2026-09-28, branch backlog-g, read-only]
PURPOSE: evidence for the BLOCKED washout-cutoff / sideslip-source
decision. Measures; decides nothing. No production file, config value or
threshold changed. Scripts: diagnostics/inspect_gated_kinematic_run.py
(compute + cache), _cs.py, _drift.py, _scale_sign.py, helpers
gated_kinematic_common.py / gated_kinematic_style.py. Figures in
diagnostics/plots_gated_kinematic/ (gitignored): cs_worst_by_source_
{dubai,v3}.png, drift_vs_time_{dubai,v3}.png, gate_exit_residual_
{dubai,v3}.png, mid_corner_beta_{dubai,v3}.png; numbers in cs_results.
json, drift_results.json, scale_sign_results.json.
METHOD (Tier B preprocessing variant of the same Tier A identity as
estimate_sideslip, Rajamani ch. 2): beta_dot = ay/v - r integrated ONLY
while moving and |ay| > gate threshold; the integrator restarts at 0 on
every gate entry and beta is held at 0 outside the gate (straight-line
sideslip taken as zero). Fully causal (cumulative sum with resets).
Threshold from each session's own racing |ay| distribution by Otsu's
method: Dubai 7.192 m/s^2 (44.9th percentile), v3 8.114 m/s^2 (47.1th);
sensitivity at 0.75x and 1.5x. Comparison sources: production kinematic
(0.05 Hz filtfilt, ZERO-PHASE/ACAUSAL -- never used for a drift claim),
causal lfilter washouts at 0.05 and 0.02 Hz (same Butterworth order),
ekf_auto_pacejka via the production dispatch (resolve_sideslip_beta).
Full production chain per source (slip -> Fy -> CS -> yaw stability ->
summarise_corners), cap=1 config defaults (golden convention).

as the recorded ~6 deg/lap, somewhat smaller), v3 -0.32 % (0.08-1.24

SUMMARY OF PRE-REGISTERED BARS (no recommendation): Bar 1 met in sign at

a decaying reset (no step at gate exit) is untested.

## Werner Eq. 4.3 completion: anchor check [2026-09-29, branch backlog-g, read-only]
Tier A. Werner_2021_MA.pdf (German, text layer usable); page numbers are
the printed ones. Translations are MINE, marked [tr.].
1. Definition, sec. 4.5.2 "Korrelation des Giermoments", p.56:
   "Das Giermoment kann für die Messdaten mithilfe der
   Differentialgleichung aus Gleichung 4.3 und Gleichung 4.4 berechnet
   werden. Das Giermoment setzt sich zusammen aus einem Teil, der von der
   Rotationsträgheit abhängt und einem Teil, der von der Gierdämpfung
   abhängt." [tr.: The yaw moment can be computed for the measured data
   using the differential equation of Eq. 4.3 and Eq. 4.4. The yaw moment
   consists of a part that depends on the rotational inertia and a part
   that depends on the yaw damping.]
   "Die Gierdämpfung ergibt sich aus den effektiven
   Schräglaufsteifigkeiten der Vorder- und Hinterachse sowie den
   Hebelarmen der Achsen zum Schwerpunkt und der Fahrzeuggeschwindigkeit.
   Bei der Ermittlung der effektiven Schräglaufsteifigkeiten ist zu
   beachten, dass diese im nichtlinearen Bereich des Reifens keine
   Konstante mehr darstellen." [tr.: The yaw damping follows from the
   effective cornering stiffnesses of the front and rear axle, the axles'
   lever arms to the centre of gravity and the vehicle speed. When
   determining the effective cornering stiffnesses, note that they are no
   longer constant in the tyre's nonlinear range.]
   Eq. 4.3: Mz = Iz * psi_ddot + D_psi * psi_dot
   Eq. 4.4: D_psi = (C_alpha,f,eff * l_f^2 + C_alpha,r,eff * l_r^2) / v
2. What Fz is needed FOR, p.56:
   "Um die effektiven Schräglaufsteifigkeiten mithilfe des Reifenmodells
   zu jedem Zeitpunkt zu berechnen, sind neben den Schrägläufen
   Informationen zur Radlast Fz erforderlich. Aufgrund fehlender Sensoren
   zur Ermittlung der Radlasten stehen diese Daten nicht zur Verfügung,
   was die Berechnung des gierdämpfungsabhängigen Teils des Giermoments
   verhindert." [tr.: To compute the effective cornering stiffnesses WITH
   THE TYRE MODEL at every instant, information on the wheel load Fz is
   required besides the slip angles. Because sensors for determining the
   wheel loads are missing, these data are not available, which prevents
   the computation of the damping-dependent part of the yaw moment.]
   -> Fz is needed ONLY to evaluate C_alpha,eff through his Pacejka tyre
   model (sec. 2.1.3, MF parameters load-dependent), at the operating
   (alpha, Fz). He assumes Fz comes from wheel-load SENSORS (their absence
   is his stated blocker).
3. What "effective" means, p.56-57: "Da die effektiven
   Schräglaufsteifigkeiten im nichtlinearen Bereich des Reifens abnehmen
   und beim Querkraftmaximum des Reifens den Wert Null annehmen, ..."
   [tr.: Since the effective cornering stiffnesses decrease in the tyre's
   nonlinear range and reach zero at the lateral-force maximum, ...] --
   i.e. the LOCAL TANGENT slope dFy/dalpha at the operating point, per
   axle.
4. His own finding, p.57: "Der trägheitsabhängige Teil des Giermoments
   nach Gleichung 4.3 ist im Vergleich zum dämpfungsabhängigen Teil für
   den Fall des Devbots betraglich zu vernachlässigen. Ebenfalls sind die
   Schräglaufsteifigkeiten von der Radlast Fz abhängig." [tr.: The
   inertia-dependent part of the yaw moment per Eq. 4.3 is negligible in
   magnitude compared with the damping-dependent part for the Devbot.
   The cornering stiffnesses also depend on the wheel load Fz.] He
   continued with a constant C_alpha = 100000 N/rad ("linear tyre at
   Fz = 5000 N") and dropped the comparison as of little added value.
   p.57 also: "Die Gierdämpfung ... die invers von der Geschwindigkeit
   abhängig ist." [tr.: the yaw damping, which depends inversely on
   speed.] Context p.12 (sec. 2.2.2): the transient to steady state is
   "Verzögert durch die Gierträgheit Iz und die Gierdämpfung Dpsi"
   [tr.: delayed by the yaw inertia Iz and the yaw damping D_psi].
SECOND ANCHOR -- Milliken RCVD sec. 5.7, Eq. 5.6, p.149 (read visually
2026-09-28): "N = (aC_F - bC_R)beta + (1/V)(a^2 C_F + b^2 C_R) r - aC_F
delta" -- the r-coefficient (1/V)(a^2 C_F + b^2 C_R) is exactly Werner's
D_psi (Milliken's C are negative by his Table 5.1 sign convention, so
D_psi = -N_r). This, not the sec. 2.1 load-sensitivity material, is the
natural second anchor: sec. 2.1 (p.25: "as the load increases ... the
cornering stiffness ... increases") is qualitative and only matters on
Werner's tyre-model route.
FINDING -- CORRECTS the BACKLOG G redirect written 2026-09-28: the
project's documented adaptation (framing correction 2026-07-24, top of
this file) already estimates the effective per-axle stiffness directly
from logged Fy/alpha (Module 4b, C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r, local windowed
slope, goes to zero/negative past the peak -- the same quantity Werner
defines in point 3). So Eq. 4.4 is COMPUTABLE WITH THIS PROJECT'S
QUANTITIES WITHOUT ANY Fz: C_alpha,eff from Module 4b, l_f/l_r from
cog_position, v from ecu_speed, psi_dot from sclu_yaw_rate. Measured Fz
would only be needed on Werner's own route (tyre model evaluated at the
operating load), which here would run through the kinematic-seeded
fitted Pacejka curve (and the non-production load-normalised D = mu*Fz
fit) and so inherit the documented beta/tyre-curve identifiability
limit. The G note's "measured Fz is better placed as a D_psi input" is
therefore true for Werner's route only, not needed for the adapted
route. Anchor HOLDS for the adapted construction -> proposal written
(docs/proposal_werner_eq43.md).
BOUNDARY: Module 5 regresses mz_inertial only (estimate_yaw_moment_
stability, "D_psi not computed yet"); the chair's reference also uses
the inertial moment only. Adding D_psi*psi_dot to the Module 5
regressand would be an estimator-input change (stab_neg_thresh
re-derivation, itself blocked) AND a chair deviation -- out of v1.

## Werner Eq. 4.3 proposal: approved [2026-09-29, reviewer, author-delegated]
docs/proposal_werner_eq43.md approved for v1 implementation (pure
function + one diagnostic, no Module 5 / payload / UI wiring), with two
implementation conditions:
(a) The hand-worked test case states every input (C_af_eff, C_ar_eff,
    l_f, l_r, v) and its expected value; the diagnostic checks the
    damping-vs-inertia magnitude against Werner's own finding (sec.
    4.5.2 p.57: the inertia part negligible next to the damping part for
    his car) and reports plainly whether it reproduces.
(b) Negative effective stiffness passes through as negative damping,
    presented as physics -- a post-peak axle (Werner p.56-57: effective
    stiffness falls to zero at the lateral-force maximum; beyond it the
    local slope is negative), in the saddle-node stability-loss context
    this project already cites as motivation (Ono et al. 1998, via
    Hoffman et al. 2008) -- never clipped, never replaced.

## Werner Eq. 4.3 v1: damping vs inertial yaw moment [2026-09-29, branch backlog-g]
IMPLEMENTED per docs/proposal_werner_eq43.md: modules/yaw_damping.py
(estimate_yaw_damping, yaw_damping_moment; pure, no config reads), new
registry node accuracy_levels.yaw_damping (Level 1), tests/test_yaw_
damping.py (hand-worked case C_af_eff = C_ar_eff = 100000 N/rad, l_f =
1.1 m, l_r = 1.4 m, v = 40 m/s -> D_psi = 7925 N m s/rad, recomputed
independently before writing; NaN paths; negative pass-through), one
diagnostic diagnostics/inspect_yaw_damping_eq43.py. Nothing wired into
Module 5, the payload or the UI. Production chain as the goldens run it
(ekf_auto_pacejka, cap=1); lever arms l_f = 1.434 m, l_r = 1.071 m from
the static corner-weight split (both sessions, config defaults). Floor:
v <= stability_estimation.moving_speed_min_mps -> undefined.
Figures: diagnostics/plots_yaw_damping/yaw_damping_vs_inertia_{dubai,v3}
.png (gitignored); numbers in yaw_damping_results.json.
COVERAGE: D_psi defined on 59.1 % (Dubai) / 64.7 % (v3) of moving
non-kerb samples -- elsewhere at least one axle's 4b stiffness is
invalid. Corner-phase instances clearing 4b's own phase floor
(cs_phase_min_valid_samples): 158 / 149; apex_3 contributes none (its
fixed window is below the floor, the known reason apex_region exists).
WERNER'S FINDING (inertia negligible next to damping, his sec. 4.5.2
p.57): PARTLY REPRODUCES. Ratio median|D_psi*psi_dot| /
median|Iz*psi_ddot| per corner-phase: Dubai p10 0.72, p50 1.87, p90
7.58, damping larger in 77 %, more than 10x in 5 %; v3 p10 0.45, p50
1.21, p90 3.27, larger in 60 %, more than 10x in 1 %. Damping is
typically the larger term here but does NOT dwarf the inertial term the
way Werner reports for the Devbot -- stated as a finding. By phase
(median ratio): Dubai entry_1 2.33, turn-in 2.86, exit_4 1.37, exit_5
1.51; v3 0.74, 1.32, 1.28, 0.99. Consequence for limitation #6 ("Iz*psidd
only ... same order of magnitude"): the omitted term is of the same
order and usually the larger one -- the limitation is real and not
negligible, but not the order-of-magnitude gap Werner found.
NEGATIVE D_psi (post-peak, passed through unclipped): Dubai 1 of 158
instances (C9 L2 exit_4, front axle negative, 87 % of samples); v3 9 of
149, all exit_4 (C1 L7/L8, C5 L7/L8, C6 L7, C8 L8, C9 L7, C13 L6, C16
L7; front, rear and mixed). These coincide with the negative worst-CS
instances of the same chain (e.g. Dubai C9 front -0.410 L2 exit_4; v3
C1 L8, C5 L8, C8 L8 exit_4) -- expected, both come from the same 4b
stiffness, so this is consistency, not independent confirmation.
Cross-reference: Dubai C4 front saturation (exit_4) -- NOT negative
(per-lap median D_psi 2175 / 1995; only 2 laps clear the floor there,
front contribution positive 1721 / 1925); C3 traction (exit_5) -- NOT
negative on any of 4 laps (3293-11306). A saturated axle at the
worst-CS SAMPLE does not have to make the phase MEDIAN of D_psi
negative; the other axle's damping usually outweighs it.

## v3 NIS health-score drift 0.0849 -> 0.0985: bisect by mechanism [2026-09-29, read-only]
Question: what moved v3's ekf_auto_pacejka health_score from 0.0849
(recorded 2026-09-03) to 0.0985 (2026-09-20 onward) on identical config
inputs? One isolated run per candidate, in order, in memory only
(monkeypatched channels.json readers; no file edited; scratch script,
not a diagnostics deliverable):
1. NIS window rate-correction: EXCLUDED by provenance -- 0.0849 IS the
   post-fix number (entry "Morning follow-up...": v3 0.1163 -> 0.0849
   under the rate-corrected window).
2. channel_corrections / FR gauge decoding: EXCLUDED -- removed in
   memory, score 0.098474 unchanged (structurally expected: the free-D
   fit never reads damper channels).
3. Corner canonicalisation / representative-lap filter: EXCLUDED on
   today's data -- disabling the filter leaves 17 stable corners and the
   score 0.098474 unchanged, because lap 9 is already excluded as
   analysis-invalid (valid laps 6, 7, 8), so the filter has nothing to
   remove. This isolates the filter; it does not isolate the lap-validity
   classification itself.
4. Session weighing: EXCLUDED earlier (0.093809 with the real weighing,
   not 0.0849).
OUTCOME: UNEXPLAINED by the four named candidates. Both values PASS the
current gate (threshold_use_ekf 0.08); no gate verdict is affected.
The 2026-09-20 entry already observed the move and offered the mass/aero
double-count fix as a guess; that path does not reach the free-D fit
(Fy = config mass * ay), so the guess is not supported either. One
plausible, UNTESTED mechanism in the same "fit population" family is
the pit-limiter lap-validity reclassification (also 2026-09-03), which
changes base_mask directly; not on the ordered list, not chased.
AMENDS the gated-kinematic entry's 2026-09-29 correction ("cause not
identified"): candidates 1-4 now excluded as above.
[2026-09-29, FINAL ROUND -- EXPLAINED, entry CLOSED] ~~OUTCOME:
UNEXPLAINED by the four named candidates.~~ Candidate 5, the pit-limiter
lap-validity reclassification (2026-09-03, "Fz-integration Phase 4"),
isolated in memory: v3's lap 9 set back to analysis-valid (its pre-fix
state) in a copied lap list handed to the fit only, parse/corners/files
untouched (scratch script outside the repo). Result: health_score
0.084871 with laps 6-9 vs 0.098474 with laps 6-8 -- the recorded value
reproduced EXACTLY (0.084871 is the six-decimal figure in the NIS gate
band decision entry). The 0.0849 was therefore measured on 2026-09-03
before that day's pit-limiter fix removed lap 9 (which ends ~22 s under
the limiter, an in-lap) from the fit population; the move to 0.0985 is
the intended consequence of the fix, not an unexplained drift. Both
values PASS; no gate verdict affected. The 2026-09-20 entry's guess
(mass/aero double-count fix) is superseded by this. Closed.

(span met inside 0.1 s), among finite CS: Dubai 0.003; v3 0.052, US-v2

## CS smoothing/persistence sweep, ten rows x nine sessions [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Variants in memory, production functions unchanged. B: alpha and Fy
low-pass cutoff (both via cs_filter_cutoff_hz) 1.0 and 0.5 Hz (production
2.0). C: cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad x1.5, x2 (0.03, 0.04 rad; cap 53 m
unchanged). D: read-out persistence of the leading-axle call, 10/25 m. E:
rolling median on CS_ratio, 5/11 samples within finite runs. B1.0+D25.
HARD bar: Dubai C4 worst-lap CS_f < -0.10 (baseline -0.134) AND C3 LS rear
exit_5 negative on 4/4 laps. Figure: diagnostics/plots/new_laps/
flapping_vs_fidelity.png (gitignored).

- A baseline: C4 -0.134, C3 LS 4/4, C3 CS_f -0.333 (record reproduced
  exactly). Mean corner-sample coverage 0.80; lap switch 0.47.
- B 1.0 Hz: DISQUALIFIED (C4 -> +0.365; C3 CS_f -> +0.199). Sample
  flapping x0.52 (mean over sessions); coverage 0.66 (Dubai 0.72 -> 0.46);
  lap switch 0.35, but called lap pairs fall 269 -> 142 -- fewer verdicts,
  not steadier ones. Dubai: 7 of 14 corners to ok.
- B 0.5 Hz: DISQUALIFIED (C4 +0.817, C4 verdict ok -- the driver-flagged
  corner lost). Flapping x0.28, coverage 0.58, lap pairs 56.
- C span x1.5: SURVIVES (C4 -0.117, 0.017 inside the bar; C3 CS_f reading
  lost, +0.088). Flapping x0.73, phase 0.34, lap switch 0.46 (unchanged).
  Coverage 0.63 (Dubai 0.42). Dubai C4 verdict "oversteer @ exit" (rear
  -0.134 wins the tie) -> "understeer @ exit" (rear +0.046).
- C span x2: DISQUALIFIED (C4 +0.422). Flapping x0.52, coverage 0.48
  (Dubai 0.24).
- D 10 m / 25 m: SURVIVE; CS values, verdicts and candidates identical by
  construction. Sample flapping x0.20 / x0.06, phase- and lap-level
  switching unchanged (0.37 / 0.47): verdicts are built from phase
  medians, not from the per-sample call.
- E median 5 / 11: SURVIVE. Sample flapping x0.92 / x0.83; phase medians,
  verdicts and lap switching unchanged (a median of a rolling median is
  nearly the median). No measurable cost, no verdict-level benefit.
- B1.0 + D25: DISQUALIFIED (B1.0's C4 loss). Sample flapping x0.04.

READING BY FAMILY. Input filtering (B) is the only family that reduces
verdict-level switching, and it does so by suppressing the estimator:
slower alpha grows windows into the 53 m cap (NaN, coverage loss), and
the surviving windows span more track, so the regression averages across
the saturation dip -- Dubai C4 erased at both cutoffs. The span floor (C)
acts the same way, more weakly: x1.5 is the only estimator-side row that
keeps C4 (0.017 margin) and it barely changes lap-level switching.
Persistence (D) and output smoothing (E) act only on the sample signal
the verdict does not read: a quieter trace display, no verdict stability.
~~Driver-report agreement~~ [CORRECTED 2026-09-30: a session-type assumption, not a recorded driver report -- see "Provenance correction batch"] (Dubai: US >= OS, no strong severity, C4 flagged)
holds on every row except B 0.5 Hz. The C3 LS traction signature is 4/4
on every row by construction (LS is a separate estimator no variant
touches); the CS-side C3 reading (CS_f -0.333) survives only A, D and E.
A persistence rule that reaches verdicts would have to act on the phase/
lap verdict sequence itself -- a design change not tested here. No winner
declared.

## CS_ratio value lens: smoothness, reproduction, demand bands, A vs B, fold/loop [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script: diagnostics/inspect_cs_value_lens.py (smooth / util / ab /
foldloop; definitions fixed in its header before the runs). Production
chain, value level only (no verdicts or thresholds). Qualifying files
and Le Mans are context rows.

SMOOTHNESS (per corner, then median over corners). Mean |dCS| per 10 ms
sample: front 0.009 (Dubai) to 0.018 (v3), rear 0.006-0.016. The
autocorrelation length of CS_ratio(s) inside corners is 6.3-11.6 m
everywhere, SHORTER than the regression window that produces it (median
footprint 10.2-24.4 m): ratio 0.31-0.74, and below 1 on 12/15 to 14/14
corners per session, Dubai 14/14 on both axles (0.45 front, 0.31 rear).
Brackets are 134-183 m long, so the value varies on a sub-window scale,
not at corner scale. Mechanism, measured: the adaptive window runs as a
sawtooth -- its start stays pinned on an old alpha extreme while the
window grows, then leaps forward in one sample when that extreme leaves.
These start jumps (footprint drop > 2 m between adjacent samples) are
1.1-1.7 % of samples and carry 12-19 % of all |dCS| in every session
(Dubai 15/17 % front/rear), about 10x their share. They are a
concentrated contributor, not the majority. Worked figure:
diagnostics/plots/cs_value_lens/worked_corner_dubai.png (Dubai C7 front,
median pairwise r 0.66; C10 front, r -0.07 -- C10 sits at the 1.0 clip
with windows at the 53 m cap, so r is uninformative there, rms 0.04).

LAP-TO-LAP REPRODUCTION (median pairwise Pearson r of CS(s) on a 1 m
grid, front / rear, session median over corners): Dubai 0.31/0.48, v3
0.33/0.52, US-v2 0.42/0.45, NBR A 0.67/0.74 (2 laps, one pair per
corner), NBR B 0.55/0.58, qualifying CDR 0.50/0.57, MLA 0.60/0.59; Le Mans
not assessable (1 lap). Per-corner range 0.01-0.93. Dubai front
highest C7 0.66, C1 0.52, C14 0.51; lowest C12 0.18, C2 0.03. Dubai C4
(the ground-truth saturation corner) reproduces weakly: front 0.24, rear
0.01.

ay_entry_threshold_g, inside brackets). Session-mean shares front > 0.5 /

NBR B 0.43/0.20, Le Mans 0.62/0.07, CDR 0.51/0.20, MLA 0.48/0.17. Rear
shares > 0.5 are higher and < 0 lower than the front's in every session,

+0.182 (6/6), MLA C3 +0.158 (6/6). No time-loss figure computed (no
reference-lap model).

all 10. The test has no power at this scale: every window spans only
1.15-1.24 deg of alpha (the 0.02 rad span floor), 15-56 samples, and 8
of 10 have zero alpha reversals -- a path whose alpha never reverses
cannot self-cross, so "fold" is guaranteed by construction. The 2026-09-02
ground-truth fold/loop reads used long runs (100 m+), not single windows.
Direction of travel, recorded as found: in all three strongly negative
front windows |alpha| FALLS by about 1.2 deg while |Fy| RISES -- Dubai

results either way; whether this is the post-peak branch traversed back
toward the peak or alpha lagging the force build-up cannot be decided
from the window alone. Figure: diagnostics/plots/cs_value_lens/
fold_loop.png.

## Slip-vs-force lag check [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script: diagnostics/inspect_cs_readout_evidence.py (lag; definitions in
its header). Signals: filtered axle slip angle vs filtered axle Fy (both
through the production 2 Hz zero-phase filter, so any lag is upstream);
lag = peak of corr(alpha(t), Fy(t+k)), |k| <= 50 samples (500 ms);
k > 0 force follows slip, k < 0 slip follows force.

POPULATION (every traversal x axle, production ekf chain): median lag
-2 to +2 samples in every session (Dubai +2, v3 0, US-v2 0, NBR A 0,
NBR B 0, Le Mans -1, qualifying -2/-1); p10/p90 from -4/+2 (Le Mans) to
-12/+26 (v3); share with |lag| >= 5 samples 0.16-0.58. No systematic lag
of window order (windows 30-60 samples): the lag is centred on zero with
a wide per-traversal spread.

CONSEQUENCE. A synthetic LINEAR tyre driven by the real slip trace with
the measured lag, through the production window rule, manufactures
negative CS on its own. Share of production negative samples it
reproduces at the same sample: Dubai 10.2 %, v3 14.9 %, US-v2 8.3 %, NBR A
8.2 %, NBR B 13.7 %, Le Mans 12.5 %, qualifying 22.0 % / 15.3 %. The lag
explains a minority (8-22 %) of the negative population, not the bulk.

DUBAI C4 (front). Lags +4, -8, +14, 0 samples (laps 1-4, i.e. -80 to
+140 ms, at most 7.9 m at local speed). Lap 3 (production min -0.67, 23 negative samples):
the lag-only tyre reaches -0.07 with 1 negative sample -- the lag does
not produce C4's negative reading. Controls (C12, C11, C6): -5..+11
samples. Kinematic beta shifts C4 front to +21..+34 samples and several
control traversals to the +50 search limit: the kinematic chain carries
a large positive lag of its own; the EKF chain's is small.

NBR B C1 (front), the first corner after the long straight. EKF chain:
whole-corner lag -5 to -14 samples on all 6 laps (slip follows force by
50-140 ms); entry segment -23..-30 on 6/6 laps and apex -20..-30 on 6/6,
i.e. at or near the 30-sample search limit, exit -5..-14. Kinematic
beta: whole-corner lag 0 to +15 (the negative whole-corner lag moves
with the beta source -> it lives in the EKF beta dynamics), but the entry
segment stays at -21..-30 on 5 of 6 laps under both sources (not beta-
specific; an entry segment with braking and little lateral content makes
the correlation poorly conditioned). The entry-concentrated pattern after
the low-slip straight is CONFIRMED at NBR C1 under the EKF chain and NOT
present at Dubai C4 (entry +4, -6, -30, 0). Consequence at C1: lap 105
lag-only min -1.42, 60 of its 90 negative samples reproduced; laps 103
and 107 (the deepest, -2.07 / -2.68) 15/179 and 1/88; laps 104, 106, 108
none. The lag explains one C1 lap largely and the deepest ones barely.
STOP condition (systematic lag of window order) NOT met; later results
are not marked conditional, with the stated 8-22 % caveat.

Script: diagnostics/inspect_cs_readout_evidence.py (foldrun). Run =

9.10 kN at 5.47 deg, no post-peak arm). NBR B C1 lap 107 loop (2 -> 1),
lap 103 loop (4 -> 7). No instance shows a post-peak arm (|Fy| falling
by >= 5 % while |alpha| grows by >= 0.02 rad) in forward time. POST-HOC
amendment, stated as such: the C1 runs start at high slip (9.3 deg) and
unwind, i.e. a peaked curve traversed backwards; a time-agnostic fold
criterion was added -- it changes no label, because crossings decide

SPECIFICITY CONTROL (added after the first read labelled almost

C12/C11/C6, NBR B C12/C13/C8, all laps): 22 of 30 read loop, 6 at-peak,
1 rising, 1 lag-artifact; median 3 crossings. A loop at 100 m is what a
healthy corner shows too -- the loading and unloading arms of any
corner cross once there is any hysteresis between them. The test has no
power at single-window scale (value-lens entry) and no specificity at
100 m scale.
C4 STATUS. The 2026-09-02 fold reads (17-32 m runs, visual, then-current
chain: C4 lap 3 peaked at 5.7 deg / 7.5 kN and declined to 7.3 deg) do

DOWNGRADED from "confirmed by fold geometry" to UNCONFIRMED: not shown

Lag-artifact: no focus instance (the lag shift changes no label).

## Sawtooth window-start repair, measured in isolation [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script: diagnostics/inspect_cs_readout_evidence.py (sawtooth, sawreport;
rule and criteria in its header). Rule: start_rep(i) = max(cap limit,
min(start_prod(i), start_rep(i-1) + 2)) -- the start may advance at most
2 samples per step, the window shrinks by at most 1 sample per step. (The
work order's "at most one" would freeze the window length: start and end
both advancing 1 per step means the window can never shrink.) The
repaired window always contains the production window, so the qualifying
set is identical by construction -- verified: identical finite masks in
all 8 sessions, both axles. The diagnostic copy of compute_cs_for_axle
reproduces cached production to median |diff| 1e-8 (float32 cached
inputs; two isolated samples at 3e-3), identical finite masks. The
diagnostic phase slicing reproduces all 5,940 production per-lap phase
medians exactly.

EFFECT (production -> repaired, front; rear alike). Window-start jumps
1.1-1.7 % of samples carrying 12-19 % of |dCS| -> 0 / 0 in every session.
Mean |dCS| step -10 to -16 % (Dubai 0.0094 -> 0.0080, v3 0.0180 ->
0.0162, NBR B 0.0150 -> 0.0130). Autocorrelation length +0.3 to +1.7 m
(Dubai 8.3 -> 8.8, v3 6.6 -> 6.9, NBR B 7.9 -> 8.4 m; Le Mans and MLA
front -0.1/-0.4) -- still well below the window. Median window footprint
+4.1 to +5.8 m (Dubai front 19.5 -> 24.8, v3 10.7 -> 14.9 m), i.e. the
repaired windows are about 25-40 % longer.
CLASSIFICATION by the pre-registered rule: per-lap phase-median shift,
all sessions, median 0.0147 / p90 0.146 (max 1.13, CDR) against the
re-export noise floor (v3 vs US-v1, same outing, 27 ms re-gridding, n =
389) of 0.0156 / 0.159 -> within noise, qualifying set identical ->
COSMETIC. Caveats stated with it: the repair lengthens the regression
support by 25-40 %, so it changes which samples each regression sees even
though it changes no qualification; and the noise floor is itself large
(a 27 ms re-gridding moves phase medians by up to 0.16 at p90), so
"within noise" is a weak statement. The repair removes the jump
component; it does not change the decorrelation scale materially.

## Synthesis for the CS read-out decision [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Written for the author's decision; no recommendation, no implementation.
1. RESOLUTION. CS_ratio decorrelates over 6-12 m inside a 10-24 m window
   on every session including Dubai; lap-to-lap shape correlation
   0.31-0.74; 47 % of consecutive-lap verdict pairs switch axle.
2. LAG. No systematic slip-vs-force lag (session medians -2..+2 samples).
   A lag-only linear tyre reproduces 8-22 % of negative CS samples. NBR C1
   carries an entry-concentrated slip-after-force lag under the EKF chain
   (partly beta-source dependent); Dubai C4's -0.67 is not lag-made.

   fold does not reproduce under today's chain, the single-window test
   has no power and the 100 m test no specificity (healthy controls loop
   22/30). Its negative reading exists only in the worst lap (pooled
   median +0.45).

   identical by construction and measured; phase-median shift 0.015 /

   leaves decorrelation length essentially unchanged; lengthens windows

## Pooled-p25 thresholds by the recorded procedure [2026-09-29, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script: diagnostics/inspect_cs_decision_table.py (thresholds, margin;
procedure in its header). The recorded STRONG/MODERATE derivation made
explicit: STRONG = physical anchor 0, noise population = negatives minus
ground-truth events (none remain, C4 unconfirmed) minus the standout
group beyond the largest gap between consecutive negatives; STRONG = the
noise floor moved outward to the next 0.01. MODERATE = midpoint of the
first gap >= 0.10 among positive values below the clip. Population: per
corner the worst phase of the statistic, per axle. Nothing from driver
reports, A-vs-B or any other check entered.
CHECK against the recorded case (Dubai, worst lap): rear standout {C4},
floor -0.065 -> -0.07 (recorded -0.07); front standout {C9 -0.410, C3
-0.333} (recorded standout group) and floor -0.134 -> -0.14 (recorded
-0.10 additionally excluded C4 as ground truth); MODERATE front 0.074 |
0.229 -> 0.15 (recorded 0.15), rear 0.159 | 0.293 -> 0.23 (recorded 0.20,
placed inside the gap). The rules reproduce the recorded judgement where
its inputs still hold.
POOLED-P25, all eight sessions pooled (derived_from-style trail):
- front: n = 129, p5/p25/median/p75 -0.567/-0.214/-0.049/+0.189;
  negatives n = 74; standout {-1.954} (gap 0.545); noise floor -1.409 ->
  STRONG_CSF -1.41. MODERATE: 51 positives below clip, first gap >= 0.10
  is 0.590 | 0.719 -> MODERATE_CSF 0.65.
- rear: n = 128, p5/p25/median/p75 -0.305/-0.078/+0.064/+0.305;
  negatives n = 48; standout {-0.686, -0.589, -0.587} (gap 0.115); noise
  floor -0.472 -> STRONG_CSR -0.48. MODERATE: 77 positives, no gap >= 0.10
  -> MODERATE_CSR undefined (row B uses an empty moderate band).
PER SESSION (STRONG f / r; MODERATE f / r): Dubai -0.04 / -0.04; 0.31 /
0.27. v3 -0.27 / -0.16; 0.24 / 0.21. US-v2 -0.39 / -0.29; 0.31 / 0.46.
NBR A -0.31 / -0.08; undefined / 0.23. NBR B -0.26 / -0.08; 0.37 / 0.46.
Le Mans -0.52 / -0.15; 0.10 / 0.39. CDR -0.70 / -0.18; 0.24 / 0.27. MLA
-0.58 / -0.05; 0.08 / undefined. Front STRONG spans -0.04 to -0.70 across
tracks.
READING: the recorded procedure presupposes a near-zero noise cluster
separated by a gap from a few genuine events. On one track that holds
(Dubai). Pooled over eight sessions the front population has no such
cluster -- its MEDIAN is already negative (-0.049), 74 of 129 corners sit
below the peak, and the negative tail is continuous -- so the largest-gap
rule lands deep in the tail (-1.41) and the rear finds no moderate gap
at all. The procedure applied faithfully yields degenerate multi-track
thresholds; the track-to-track spread is itself the finding.
MARGIN (cs_margin analogue), recorded method: the 22 recorded +/-1 %
sensitivity runs (5 inputs x 2 signs x Dubai, v3, plus baselines;
setup-sheet corner weights, no accuracy cap, full production chain incl.
the Pacejka refit) re-run keeping the sample arrays; per-phase verdicts
on pooled p25 under the thresholds above. 11 distinct corner-phases
flip. v3 C11 (apex 0.350, turn-in 0.347, exit 0.196) flips under FIVE
unrelated inputs by the same step: its front CS_ratio jumps 1.00 <->
0.19 in PROD and POOLED25 alike -- a discontinuity of the ratio itself
(the linear-reference denominator switches), not a proportional
sensitivity. Excluded as a different mechanism, as the recorded
derivation excluded Dubai C1; 2nd-largest remaining distance 0.057 ->
cs_margin 0.06. Without the exclusion: 0.35 (would mark nearly every
verdict MARGINAL). The C11 discontinuity is a production property too
(PROD jumps identically); under the current thresholds 0.19 and 1.00
both read "ok", which is why the 2026-09-19 sweep did not show it.

## IMU offsets, Part 2: heading closure per lap [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Closure residual E = integral of yaw rate over the lap minus 360 deg with
the lap's sign. Every lap on every track has a negative net heading: one
rotation direction throughout, so direction cannot help separate scale
from bias; only time vs rotation can.
E per lap: Dubai +5.95 to +6.37 deg (125 s), v3 -43.9 to -45.4 (125-126 s),
US-v2 -40.4 to -42.5, JST 21 -31.0/-31.4 and JST 29 -30.2 to -31.6
(116-117 s), CDR -29.9 to -31.3 (115-120 s), MLA -28.5 to -29.9 (114-118 s),
Le Mans +11.5 (238 s). Spread within a session at most 2.2 deg.
Scale e after removing the S0 bias: Dubai -1.39 %, v3 +3.50, US-v2 +4.40,
JST 21 +2.51, JST 29 +5.13, CDR +1.40, MLA -1.47, Le Mans -11.1 %. With the
recorded bias definition (racing, |ay| < 0.25 Otsu, moving samples): Dubai
-1.04 % and v3 -0.32 % (the record, reproduced exactly), US-v2 +1.60,
JST 21 +0.24, JST 29 +2.38, CDR -2.16, MLA -5.59, Le Mans -0.54 %.
MECHANISM: 1 % of scale is 3.6 deg per lap, i.e. 0.03 deg/s of bias over a
120 s lap, while the two straight-line bias references differ by up to 0.16
deg/s (0.07-0.11 on the serial-221 sessions). The scale estimate inherits
that uncertainty: the six serial-221 sessions spread from -1.47 to +5.13 %
(S0) and from -5.59 to +2.38 % (recorded definition), which one logger
cannot carry. Bias-only
reading, E/T: Dubai +0.050, v3 -0.35, US-v2 -0.33, JST 21 -0.27, JST 29
-0.26, CDR -0.26, MLA -0.25, Le Mans +0.048 deg/s; lap-to-lap within about
+/-0.01 deg/s, and within 0.01-0.16 deg/s of the S1 straight medians.
Paul Ricard and NBR (both serial 221) cannot share one (bias, scale) pair:
solving the two tracks' closures jointly gives about -1.1 deg/s and -28 %,
which is not physical, so the bias differs between the two events.
READING AGAINST THE RECORD: the recorded gyro scale (Dubai -1.04 %, v3
-0.32 %) is reproduced under its own bias definition, but it is not
identifiable at the percent level from this data: a 0.03 deg/s change of
the bias reference moves it by 1 %, and no straight-line reference here is
that accurate. The closures are consistent with a per-session constant
bias and a scale near zero; they do not show that scale is zero. The
recorded 5-27 % attribution, which used that scale, carries the same
uncertainty.

## IMU offsets, Part 4: consequence for the in-corner drift [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Dubai and v3 (the sessions of the recorded 2 / 14 deg finding), gated_x1
re-integrated in memory with the cached Otsu threshold.
PRE-REGISTERED CORRECTION (constant S0 medians for yaw rate and ay):
Dubai gate-exit |residual| median 2.00 -> 2.27 deg, max 10.05 -> 12.04;
v3 1.76 -> 2.13, max 14.44 -> 19.79. Slope against heading change +0.039 ->
+0.041 (Dubai), +0.062 -> +0.074 (v3). The correction makes the drift
larger.
POST-HOC DECOMPOSITION (added after that run, labelled as such): yaw only
(S0) Dubai 2.01 / v3 1.86; yaw only with the closure excess (+0.050 /
-0.351 deg/s) 1.96 / 1.82; ay only (S0) 2.26 / 1.98. A yaw-bias correction
moves the median by at most 0.06 deg. On v3 it removes the turn-independent
part (mean residual +0.68 -> +0.05 deg) and leaves the turn-proportional
part (positive turns +3.61, negative -1.94 deg). The straight-line ay
median, applied inside corners, shifts the mean residual by -0.5 to
-1.5 deg: whatever sets straight-line ay does not act as a constant
offset in corners.
MECHANISM: a constant bias gives a drift of one sign in left and right
turns alike. The recorded in-corner drift carries the sign of the turn:
its slope against heading change stays at 0.038-0.075 rad/rad in every
offset row and matches Part 3's odd term a2. Constant offsets
explain almost none of the unexplained drift. It stays a
heading-proportional error between ay/v and r of about 2-7 %; its source
(gyro scale, ay scale, roll-gravity in ay, speed scale) is not separable
here. Part 2 showed gyro scale is not identifiable at the percent level.
STRAIGHTS, kinematic vs EKF (EKF inputs unchanged; EKF median |beta| on S0
0.17 / 0.42 deg): kinematic_prod median |gap| 0.59 -> 0.66 (Dubai), 0.58
-> 0.57 deg (v3); causal 0.05 Hz 0.56 -> 0.63, 0.93 -> 1.10 deg. No better
agreement: the washout already removes a constant bias's integral.

## IMU offsets, Part 5: synthesis [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Per session, yaw bias as closure excess E/T (S0 median) / ay S0 median /
gyro scale / polynomial verdict:
- Dubai: +0.050 (+0.01) deg/s / +0.12 m/s^2 / not identifiable (-1.04 to
  -1.39 % by definition) / constant.
- v3: -0.35 (-0.25) / +0.48 / not identifiable (-0.32 to +3.50 %) /
  constant.
- US-v2: -0.33 (-0.20) / +0.48 / not identifiable (+1.60 to +4.40 %) /
  constant.
- NBR JST 21: -0.27 (-0.19) / +0.40 / not identifiable / constant.
- NBR JST 29: -0.26 (-0.105) / +0.50 / not identifiable / constant.
- NBR CDR: -0.26 (-0.22) / +0.37 / not identifiable / constant.
- NBR MLA: -0.25 (-0.30) / +0.29 / not identifiable / constant.
- Le Mans: +0.048 (-0.12) / -0.30 / not identifiable / constant (1 lap).
No time trend, no visible temperature dependence, and no g-sensitivity
consistent across sessions.
CORRECTION CANDIDATE: only a per-session constant yaw bias is measured
well: the closure excess repeats to about +/-0.01 deg/s lap to lap. Its
simplest adequate form is degree 0; nothing higher earned its keep. Its
measured effect on the in-corner drift is at most 0.06 deg median. A
straight-line ay constant is not a candidate: applied in corners it
worsens the drift. What a yaw-bias correction would touch, as an
estimator-input change: prepare_vehicle_state's yaw_rate_radps and every
consumer of it -- kinematic beta, the EKF measurement (no bias state), slip
angles, CS_ratio, yaw stability (beta), Eq. 4.3 -- hence STRONG/MODERATE
CS thresholds and cs_margin re-derived, the stab_neg_thresh item, pipeline
goldens, ANALYSIS_SCHEMA_VERSION; k=1.01211 queued into the same boundary.
WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX: the heading-proportional in-corner error (2-7 %
between ay/v and r), which is the bulk of the recorded drift; the
curve-beta identifiability, i.e. the absolute beta scale, which no IMU
offset correction touches.

everywhere; under D1 it shortens (front 5.8-7.7 m, rear shorter on every
session, e.g. Dubai 7.1 -> 5.9 m). No filter lifts the scale CS varies on
to window scale.
COVERAGE (finite CS share of corner samples, rear): D1 cuts it most --
Dubai 0.732 -> 0.487, JST 29 0.769 -> 0.618, US-v2 0.892 -> 0.743; B4/B2
-2 to -11 % (B2 on JST 21 +6 %); C within 2 %, D2 within 6 %. Mechanism: a slower beta gives a slower
alpha, so more windows reach the 53 m cap before the slip-span floor (NaN)
-- the signal-suppression route of the 2026-09-29 sweep's B rows, reached
upstream. Floor-termination share falls with it (D1 rear 0.0-1.7 % vs
0.0-2.8 %).
FLOOR ROWS: F1 (speed +1 %) and F2 (ay +2 %) move the median |per-lap
phase median| by 0.131 and 0.151 -- as much as the strongest filter.

vs OS 11), and F2 (ay +2 %) gains two resolved corners on each of front
and gap. The battery and the resolvability count move as much under a
known 1-2 % input-scale error as under any filter.

## (b) Part 3: synthesis [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Families:
- Yaw rate + ay upstream (B4, B2): smoother CS traces, the largest
  switch-rate reductions, but both lose the Dubai C3 utilization gap; B4
  also loses Dubai's understeer direction. Disqualified.
- Speed upstream (C): nearly inert on the trace (roughness and coverage
  within 2 %); +1/+3 resolved corners, within the 2/2 floor; loses
  Dubai's understeer direction (5 vs 7). Disqualified.
- Beta before alpha (D2, D1): D2 is a near-cascade of the production 2 Hz
  alpha filter and loses Dubai's direction. D1 survives the battery and
  clears the switch-rate floor, but with no resolvability gain, shorter
  (not longer) decorrelation lengths, rear coverage down by up to a third,
  about half as many called lap pairs, and 7-8 changed calls per session.
- Combination E (C + D1): as D1 within noise (front +1, gap +1 resolved,
  both inside the floor).
EXIT BY THE PRE-REGISTERED CRITERION: D1 and E qualify for a variant
proposal (no battery loss, switch rate improved beyond the 0.066 floor,
confirmed on CDR and MLA). Measured beside that: the gain rests on fewer
called verdicts; resolvability does not improve beyond the floor; the
battery itself is not robust at the floor (a 1 % speed error alone loses
three elements); a production adoption would shift 6-9 calls per session
and owes the full re-derivation. The author rules between a D1/E proposal
and closing (b) as tested-upstream-nothing-earned-production.

## (c) Part 1: yaw-rate cross-lap pooling, flags and steering counteraction [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script: diagnostics/inspect_yaw_pooling.py (rules in its header before the
runs). Screening JST 29, US-v2, MLA; Dubai only for the C3-LS
cross-reference. Yaw rate low-passed at 4 Hz, pooled per corner on a 1 m
track grid over the analysis laps (kerb samples excluded); envelope
p10-p90; margin m = 3 x robust std of the filtered yaw rate's deviation
from its 0.5 Hz trend on straights: JST 29 1.67, US-v2 1.74, MLA 1.91,
Dubai 1.52 deg/s (noise sigma 0.51-0.64 deg/s). Flag = >= 5 m beyond the
envelope by more than m.
FLAGS: EXCESS (more rotation than the envelope in the turn direction)
on 23 of 90 corner-laps (JST 29, 31 flags), 38 of 153 (US-v2, 53), 21 of
90 (MLA, 23); Dubai 4 of 56. DEFICIT on 39 / 52 / 28 corner-laps (Dubai
16). Peak excess 2-12 deg/s (US-v2 C12 lap 53 +12.3).
COUNTERACTION (steering unwinding above T within 150-300 ms of the flag
onset; T = 3 x robust std of steering rate on straights, 19-29 deg/s;
steer/yaw sign +1 everywhere): corroborated 25/31 (0.81, JST 29), 41/53
(0.77, US-v2), 21/23 (0.91, MLA), 4/4 Dubai; the same test at the same
grid positions on the other laps gives 0.58, 0.48, 0.47, 0.58. Flags are
followed by unwinding 1.5-1.9x as often as the positions' base rate. The
threshold sits far below in-corner steering activity (+/-200-400 deg/s
in the figure), so the base rate is near one half and the test is weakly
specific.
CROSS-REFERENCE: JST 29 C1 carries EXCESS flags on laps 103, 104, 107
(corroborated) and 108 (not), and DEFICIT on lap 105 -- laps 103 and 107
are the two deepest NBR B C1 CS readings (-2.07 / -2.68, 2026-09-29);
lap 105 is the lap whose negatives the lag-only tyre largely reproduced.
Dubai C3 (the C3-LS traction corner): DEFICIT on laps 1 and 2, no excess
-- less rotation than the pooled envelope, as a traction-limited exit
would show. Coincidences recorded, not validations.
Figures: diagnostics/plots/yaw_pooling/yaw_pooling_<key>.png (gitignored).

## WP-HARDEN: CS display hardening implemented [2026-09-30, branch new-laps]

Variant A of the CS read-out decision, implemented per PLAN.md "WP-HARDEN". Display layer only: candidate generation, evidence, scores, classification, thresholds and ANALYSIS_SCHEMA_VERSION unchanged; no golden regenerated.
- Code: modules/decision_frame.py merge_lever_conflicts, apply_evidence_floor, harden_display_rows (after group_display_rows, before apply_display_top_n); render_card_header / render_tail_line render conflict cards and the tail state "below evidence floor". ui/views/outing_form.py calls the step, names the below-floor count in the summary line, and shows a conflict card's reasoning under one heading per direction. Config: decision_frame.json display_evidence_floor = 0.5 (reviewer-chosen midpoint of the 0.3-0.75 near-inert sweep range, decision-table package 2026-09-29; revisit when real data makes it bind). Tier C with one calibration value.
- Method. Floor: a display row ranks only if problem weight (its strongest member's score term) >= 0.5 or its candidates span >= 2 corners; otherwise it joins the tail after the top-N overflow. Conflict: rows moving one parameter with different action keys anywhere in the session form one card -- resolve_conflicts' own per-corner rule (same parameter, different direction/target) extended to the session, cards built as connected components, placed at the best member's rank. Per-member judgement: a card ranks if at least one member clears the floor on its own; if none does, the whole card is one tail line. Driver-disagree markers read every member at every tier.
- Invariance: harden_display_rows asserts that the candidate ids leaving it equal those entering it; tests/test_display_hardening.py checks on real Dubai that they equal the proposed candidate set and that the input rows are unchanged (13 tests).
- Goldens: recommendations_* compare modules.recommendation.generate_recommendations output, which never passes through the display split; golden files byte-identical.
Census (diagnostics/inspect_cs_decision_table.py hardened; eight cached sessions, data-only, floor 0.5; before = production grouped rows without hardening):
- Both-direction pairs in the top 3, before: Dubai, US-v2, NBR B, CDR, NBR-QP MLA (5 sessions); after: 0 everywhere. The prototype counted 4: its matcher knew only increase/decrease, the CDR pair is rear ARB stiffen + soften (rows 2 and 3). Conflict cards per session (Dubai, v3, US-v2, NBR A, NBR B, LMN MLA, CDR, NBR-QP MLA): 1/0/3/2/5/2/2/4 against the prototype's all-row pairs 1/0/2/1/4/1/1/2 -- the difference is the ARB soften/stiffen pairs.
- Thin #1 (below the floor), before: Dubai, US-v2, NBR-QP MLA; after: 0.
- TC recommendation #1, before 6/8; after 2/8 as a plain row (NBR A tc_lon +1, CDR tc_lat +1), as predicted (1-2/8). Counting TC conflict cards: 5/8 (US-v2, NBR B, NBR-QP MLA #1 is a tc_lon card).
- #1 after: Dubai none (empty top 3); v3 diff +1 (unchanged); US-v2 tc_lon card; NBR A tc_lon +1 (unchanged); NBR B tc_lon card; LMN MLA rear-ARB card (was the stiffen row; both members pass, pw 1.20 / 0.96); CDR tc_lat +1 (unchanged); NBR-QP MLA tc_lon card.
- Tail (overflow / below floor / non-proposed): Dubai 0/5/36, v3 0/1/36, US-v2 3/2/32, NBR A 3/0/35, NBR B 1/4/32, LMN MLA 1/0/37, CDR 2/2/33, NBR-QP MLA 3/1/33.
- Cards whose members all fail, now tail lines: Dubai tc_lon (C9 / C4, pw 0.300 each), NBR B wing and splitter (C8 0.400 / C9 0.150 each), NBR-QP MLA front ARB (C2 0.333 / C1 0.167). Mixed cards (one member fails) ranked visible: US-v2 tc_lon (C17 0.133 fails) and rear ARB (C12 0.133 fails), NBR-QP MLA tc_lon (C2 0.400 fails).
DIVERGENCE from the decision-table prediction: Dubai's visible list is empty. Every Dubai proposal is one corner at pw 0.300 (severity moderate x confidence), and the tc_lon card that the per-card rule made #1 fails per member. This is what the approved rule says -- the per-member judgement was introduced precisely because the card cleared the floor on paired thin evidence -- but the reference session now shows no proposal above the tail.
Limitation: evidence with severity None (intervention, kerb, driver feedback) carries problem weight 0, so a single-corner candidate built only on such evidence can never rank; for a driver-reported (feedback-only) candidate this is untested by the census, which is data-only.
[2026-09-30, close-out rulings, reviewer] Dubai's empty top 3 accepted as a designed outcome (no floor-clearing problem -> no ranked proposal; in the closed-loop era a team change against an empty top 3 is a scoreable divergence, not a tool failure); floor 0.5 not revisited. Spec amendment: members with feedback-only or both-agreeing provenance and |feedback| >= 2 pass the floor -- the generation gate that ruled such feedback sufficient evidence doubles as its floor, since their problem weight is 0 by construction. Action-key conflict matching (evidence: CDR's rear ARB stiffen + soften pair) and ranking of mixed cards confirmed. Record: PLAN.md WP-HARDEN "CLOSE-OUT RULINGS".

## (f) Part 1: event lists, three channels [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script diagnostics/inspect_event_coincidence.py (rules in its header before the run; approved proposal, author rulings 2026-09-30). Unit corner-lap. YAW: core/yaw_pooling flags with the (c) pre-registered constants, EXCESS and DEFICIT separate. CS: per corner-lap worst-phase CS_ratio (min over phase medians, apex from the apex region = the classifier's read-out), event below the session's own p10, front/rear separate; sample minimum and position kept as attributes. ## NBR C1 fixed-position CS dip: kerb strike at the apex [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Follow-up approved in "(f) exit rulings" item 4. Script diagnostics/inspect_nbr_c1_dip.py (rules in its header); JST 21 (laps 72, 73) and JST 29 (laps 103-108), 600-640 m; figures diagnostics/plots/nbr_c1_dip/nbr_c1_dip_<key>.png (gitignored). Census from the files: log_susp_travel_fl/fr/rl/rr alive at 100 Hz on both; ride height FL failed on both.
What is physically there: the C1 apex (minimum speed 64-74 km/h, steering 136-198 deg), and on every lap of both outings a vertical event at 612-627 m -- az first drops toward 0 g (unloading), then spikes to 3-4 g; all four damper travels swing 15-30 mm; ay swings by about 10 m/s^2 and yaw rate by about +/-20 deg/s; the raw yaw acceleration reaches +/-400-600 deg/s^2. The production kerb mask (|az - 1 g| > 1.2 g, +/-5 samples) flags it on every lap (11-51 samples in 600-640 m; mask edges 613-627 m).
Which input moves first (largest |rate| per metre in 590-640 m, relative to each lap's CS dip): az, ay, yaw rate and all four dampers peak within 0-3 m of each other on every lap -- one common instant, the strike. No lateral input leads it; speed peaks 3-23 m earlier (braking), steering mostly 10-20 m later (on laps 103 and 107, 12-17 m earlier). The dip sits at a kerb-mask edge on every lap (dip 612-626 m vs mask edges 613-627 m).
CS window at the dip (reconstruct_cs_window_start): 2-12 m long, at or near the minimum window. Two families by sign:
- A, alpha_f rising while Fy_f falls (laps 72, 103, 105, 107; includes the two deepest, -2.07 and -2.68): the dip lies at or just after the mask; the windows of 72, 103 and 107 contain 17, 11 and 9 kerb-flagged samples; the inputs peak at -3 to 0 m.
- B, alpha_f falling while Fy_f rises (laps 73, 104, 106, 108): the dip lies 1-2 m before the mask starts, the window holds no kerb sample, and the inputs peak 3-7 m after the dip -- the unloading phase before the az threshold is crossed.
Estimator property found (code read, modules/stability_analysis.compute_cs_for_axle): kerb samples are excluded only as window END points (moving & ~kerb gates index i); the regression uses every sample in alpha[start:i], Fy[start:i], kerb-flagged ones included. A window ending just after a kerb run therefore regresses over the strike.
~~Mechanism (named, not yet counterfactually tested): the fixed-position C1 dip is an input transient of the CS estimator at a kerb strike, not a tyre-saturation event.~~ [CORRECTED 2026-09-30, (g) step 0: the counterfactual with kerb samples excluded inside the windows leaves the C1 dips in place (JST 29 lap 107 -2.68 -> -2.66, lap 103 -2.07 -> -2.00, lap 108 deeper, -1.61 -> -2.70). The window-contents part of the mechanism below is REFUTED as the driver. What stands: the dip coincides with the kerb strike on every lap, and the strike's ay/yaw-rate disturbance extends beyond the samples the az-threshold mask flags. See "(g) step 0: kerb samples excluded inside CS windows".] Original text: the fixed-position C1 dip is an input transient of the CS estimator at a kerb strike, not a tyre-saturation event. The strike disturbs ay and yaw rate at once; Fy_f = m ay a_frac + Iz psidd / L carries both (the raw psidd term alone spans up to -7.9..+4.1 kN over a dip window, the same size as the Fy_f change across it, -5.9..+3.2 kN), and alpha moves with the same yaw-rate transient; minimum-length windows at the mask edges turn that into a negative slope. The kerb mask covers the impact but not the unloading before it (family B), and the window rule lets kerb samples into the fit (family A). Consistent with (f): the C1 dips carry no CS event under the worst-phase median read-out, only sample minima.
Not done (read-only): no re-estimation without kerb samples in the windows. That counterfactual would change CS values, so it is an estimator-input question (boundary class) and needs its own proposal.

## (g) close-out rulings [2026-09-30, author]

1. (g) CLOSED: kerb samples excluded inside CS windows was tested and is near-inert; nothing ships. The sawtooth window-start repair, tested alongside it as the KS variant, stays PARKED.
2. No kerb-detection proposal. OPEN LIMITATION recorded: CS_ratio minima cluster at kerb-mask edges 3-5x chance (pooled over eight sessions: front 3.05x, deep tail 5.09x; rear 2.34x, deep tail 2.94x). The cause is unresolved: apex physics next to kerbs, or strike disturbance in samples the az-threshold mask does not flag. Kerb samples inside the windows are refuted as the driver. The verdict impact is bounded small: 1-3 changed corner calls per session under K. Reopen: a kerb-heavy track where the association demonstrably reaches verdicts.
3. Both step-0 operationalisations accepted as recorded: "drops toward chance" = the excess over chance at least halves on both axles; "no new deep dips" = at most 1 new deep-tail minimum per session and axle more than 3 m from a kerb-mask edge, plus trace inspection.
FINDING, chair reference (read-only, docs/literature/cornering_stiffness_estimator.py and data_handler.py): the reference has no kerb concept; its CS windows are contiguous left-sided slices over all samples with nothing masked inside, on inputs read from an "ACC CSV" format. Production's kerb handling -- kerb samples excluded as CS window endpoints, via moving & ~kerb -- is therefore already a deviation from the chair, class DOMAIN IMPROVEMENT ("based on their version, which is not wrong"): this car's data carries kerb strikes the reference's inputs do not.
FINDING, battery gaps under K: excluding kerb samples inside the windows WIDENS two rear-minus-front battery gaps rather than eroding them -- US-v2 C13 +0.507 -> +0.973, JST 29 (NBR B) C9 +0.168 -> +0.321 (KS: +0.828 / +0.347). Both corners have kerb-affected minima (US-v2 C13 front 3/9 windows with kerb samples; JST 29 C9 front 5/6), so kerb samples in the windows had been compressing these gaps. The balance signals the battery rests on are not kerb artifacts; if anything they are understated at baseline.

## Roll closure check: the roll-rate channel carries yaw cross-coupling [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Work order after the (g) close-out: does the (a2) roll-leakage constant survive, and is (a3) proposable on data alone? diagnostics/inspect_imu_offsets.py modes rollcheck (pre-registered) and rollcheck2 (post-hoc, labelled), a2 caches; JST 29, US-v2 (serial 221) and Dubai (serial 147 control). Figure diagnostics/plots/imu_offsets/roll_closure.png (gitignored).
Entry: with bias 0 the mode reproduces the recorded (a2) roll gradients and median window-end |phi| exactly (0.9985 / 0.9487 / 2.4188 deg/g; 2.98 / 2.13 / 4.96 deg).
PART 1 (pre-registered).
- 1.1 Constant bias (S0 straight-line median: +0.46 / -0.01 / -0.135 deg/s): closure is NOT proportional to window duration (R^2 0.02 / 0.30 / 0.02; fitted beta -0.55 / -0.64 / +0.30 deg/s against the bias). Removing the bias changes the median |closure| from 2.98 / 2.13 / 4.96 to 3.76 / 2.12 / 4.26 deg -- worse on JST 29.
- 1.2 Reproducibility: the bias-removed closure is a property of the corner -- eta^2 0.984 / 0.982 / 0.997 against permutation nulls of 0.17 / 0.15 / 0.25 (p 0.0005); lap-to-lap sd 0.05-2.0 deg against corner means up to +/-15 deg (JST 29 C5 -15.5, C7 -14.5, C11 -14.7); one sign on every lap in 8/10, 13/15, 9/9 corners; the corner-mean sign follows the TURN DIRECTION in 7/10, 14/15, 9/9.
- 1.3 Pre-registered verdict: BANK-DOMINATED on all three (shares bias / bank / noise: -0.49 / 1.46 / 0.03; 0.02 / 0.96 / 0.02; 0.09 / 0.91 / 0.00).
POST-HOC (labelled; the turn-direction sign and 15-deg size do not fit road bank): yaw rate leaking into the roll-rate channel (sensor pitch misalignment or cross-axis sensitivity: p_meas = p + r sin(theta0); on gradients also Euler coupling) integrates to sin(theta0) x heading change, reproducible per corner, signed by turn direction.
- Lap-closure bias (mean roll rate over each full analysis lap, which a bias-free gyro integrates to ~0): -0.147 / -0.077 / -0.193 deg/s, stable to +/-0.006 across laps. The straight-line median misses it (JST 29 +0.46, wrong sign): on these tracks the car rolls on straights too, so the median is not a bias estimate for this channel.
- Coupling fit C_after = s x dpsi + c (lap-closure bias; S0 in brackets): s +0.036 / +0.023 / +0.038 (implied axis angle 2.09 / 1.31 / 2.18 deg; S0 2.23 / 1.35 / 2.17), c -1.71 / +0.26 / +0.04 deg, R^2 0.43 / 0.89 / 0.80; explains 56 / 89 / 81 % of the bias-removed mean-square closure (S0: 74 / 90 / 82 %). Residual after it: median |C| 3.50 / 0.59 / 2.34 deg, still corner-bound (eta^2 0.97 / 0.74 / 0.98) -- the part that can be bank or grade; the lower R^2 on the Nordschleife fits its gradients (Euler coupling varies by corner).
- The angle differs between the two serial-221 sessions (1.3 vs 2.1 deg): not one fixed sensor constant.
PART 2.
- 2.1 Leakage with the bias removed (pre-registered): 1.74 -> 1.46 % (JST 29), 1.66 -> 1.65 % (US-v2), 4.22 -> 4.29 % (Dubai) -- bias removal alone barely moves it. With the coupling also removed (post-hoc, lap-closure bias): -0.32 deg/g (magnitude 0.57 %, OPPOSITE sign to leakage) / -0.08 deg/g (0.13 %, opposite sign) / +0.76 deg/g (+1.32 %). The closure-forced sensitivity row agrees in direction (0.09 / -0.10 / 0.58 deg/g).
- 2.2 The position-bound closure is mostly not bank: 56-89 % is heading-proportional coupling. The remainder is corner-bound (bank or grade); a correction that included it would be position-dependent, which fails the simplicity principle. The per-session constant that (a2) measured is not a roll-leakage constant: it is dominated by a sensor-axis artifact whose size is not even stable within one logger serial.
PART 3, the (a3) gate: the roll term is NOT measured well enough to propose (a3) on data alone. The (a2) leakage constant (1.5-2.6 % serial 221, 4.2 % Dubai) does not survive: most of it is yaw cross-coupling in sclu_roll_rate; with that removed the serial-221 leakage is 0.1-0.6 % and of the opposite sign, and Dubai keeps 1.3 %. What remains is neither stable nor simple. (a3) genuinely needs the engineer's sensor answers, and the roll-gyro question sharpens: not only bias, but the roll-rate sensor's axis alignment / cross-axis sensitivity to yaw, and whether sclu_roll_rate is a raw body-axis rate. The C4 row of (a2) Part 3 and the C3+C4 collapse rest on the contaminated constant (correction notes added there).
