## Sensor tilt vs static attitude, eight sessions [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

HARDWARE (author-supplied, 2026-09-30): ONE gyro cluster (SCLU) on the transmission tunnel at the centre console, near the CG, body-fixed and immovable relative to the body; MRR_EgoYawRate is therefore a bus copy. A body-fixed sensor tilts with the car's static attitude, so rake and ride-height changes between sessions change its alignment to the road.
Script: diagnostics/inspect_imu_offsets.py modes attcompute <key> and attitude (rules in the header before the run; two labelled corrections/post-hoc blocks). Figure diagnostics/plots/imu_offsets/tilt_vs_attitude.png (gitignored).
DATA FINDINGS (channel census, read from the files):
- The header unit of the same channel differs between files: log_rideheight_rake is [ft] on v3, US-v2, CDR and QP MLA (the four files that also carry l_rake) and [m] on Dubai, JST 21, JST 29 and Le Mans; log_rideheight_rl is [m] on the same four [ft] files and [mm] on the others. The first run applied mm rules to raw values and failed its entry check; after conversion by header unit the recorded NBR A/B band medians are reproduced exactly (-94.98 / -89.75 / -85.19 and -97.49 / -92.75 / -88.91 mm).
- ~~log_rideheight_rake is not the laser rear-minus-front rake: about -92 mm on the four NBR files against a laser rake of about +10 mm; on Paul Ricard, Dubai and Le Mans the two roughly mirror each other (e.g. US-v2 -13.4 vs +14.2 mm). A different zero or definition per file -- its absolute level is not comparable across files.~~ [CORRECTED 2026-09-30: the definition is identical in all eight files, log_rideheight_rake = 0.528 (FL + FR) - 0.528 (RL + RR), zero intercept; the NBR level comes from the dead FL laser (stuck at -101 mm) entering the front average. See "Ride-height measuring points (team document) and the rake channel".]
- Dead channels: log_rideheight_fl on all four NBR files; log_rideheight_rake_mc on all eight. Laser rake therefore uses FR alone as the front on NBR.
PART 1, attitude (laser rear-minus-front, 150-200 km/h, whole file as in the recorded method): Dubai -0.6, v3 +12.3, US-v2 +14.2, JST 21 +7.6, JST 29 +11.0, Le Mans -1.9, CDR +9.5, QP MLA +9.3 mm; spread 16.1 mm = 0.37 deg over the 2.505 m wheelbase (config vehicle.wheelbase_m; laser positions are not the axles, so this is the geometric expectation, not a calibrated angle). Rear left-minus-right: -1.0 to -2.9 mm (0.04-0.10 deg over the placeholder 1.64 m track).
PART 2, orientation estimates: yaw-leak axis angle (roll-check method, lap-closure bias) Dubai +2.18, v3 +1.20, US-v2 +1.31, JST 21 +1.90, JST 29 +2.09, Le Mans +1.73, CDR +2.53, QP MLA +2.01 deg (R^2 0.43-0.89); straight-line ay offset (a) S0 +0.12 / +0.48 / +0.48 / +0.40 / +0.50 / -0.30 / +0.37 / +0.29 m/s^2 (tilt equivalent -1.72 to +2.92 deg); (a2) referee intercept -0.07 / +0.37 / +0.39 / +0.51 / +0.47 / +0.05 / +0.47 / +0.40 m/s^2.
PART 3, correlation and models (A free slope; B slope fixed at the geometric 1 + one mounting offset per logger; B' free slope + per-logger offset):
- Yaw-leak angle vs attitude: magnitudes cannot close. The laser-rake spread is 0.37 deg against a leak-angle spread of 1.33 deg; the fitted slopes have the WRONG sign (laser rake -1.06, r -0.32; rake channel -0.24, r -0.57); model B (geometry) leaves rms 0.44 deg (laser rake) / 1.11 deg (rake channel). The known NBR A -> B rake change (+2.5-3.7 mm, ~0.07 deg) goes with a leak-angle change of +0.19 deg -- about three times the geometric maximum. The leak angle groups by TRACK: Paul Ricard 1.20 / 1.31 deg with tight fits (R^2 0.83 / 0.89); NBR 1.90-2.53 deg with loose fits (R^2 0.43-0.63); Dubai 2.18, Le Mans 1.73 (serial 147). Consistent with a fixed mounting component (closest to it on the flat Paul Ricard) plus a track-dependent part (road-gradient Euler coupling on the Nordschleife is the named, untested candidate), not with a rake-dependent part.
- ay offset vs roll attitude: magnitudes cannot close (0.04-0.10 deg of logged roll attitude against 0.7-2.9 deg of tilt equivalent). The referee intercept splits cleanly by LOGGER: serial 221 +0.37 to +0.51 m/s^2 on both Paul Ricard and NBR, serial 147 -0.07 / +0.05; model B gives mounting +2.60 deg (221) and -0.01 deg (147), rms 0.31 deg. The (a) S0 median is track-dependent on serial 147 (Dubai +0.12, Le Mans -0.30), i.e. crossfall on the straights, which the referee intercept (in-corner, regressed on r v) does not carry.
PART 4, consequence (characterisation only, no proposal):
- Constant ay offset item: on serial 221 a fixed +0.37-0.51 m/s^2 (tilt equivalent 2.2-3.0 deg) that does not follow logged attitude -- consistent with a fixed mounting roll tilt of the SCLU or an accelerometer zero offset (not separable from this data); serial 147 shows no such offset. Attitude differences between sessions do not explain it.
- (a3) roll term: the yaw leak is not attitude-driven; it has a fixed component plus a track-dependent part, so it is a per-session quantity that must be measured per session (the roll-check fit does that), not a constant derivable from rake geometry. This strengthens the roll-check gate answer: no stable, simple roll term exists on data alone.
- A stable decomposition "fixed mounting tilt per logger + attitude-dependent part" does NOT exist for the yaw leak (the attitude part has the wrong sign and is too small); it exists only for the ay intercept as "fixed per logger", with no attitude part.

## Ride-height measuring points (team document) and the rake channel [2026-09-30, branch new-laps, read-only]

Source: Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) team document "Ride height measuring points" (team data, protected reference; not committed). It defines per corner, in mm: FIA chassis reference points (X, Y = reference; Z +46 front, +70 rear); ADAC ride-height measuring points (front X 0, Y -/+40, Z 0; rear X +30, Y +/-30, Z 0); Porsche laser ride-height points (front X -281, Y +89 FR / -82 FL, Z +171; rear X +540 RR / +542 RL, Y -148 RR / +149 RL, Z +100). All Z relative to the flat underbody; laser X/Y at the centre laser light, Z at the sensor's bottom window. It defines no rake channel.
RAKE CHANNEL, read from the data (OLS of log_rideheight_rake on the four raw laser channels, header units converted, samples above 30 km/h, all eight files): log_rideheight_rake = 0.528 (FL + FR) - 0.528 (RL + RR) = 1.056 x (front mean - rear mean), zero intercept, rms residual 0.00 mm, IDENTICAL in every file. The NBR level (about -92 mm) is the dead FL laser, stuck at -101.0 mm on all four NBR files, averaged into the front: no per-file zero exists. The 1.056 factor is not explained by the document's coordinates without the front-to-rear reference distance; no consumer needs it. No production module reads any ride-height or rake channel (only the config/channels.json registry entry for log_rideheight_fl).
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TILT CHECK ("Sensor tilt vs static attitude, eight sessions"):
- The laser Z offsets are constant and cancel in cross-session differences; the NBR laser rake already used FR alone, so the dead FL never entered the check's laser numbers.
- The lever arm: the lasers sit 281 mm ahead of the front and about 541 mm behind the rear reference points, so their spacing is about 3327 mm if the FIA reference points sit at the 2505 mm wheelbase (an assumption; the document gives offsets, not the reference distance). Pitch angles scale by 0.753: the cross-session laser-rake spread 0.37 -> 0.28 deg; fit slope -1.06 -> -1.40 (still the wrong sign); geometric model B rms 0.44 -> 0.43 deg (mounting 147 +1.97, 221 +1.66 deg).
- No conclusion moves. The margin is a factor of about 5 (0.28 deg of attitude spread against a 1.33 deg spread of the yaw-leak angle), not two orders; the null result rests chiefly on the wrong-sign slope, which a rescaling cannot flip.

## Kerb-detection variants, Part 1: strike disturbance envelope [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

Work order 2026-10-01 (follow-up to the PARKED open limitation "CS minima cluster at kerb-mask edges"). Script diagnostics/inspect_kerb_mask_variants.py (rules for Parts 1-3 in its header before the first run). Tier B, preprocessing; no anchor claimed. Tier 1: JST 29, US-v2, QP MLA.
Census from the files: log_acc_z and log_acc_y in [G], sclu_yaw_rate in [rpm], all native 100 Hz, on all three; grid 100 Hz (1 sample = 10 ms); grid identical to the new_laps cache and new_laps moving = raw moving & ~production mask (asserted).
Method: event = a contiguous run of the production mask (|az - 1 g| > 1.2 g, dilated +/-5 samples) touching a moving analysis-lap sample. Local trend = cubic in time over 1.0 s context each side, mask samples excluded, three passes of 3-sigma clipping; noise = 1.4826 x MAD of the retained residuals; disturbance = |residual| > 3 sigma; the envelope extends while the next exceedance lies within 0.10 s (bridges the zero crossings of an oscillating transient). Null control: one pseudo-event per event of the same length at a random in-corner position >= 2 s from any mask sample (seed 20261001).
Correction after the first run (recorded): the first pass let the envelope walk into a NEIGHBOURING mask run, crediting one strike with the next one's disturbance (it produced az minima "before the trip" below -0.2 g, which is impossible without a trip). The walk now stops at the neighbour run; the counts reaching one are reported (JST 29 ay 18/154 each side, US-v2 ay 55/54 of 285, QP MLA ay 20/17 of 139). All numbers below are after the correction. Kerb sites are typically several mask runs in a row, so the uncorrected pooled p75 (pre 18 / post 16 samples) roughly halved.
Extension beyond the mask edge, samples p25/p50/p75/p90 (metres at p75/p90), events vs null control:
- JST 29 (154 events): ay pre 0/0/5/11 (1.9/4.4 m), post 0/0/3/9; yaw pre 0/0/0/5, post 0/0/0/8; az pre 0/0/0/2, post 0/0/0/1. Share of events with any pre-extension: ay 0.44 vs control 0.08; yaw 0.16 vs 0.06.
- US-v2 (285): ay pre 0/2/10/20 (3.1/7.5 m), post 0/1/8/19; yaw pre 0/0/0/6, post 0/0/0/6; az pre 0/0/5/14, post 0/0/5/12. ay pre share 0.63 vs 0.11.
- QP MLA (139): ay pre 0/0/6/14 (2.2/5.1 m), post 0/0/4/11; yaw pre 0/0/0/4, post 0/0/0/6; az pre 0/0/0/3, post 0/0/0/1. ay pre share 0.47 vs 0.12.
- ay/yaw union, pooled Tier 1 (n 578): pre 0/2/9/18, post 0/1/8/17 samples; control 0/0/0/8 and 0/0/0/9.
Reading: the disturbance past the mask is real (event shares 3-6x the control's) but short: the median event has 0-4 samples (0-40 ms), the p75 8-10 samples (80-100 ms, ~2-3 m), the p90 about 0.2 s. It is carried by ay; yaw rate extends on only 15-23 % of events (control 4-12 %). Pre and post are about symmetric. The production dilation (+/-5 samples) already covers the median.
Unloading (does az dip toward 0 g before the threshold trips?): the raw trip comes from below (az < -0.2 g, the unloading itself crossing the threshold) on 65/154, 103/285, 61/139 events. A downward az excursion beyond 3 sigma that reaches back before the dilated onset exists on 11/154 (0.07), 82/285 (0.29), 14/139 (0.10); its length before the onset p50/p75 2/6, 6/11, 4/8 samples; start to raw trip p50 7, 11, 10 samples (70-110 ms); az minimum before the trip p50 -0.07, +0.05, +0.08 g. So the unloading precedes the trip by ~0.1 s, but the existing 5-sample dilation already swallows most of it; it reaches past the mask on a minority of events, most on Paul Ricard (US-v2).
Named sites, per lap:
- NBR C1, JST 29 (mask 614-627 m): ay disturbance before the mask on 5 of 6 laps, 9-21 samples = 2.0-4.4 m (laps 103 -2.0, 104 -2.4, 106 -3.3, 107 -2.4, 108 -4.4 m); after it 0-1.8 m; yaw before 0-4.5 m; az unloading past the mask only 0.4 m (laps 107, 108). This matches C1 family B (dip 1-2 m before the mask) and is the clearest under-detection case in the set.
- NBR C1, QP MLA (laps 283, 284, 287): pre-extension 1.1-3.9 m (yaw on 283, ay on 284/287), post up to 2.4 m.
- NBR ~4480-4540 m, JST 29 and QP MLA: three to five mask runs per lap; extensions are 0 on most runs, a few 0.4-6.5 m (JST 29 lap 108 4509-4522 m the largest: ay -5.7/+4.4 m). The site is covered by the existing mask almost entirely; it does not look under-detected.
- (US-v2 600-640 m is a Paul Ricard position, not NBR C1; printed by the site rule, not a named site.)

## Kerb-detection variants, Part 2: variant masks [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

Constants fixed in the script header from Part 1, before scoring. A = production mask (|az - 1 g| > 1.2 g, +/-5 samples). B = A dilated asymmetrically by 9 samples (0.09 s) before and 8 samples (0.08 s) after each run: the pooled Tier-1 p75 of the corrected ay/yaw union extension; p75 not p90 because the null control's own p90 (8-9 samples) marks detector false positives there. C = each run's onset moved back to the start of its downward az excursion (Part 1 detector), end unchanged. D = each run widened to its own measured ay/yaw disturbance envelope (Part 1 detector), never narrower than A. C and D are built on every run of the session. Simplicity order B < C < D.
Masked share of moving analysis-lap samples (A / B / C / D): JST 29 0.038 / 0.069 / 0.038 / 0.055; US-v2 0.049 / 0.084 / 0.055 / 0.082; QP MLA 0.034 / 0.062 / 0.035 / 0.051. B nearly doubles the masked share; C barely moves it (the unloading past the dilation is rare, Part 1).

Enrichment is read against each variant's OWN mask edges (pre-registered: production edges would sit inside a widened mask's NaN region and collapse by construction -- they give B 15.3 / 12.5, which is that artifact, informative only).
- Leg 1 (excess over chance must halve on both axles), pooled Tier 1, enrichment front / rear: BASE 2.89 / 2.18; A 2.83 / 2.25; B 2.82 / 2.66; C 2.97 / 2.27; D 2.53 / 2.21. Excess front 1.89 -> 1.83 / 1.82 / 1.97 / 1.53, rear 1.18 -> 1.25 / 1.66 / 1.27 / 1.21. ALL FAIL. Best is D on the front (-19 % of the excess); no variant moves the rear down. No broad new dip pattern. Traces agree with the scores.

## Kerb-detection variants, Part 4: synthesis [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

No variant collapses the enrichment. The most complex (D, measured ay/yaw envelope) removes about a fifth of the front excess and none of the rear at ~1.5x the masked share; the simplest (B) removes nothing measurable while nearly doubling the masked share, and fails leg 2. By the selection principle nothing earns a proposal; no adoption shape is written.
What the result says about the cause. The measurable strike disturbance past the az mask is short (p75 80-100 ms, Part 1), and masking all of it (D) leaves the clustering at the new edges nearly intact; when the mask widens, the minima move with its edge (C1 lap 107 deepens at the new edge under B and D). The pre-onset part of the association was partly under-detection (it shrinks under D); the post-end part, now the larger share, is not reachable by any mask width tested. That favours the apex-physics reading -- kerbs sit at apexes, and the CS minimum lands on the first non-masked sample next to wherever the mask ends -- over "the mask misses the disturbance". One mechanism remains untested and is named, not claimed: under the K machinery a window ending just after a mask reaches back across the masked gap and regresses pre-strike against post-strike samples; that is a window-construction property, independent of detection, and would also follow the edge.
Limitation entry gains the result: kerb-detection widening (dilation, unloading onset, disturbance envelope) tested on Tier 1, enrichment persists (front excess changes +4 % to -19 %, rear none falls); the cause is now narrowed to the post-strike side, apex physics or window construction, not under-detection.

## Kerb-detection variant rulings [2026-10-01, author]

1. Own-edges scoring CONFIRMED correct: the production-edge version is circular by construction (a widened mask turns the production edges' surroundings into NaN).
2. Kerb-detection variants CLOSED: tested, nothing ships. No variant halves the clustering; the simplest (B) gains nothing. Mask under-detection is largely refuted as the driver of the kerb-edge association; apex physics is promoted to the leading explanation.
3. Window-reach check APPROVED (read-only), the last step on this question: does the CS window span masked kerb gaps and fit pre-strike against post-strike samples as one population? If the no-crossing variant also fails the step-0 legs, apex physics wins by elimination and the limitation closes as characterised.

## Window-reach check: CS windows across masked kerb gaps [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

Approved in "Kerb-detection variant rulings" item 3 as the last step on the kerb-edge question. diagnostics/inspect_kerb_mask_variants.py modes reach, trunc, score_t (Part 5 rules in its header before the run). Tier 1 (JST 29, US-v2, QP MLA), production mask.
MEASUREMENT (window at each per-corner-lap CS minimum; straddle = unmasked samples both before the window's first masked sample and after its last):
- BASE (production window): near-edge minima hold masked samples in 61 % (front) / 47 % (rear) of windows vs 9-10 % for the other minima; masked share p90 1.00 / 0.81 (the window is mostly strike); straddle only 16 % / 13 % (other minima 3 %). Near-edge windows are shorter (p50 29 / 28 samples vs 36 / 40).
- A (kerb samples excluded inside windows, (g) K): near-edge straddle 44 % / 38 % vs 9 % / 7 % for the other minima; on the post-end side 59 % / 54 % straddle; post-gap unmasked samples in a straddling window p50 6 / 3. On the pre-onset side windows rarely hold masked samples (21 % / 0 %).
- So the window does span the gap where the post-end minima sit: under K it regresses a handful of post-strike samples together with the pre-strike stretch.
DECISIVE VARIANT T (window may not contain a masked sample; truncation and restart coincide for a left-sided window; self-check T with no mask = BASE exactly on 20 000 JST 29 samples):
- Leg 1: FAIL, enrichment RISES: front 2.89 -> 4.53, rear 2.18 -> 2.57 (excess 1.89 -> 3.53, 1.18 -> 1.57). Per session front JST 29 3.76 -> 6.02, US-v2 2.74 -> 4.44, QP MLA 2.18 -> 3.05.

T removes the post-end side -- largely by construction, since CS is NaN for about one minimum window after every gap -- and the remaining clustering is entirely pre-onset, in windows that hold no masked sample and end before the strike. - QP MLA ~2800 m (C8), front BASE -> T: lap 283 -1.11 -> -2.45, 284 -1.83 -> -2.34 (B and D gave the same -2.45). The dip deepens whenever the windows next to that kerb are cut short; it is a short-window property of that site, not a crossing effect (BASE windows there do not cross).
- 4500 m site: T lifts the dips (JST 29 lap 107 -1.71 -> +0.38; QP MLA lap 286 -2.00 -> +0.74), as B did.
- Traces (BASE / A / T stacked; JST 29 and QP MLA inspected, US-v2 rendered): T leaves more NaN holes, shrinks C1 on two JST 29 laps, adds a deep JST 29 C10 front dip near 3330 m (-3.36) and deepens QP MLA 2800 m; no other new pattern. Traces agree with the scores.
SAWTOOTH INTERACTION (stated, not run): the parked sawtooth repair constrains the window start to advance by at most 2 samples per step; T moves the earliest admissible start forward by the whole gap at every strike. The two rules act on the same start construction and conflict at every gap: either the repair lets the window reach back across the strike (violating T), or T resets the repair's history (the repair is inert on every post-gap stretch). A future window-construction change must decide this precedence explicitly; T's result gives no reason to open that boundary.
EXIT (pre-registered legs): T fails legs 1 and 2. Window reach explains part of the post-end minima under the K machinery, but forbidding it raises the enrichment and leaves the pre-onset clustering in clean windows intact. By the author's ruling: apex physics wins by elimination; the limitation closes as characterised.

## Kerb-edge association: closed as characterised [2026-10-01]

Elimination chain, all Tier 1 with the step-0 exit legs: (1) kerb samples inside the windows ((g) K) -- near-inert; (2) mask under-detection (dilation B, unloading onset C, measured ay/yaw envelope D) -- the measurable strike disturbance past the az mask is short (p75 80-100 ms); masking all of it removes at most a fifth of the front excess; minima follow the new edge; (3) window reach across the masked gap (T) -- enrichment rises, the residual clustering sits in clean pre-strike windows. Remaining explanation, by elimination: apex physics -- kerbs are placed at apexes, where the tyre's real force-saturation minimum sits, and any masking pushes the sample minimum onto the nearest unmasked sample. Not proven by direct measurement; it is what survives three independent tests. Verdict impact stays bounded small (1-3 changed corner calls per session under every variant tested). Production kerb handling (az threshold, +/-5 dilation, endpoint-only exclusion) unchanged.

## (d) tyre-curve baseline prior: proposal, rulings, feasibility [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, documentation only]

SOURCE: supervisor direction (d), intermediate meeting 2026-09-30 -- one baseline tyre curve per axle fitted ONCE from all sessions (his grounds: same tyres, similar conditions; recorded as chair-practice grounds), per-session fits expressed as deviations from it. Differs from the failed refit loop ("Refit-loop conclusion: structural non-convergence confirmed on two sessions, two failure directions"): the prior is fitted once and never fed its own output, so there is no loop to drift. What it does NOT fix: curve and beta stay jointly unobservable from ay and yaw rate; the prior inherits the kinematic seed's bias direction (accuracy: Level 2, pooled session measurement, kinematic-seeded). Runs on current inputs; refit caveat: if (a3) ever ships, the prior is refitted.
REVIEWER WARNING (standing correction, recorded): (d) is NOT judged by distance from production's current fits -- production is our own calibrated configuration, not truth. Criteria are forward-looking only.
PREMISE CORRECTION (census rule): recorded per-session Pacejka free-D fits exist for TWO sessions only -- Dubai (front B=10.457 C=1.940 D=8184.0 E=0.091; rear B=11.759 C=1.982 D=9213.6 E=-2.281) and v3 (post pit-limiter fix: front B=8.521 C=1.888 D=8355.4 E=-0.518; rear B=8.371 C=2.007 D=9486.2 E=-1.381, health 0.0985). The other six sessions' baselines are created in step 0.
METHOD (approved):
- Fit population = production's own: kinematic alpha_f/r_filt, Fy_f/r_filt (estimate_lateral_forces), _base_mask (moving, not kerb, analysis-valid laps); free-D (config tyre_fit_auto.load_normalised_fit_enabled = False).
- Prior: production's _fit_axle_pacejka, unchanged, on the CONCATENATED pool (Powell from the chair start guess). Pool: the six serial-221 sessions (v3, US-v2, JST 21, JST 29, CDR, MLA) -- they share the characterised IMU offset family ((a) Part 1); Dubai and Le Mans (serial 147) are out-of-pool transfer tests. All-eight pool and equal-per-session weighting are sensitivity rows.
- Deviation, Option B: Fy = lambda_s * F_prior(alpha), B, C, E and D_prior frozen, lambda_s by closed-form least squares through the origin (Tier B). Rejected: A (prior as Powell start -- implicit, path-dependent). [2026-10-01 NOTE: Option A is the author's VARIANT 1 (prior-as-start) of the recorded tyre-model architecture and is to be tested at full depth (PLAN.md "PHASE 1 PLAN, anchored 2026-10-01", sections 3 and 5 Q3; "Phase 1 anchoring" below). Scope line for this rejection: an a-priori proposal-stage rejection, never run in (d); (d2) Part 2/3 ran the same fit at w 0 and recorded its start-point dependence as a side fact.] Held as escalation: B2 (separate force and slip scales), C (penalised MAP fit -- new covariance tunable, own anchor).
ANCHOR (Tier A): PENDING. Text search of the on-file PDFs, 2026-10-01: RCVD (docs/literature/Racecar_vehicle_dynamics.pdf) has no text layer (0 of 928 pages) -- not searchable. Rajamani sec. 13.9 (verified on the rendered page): D and BCD are separate functions of Fz (eqs. 13.68, 13.69, tyre constants a1-a8), mu named in the prose only; no single-scale treatment -- does not anchor Option B. It DOES verify: asymptote y_s = D sin(pi C/2) (eq. 13.67, the C <= 2 band ground) and that E changes neither origin slope nor peak (item 7). Author is sourcing Pacejka's book (Magic Formula scaling factors). Step 0 may run (production fit + closed-form LS scale); nothing ships without the anchor. [2026-10-04 ANCHOR NOTE: Pacejka, Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics 2nd ed., is now on file; sec. 4.3.2 introduces user scaling factors lambda (lambda_Kya, lambda_muy) for changing cornering stiffness and friction while keeping realistic relationships -- the book frames them as a tool to investigate such changes 'in a qualitative way', not as an identification method. (d) stays closed as ruled; this records the anchor's existence and its stated scope.]
PRE-REGISTERED CRITERIA (bands accepted 2026-10-01):
- K1 stability: LOSO priors (each pool session left out) within 3 % of the full prior's D over the pooled visited range (0 to pooled p95 |alpha|); each session's lambda under its LOSO prior within 2 % of its full-prior lambda; independent-fit spread on the same grid reported as context only (B's shape spread is zero by construction, so "tighter" alone is not evidence).
- K2 plausibility: C in (1, 2] (Rajamani eq. 13.67); E <= 1; implied mu = D / mean axle Fz in config mu_plausibility_band [1.2, 2.0] (citation open); BCD/Fz in [6, 24] rad^-1 -- reviewer-accepted engineering range around the recorded 12 rad^-1, citation open (inherits the existing citation debt); lambda within +/-15 %, |lambda-1| < 5 % not interpreted as a grip difference (input-scale error budget: GPS k, ay scale, config mass vs fuel); peak slip angle reported in/out of pooled visited p99 (out = extrapolated label, not a fail).
- K3 rear large slip: region |alpha_r| > median of per-session p99. STABILISES only if the prior rear peak is inside pooled visited p99 AND LOSO rear peaks spread <= 0.5 deg AND no common-sign residual bias beyond 2 SE in the region's bins; else IMPOSES (rear large-slip curve stays labelled extrapolated).
- K4 NIS gate, read one-way: worsening (pass -> warn/fail, sweep leaves band) counts against; improvement counts for nothing (the gate measures filter consistency, not curve truth).
- K5 MASKING (negative criterion), any of: (i) binned residual of the B fit with >= 2 adjacent bins beyond 2 SE (traversal bootstrap) absent from the independent fit, on >= 2 sessions; (ii) JST 21 vs JST 29 (same track, same day, setup change): independent fits differ beyond noise on the common grid but B's lambda gap is within noise (if the independent fits do not differ, the test is uninformative); (iii) out-of-pool Dubai/Le Mans lambda outside +/-15 % or pattern (i); (iv) K4 worsening on any session.
- K6 downstream: the (b) survival battery and the per-iteration trace render; production proposal only if K1-K4 pass, K5 does not trigger and the battery improves at comparable complexity.
ENTRY CHECKS: EC1 caches -- no existing cache holds the fit inputs or fit manifests; the imu_offsets a2 caches hold base_mask's inputs for all eight; all nine raw files present; step 0 builds its own per-session cache from one production fit_session_pacejka run each. Dubai and Le Mans stay out of the pool (different tyres, author-confirmed; logger serial 147) and serve as out-of-pool comparison sessions. The (d) step-0 criteria K1-K6 do NOT apply: no pass/fail scoring, the author inspects and rules. Production default unchanged until the author rules.
SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_tyre_prior_d2.py; all definitions below were fixed in its header before the runs they govern. Outputs diagnostics/plots/tyre_prior_d2/ (gitignored): census.json, intake_*.json, prior.json, part3.txt, report.txt, selection.json, fit_<key>.png, traces_<key>_{prod,w1}.png.
TIER: A (prior-plus-deviation tyre fit) -- anchor still PENDING as in (d); nothing ships without it. B: pooling, penalised least squares (Tikhonov regularisation towards a reference curve), unit conversion, census checks.
PRE-REGISTERED, Part 2 (anchored fit): per axle minimise mean_i (F(alpha_i; p) - Fy_i)^2 + w * mean_g (F(g; p) - F_prior(g))^2 over (B, C, D, E), Powell from the prior's parameters, g = 200 points on [0, p99 |alpha|] of the fitted population. The penalty sits on the curve, not on the parameters, because B, C and E trade off along a ridge on which the curve barely moves ((d) step 0, LOSO_cdr); a parameter penalty would pull along the ridge without constraining the force characteristic. Reading of w: deviation from the prior shrinks by about 1/(1+w). Grid w = 0 (prior as start only = unanchored control), 0.1, 1, 10. CHOICE RULE: smallest of {0.1, 1, 10} with (G) no new fallback on any usable session and gate-pass count not below production's, and (C) Part 3 CONVERGES on every retry session; none -> no weight selected, w = 1 shown in Part 4 as reference only.
PRE-REGISTERED, Part 3 (loop): retry sessions = pool session with most analysis laps, v3 (recorded divergence), pool session with fewest analysis laps. Pass 1 = Part 2 anchored fit on kinematic alpha; pass p >= 2 = anchored fit on alpha from pass p-1's resolved beta (beta_ekf_with_fallback, kinematic after a fallback), prior frozen, penalty anchored at the prior, Powell from the prior every pass, R derived afresh each pass (production steps (c)-(e)); max 4 passes. m_p = max over axles of max(|dD|/D_prev, max_g |dF| / D_prior) on a fixed grid [0, pass-1 p99]. CONVERGES iff m_3 < m_2, m_4 < m_3, m_4 <= 1 %; DIVERGES iff m_4 > m_3 or D-delta sign alternation without shrinking; else SHRINKING, NOT CONVERGED within 4 passes. Watch items: D inflation (record +34.6 % Dubai, +51.3 % v3) and linear collapse.

## (d2) addendum: where the loop drift lives -- visited vs extrapolated slip range [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

QUESTION (author): does the Part 3 drift live inside each session's visited slip range, or beyond it (the fit inventing the invisible peak while the visible curve holds)?
METHOD (fixed in the script header before it ran; diagnostics/inspect_tyre_prior_d2.py mode drift; curves rebuilt from the cached per-pass B, C, D, E, no new EKF run): split points = pass-1 visited p95 / p99 of |alpha| (kinematic, base_mask), fixed across passes; "beyond p99" ends at the largest per-pass visited p99 of that session and axle (how far the filter's own alpha reaches). PER PASS (drift.txt in full): the pass 1 -> 2 step is large in every region, including inside p95 (w0: 3-12 % of D_prior) -- the one-time switch of the fitted alpha from kinematic to the filter's own; the figures show the initial slope changing with it. From pass 2 on, the change inside p95 is 0.05-2.8 % RMS per pass (0.4-2.8 % at w <= 1), while beyond p99 it stays larger on the unanchored rear axles (v3 rear w0 11.3 % then 5.9 %; JDR 10 rear w0 7.9 % then 2.6 %) -- the peak keeps climbing outside the visited range while the visible curve nearly holds (v3 rear w0 figure: passes 2-4 coincide below p95 and fan out beyond it).
READING: at w = 0 and 0.1 the total drift is extrapolated-dominant on 11 of 12 session-axles (JST 19 rear w0.1 the exception), and the inflation the record describes (D growth) is mostly the invisible peak rising. But the visible curve does not hold over the whole loop: the first refit moves it 3-12 % inside p95, and it keeps moving 1-3 % per pass afterwards on v3 and JST 19.
RE-READING (stated as a re-reading, no new criterion shipped): the Part 3 rule with the metric restricted to the curve change inside p95, max over both axles per pass:
- JDR 10: w0 17.06 / 1.90 / 1.30 % SHRINKING; w0.1 15.06 / 1.41 / 1.13 % SHRINKING; w1 9.14 / 0.90 / 0.82 % CONVERGES.

Per axle alone, JDR 10 front would pass at w0 and w0.1 (0.57 % at pass 4) while its rear does not. ## Door 2: transient-weighted fitting under the (d2) loop -- no signal, door closed [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, read-only]

Hypothesis (author work order "Doors"): the curve/beta degeneracy is exact only in quasi-steady cornering, so a fit weighted towards transient samples should drift less under the fit -> EKF -> refit loop. Fixed in the header of diagnostics/inspect_tyre_prior_d2.py before the runs (modes tloop, door2; output door2.txt): sample weight w_i = max(1, |alpha_dot_i| / median |alpha_dot|) on the alpha being fitted in that pass (median 0.7-1.1 deg/s, half the population above 1, max weight 17-49), weighted mean data term so the prior penalty keeps its scale, residuals to the R derivation unweighted; loop, retry sessions and split points as (d2) Part 3 and the drift addendum; w 0 scored, w 1 reported. SIGNAL iff the post-switch walk inside p95 (m'(2->3) + m'(3->4), max over axles) at w 0 is at most half the uniform value on 2 of 3 sessions. RESULT: 0 of 3 -- walk ratio transient/uniform JDR 10 0.74 (2.36 vs 3.20 %), v3 1.00 (5.59 vs 5.56 %), JST 19 0.95 (5.44 vs 5.70 %); the uniform values recomputed here reproduce the addendum (3.20 / 5.56 vs 5.53 / 5.70 %). The invisible-peak inflation is not reduced either: D_rear pass 4 / pass 1 at w 0 +27.9 / +54.2 / +17.1 % transient vs +21.5 / +50.1 / +13.5 % uniform. v3's transient pass-1 gate reads warn (0.0566) where uniform passes. At w 1 (not scored) the walk ratio is 0.72-0.93. Reading: on this logging, |alpha_dot|-weighting carries no usable separating information for the curve/beta pair; the degeneracy is not broken by emphasising transients. Door 2 CLOSED.

ANCHOR SEARCH (books in docs/literature/, text-searched this session; the Kiencke & Nielsen PDF text layer is a font-substitution cipher, decoded with a fixed character map before searching; section numbers read from its contents pages):
- [2026-10-01 CORRECTION, numbering only, content unchanged, each number checked on the printed body page: ~~8.1~~ 9.1; ~~8.1.2~~ 9.1.2; ~~8.1.4~~ 9.1.4; ~~8.1.1 Eq. (8.1)~~ 9.1.1 Eq. (9.1) and ~~Eq. (8.2)~~ Eq. (9.2) (book pp. 352-353); ~~8.6.1 (Eqs. 8.72-8.74)~~ 9.7.1 (Eqs. 9.82-9.84, p. 403; the "under 5 %" sentence p. 404); ~~8.3.1~~ 9.4.1 (Eqs. 9.22-9.24, p. 376); ~~8.5~~ 9.6 (inputs/measurements 9.6.2 Eq. 9.78, p. 399); ~~8.5.3~~ 9.6.3 (yaw-rate threshold, p. 402); ~~7.3.1/7.3.2~~ 8.3.1/8.3.2. The numbers below are the original, wrong ones.]
- Kiencke & Nielsen 2005, 8.1 (Vehicle Velocity Estimation): v from fusion of all four wheel speeds plus the longitudinal accelerometer (Kalman 8.1.2, fuzzy 8.1.4). 8.1.1 Eq. (8.1) transforms wheel speeds to the CoG with yaw rate, steer angle and beta, stating beta "must be known only for extreme curves" -- the beta content of wheel-speed MAGNITUDE is second order. 8.1.1 Eq. (8.2): accelerometer preprocessing carries a road-gradient term and an a_y sin(beta) term (the tangential-acceleration identity d|v|/dt = a_x cos beta + a_y sin beta). 8.6.1 (Eqs. 8.72-8.74): the residual a_x,meas - r_eff*omega_dot of the NON-DRIVEN wheels is solved for road gradient; stated resolution "under 5 % of absolute road gradient". 8.3.1: friction-value estimation needs wheel angular acceleration, brake torque (from pressure), drive torque (engine torque signal), straight driving. 8.5 (side-slip observer): longitudinal wheel forces are explicit inputs, v and yaw rate are measurements; 8.5.3: above a yaw-rate threshold v is dropped as a measurement because the longitudinal force model fails near the limit. 7.3.1/7.3.2: contact-point velocities; wheel slip needs the tyre slip angle (Burckhardt vs Reimpell definitions differ in the projection).
- Rajamani 2012: 14.1.4 review -- slip-slope friction estimation (Gustafsson 1997) uses the undriven axle as absolute velocity reference, slip from driven-minus-undriven speed, traction only, low slip; braking unusable. 14.5: accelerometer bias as an augmented Kalman state (GPS velocity as measurement). Ch. 8 ESC model: combined Dugoff with per-wheel slip ratios, Vx assumed known. 5.6: absolute velocity not measurable, slip must be estimated.
- Segers 2014, 4.2 (Eq. 4.11-4.12): slip ratio against free-rolling wheel speed, effective radius assumed constant; 4.3: TCS channels (nominal slip, reference speed, actual drivetrain slip). Werner 2021: no estimation content. Ulsoy/Peng/Cakmakci 2012 ch. 14: sideslip usually from the bicycle model (steer, yaw rate, a_y, speed) -- the production family.
- Chair tooling (read-only): calc_long_slip_vectorized takes vx AND vy as inputs -- slip computed from a known sideslip, never the reverse.
- No book on file presents solving the tangential-acceleration residual for beta as a method; the identity (K&N ~~8.1.1 Eq. 8.2~~ 9.1.1 Eq. 9.2 [corrected 2026-10-01]) and the residual-with-non-driven-wheels construction (K&N ~~8.6.1~~ 9.7.1 [corrected 2026-10-01], solved for gradient) are section-verified.

CHANNEL CENSUS (streaming liveness over 20 usable files, headers read from each file; scratch tooling, not kept): log_speed_fl/fr/rl/rr 50 Hz live 20/20; abs_vVeh_absRef 100 Hz live 20/20 (unit mph on Dubai/Le Mans, kph on serial 221 -- per-file units); log_gps_speed and NMEA RMC/VTG speed-over-ground 10 Hz live 20/20; log_pbrake_f/r 100 Hz live 20/20; ecu_slip_act / ecu_slip_nom 50 Hz live 20/20 (ECU drivetrain slip, mean 0.77-1.35 %); ecu_B_tc_act live 19/20 but active on 0.4 % of Dubai samples and ~0.01 % on serial 221; ecu_nmot, ecu_gear live. Driveshaft torque IMSA_MDriveshaftRL/RRFilt and driveshaft rpm: present but all-zero on the two logger-147 files, absent on all 18 serial-221 files -- no measured drive torque anywhere; no engine-torque channel found. IMSA_GPS_vSpeed and MRR_EgoVehSpeed dead. Wheel circumferences (abs_circ, ecu_circwheel, log_circ) configured constants, 1 Hz. Two x-accelerometers on Dubai disagree in session mean by 0.073 g (log_acc_x +0.056, sclu_acc_x -0.017 g). Dubai log_gps_alt spans 9.8-76.9 m session-wide: track flatness is NOT established from the file.
PREMISE CORRECTION: the 2026-09-03 external-reference census ("Refit-loop conclusion") records v3 as having no log_gps_speed. v3 carries log_gps_speed live (10 Hz, n 6,860, max 252 kph); the earlier claim is wrong. It did not change that closure (GPS speed is not a sideslip reference).

PHYSICS OF THE QUESTION: wheel speeds carry beta in two ways. (a) Magnitude: a free-rolling front wheel reads the wheel-plane component of the contact velocity; given |v|, the sensitivity to beta is (delta - beta) = alpha_f + l_f/R, about 0.07-0.26 % of speed per degree of beta -- against the recorded GPS-referenced residual (WP5b(d): post-k std 0.319 m/s, about 0.8 % per sample, GPS latency 0.32 s) and cornering-correlated rolling-radius changes that straights cannot calibrate. (b) Derivative: in quasi-steady cornering a_x,meas - d|v|/dt = -a_y sin beta (+ bias, gradient, mount yaw x a_y, IMU lever arm x r^2) -- first order in beta, scaled by a_y, independent of any tyre curve. Rear wheel speed adds longitudinal slip (force information), not beta.

PROPOSAL (awaiting rulings): Option 1 (recommended) -- derivative form, front non-driven wheels (K&N ~~8.6.1~~ 9.7.1 construction, ~~Eq. 8.2~~ Eq. 9.2 identity [corrected 2026-10-01]), staged: Stage 0 read-only discrimination test on flat-track sessions against the (d2) loop's w 0 per-pass beta; Stage 1 (only on pass) a third EKF measurement in the loop harness, scored like Door 2. Option 2 -- magnitude form against GPS speed: rejected on recorded numbers. Option 3 -- rear slip / combined-slip constraint ((ii)/(iii) of the work order): adds force information or removes samples; cannot add beta information by construction. Pre-registered criteria, cost and OPEN questions as in the session report; nothing is run until the author rules.

## (e) proposal: combined slip in the analysis layer -- anchors, signal inventory, ecu_slip provenance probe, proposal [2026-10-01, branch new-laps, proposal turn, census + one-session probe only]

SCOPE (reviewer ruling, restated): (e) targets the ANALYSIS layer -- a combined-slip / friction-budget reading as evidence -- not the beta estimator. Door 1's closure (exit = a sensor) stands; slip angles still come from estimated beta, so nothing here can reopen it. Grounds (author): a tyre is only ever at its limit in combined slip; a pure-lateral reading structurally under-reads rear saturation on traction exits.

(8.6)/(8.7) (braking/acceleration) and the same combined Dugoff as Eqs. (8.8)-(8.12), stated as taken from 13.10. The two earlier project citations ("Ch. 13.10", 2026-08-19; "Ch. 8 ESC", Door 1) are both correct and name one model.
- Milliken & Milliken, RCVD (scan, page images read): 2.4 Combined Operation (p. 41; SAE vs Sakai slip-ratio sign table); 2.7 Friction Circle and Ellipse (pp. 57-60, Fig. 2.31; resultant sqrt(Fx^2 + Fy^2) worked example; the outside envelope "may be slightly elliptical"); 9.1 Conceptual Development (pp. 345-346: vehicle friction circle after Rice; a car cannot reach it because of traction limits, load transfer, suspension effects, LIMITING STABILITY BALANCE -- the axles seldom reach their limit at the same time -- and brake balance); 9.3/9.4 (pp. 350-354: computed g-g envelopes "neither circular nor elliptical"; RWD example: +0.2 g acceleration at fixed steer drops lateral trim 0.41 -> 0.36 g; measured g-g diagrams read as utilisation of the combined area); 14.3 Combined Slip Characteristics (pp. 480-482, Eqs. 14.13-14.17, normalised combined slip, needs measured tyre data).
- Segers 2014: 4.2 Eqs. (4.11)/(4.12) slip against a free-rolling wheel, effective radius assumed constant; Eq. (4.13) drivetrain slip SR = 100 % x (0.5 (v_RL + v_RR)/v_FL - 1); 4.3: a Bosch engine-controlled TCS logs "nominal slip value" (ECU table over speed, throttle, lateral g), "reference speed" and "slip of drive train" (Eq. 4.13) -- the written anchor for ecu_slip_nom / ecu_slip_act.
- Pacejka, combined-slip Magic Formula: book being sourced by the author; nothing rests on it.
CITATION DISCREPANCY FOUND: the Door 1 records cite Kiencke & Nielsen as "8.1.1 Eq. (8.2)", "8.6.1 (Eqs. 8.72-8.74)", "8.5", "7.3.1/7.3.2". In the printed book (contents pages and body headings checked, pp. 352-353 and 404) these are 9.1.1 Eq. (9.2) [a_X,C = a_X - g sin(chi - chi_road) + a_Y sin beta], 9.7.1 (the "under 5 % of absolute road gradient" sentence is on p. 404), 9.6 (side-slip observer) and 8.3.1/8.3.2. Content correct, numbering one chapter low throughout (most likely the cipher decode of digits). Not corrected here; raised with the author.

SIGNAL INVENTORY (Dubai header census this turn; pool liveness from the Door 1 census and the (d2) intake records of the same 20 files):
- Route (i) ecu_slip_act / ecu_slip_nom, 50 Hz, 0.1 % quantum, live 20/20; ecu_B_tc_act 50 Hz; ecu_mi_tc [%] 10 Hz (TC torque intervention, not examined); ecu_circwheel_front_act / rear_act 2.121 / 2.218 m constant, identical to abs_circ_* and log_circ_* (ratio 1.0457); ecu_speed_fl/fr/rl/rr byte-identical to log_speed_*.
- Route (ii) wheel-speed kappa: log_speed_* 50 Hz live 20/20, already the production LS_ratio input (modules/longitudinal_forces.estimate_slip_ratio: (v_axle - ecu_speed)/ecu_speed, rear divided by 1 + 0.0141, a constant measured on Dubai only).
- Route (iii) demand side: log_acc_x/y 100 Hz; production Fx_r (m a_x, all drive on the rear, brake split by measured pressure, drag placeholder 0) and Fy_r (2-DOF balance from m a_y and I_z psi_dd -- beta-free) already exist; Level-1 Fz_r carries NO aero (lift_coeff 0.0 placeholder); Level-4 damper loads only where the gauges pass quality.
- Damper gauges (new census fact): log_dms_dam_* pass quality on 4 of 20 files (Dubai, Le Mans, PR US-v2, v3). On the 16 NBR files they are LIVE (std 1.7-2.1 kN, the healthy-corner scale) but carry a +60-65 kN additive offset on all four corners (two files read directly), so the range gate fails them -- recoverable only by an offset calibration of the v3-FR kind, not dead.

PROBE: what ecu_slip_act is (Dubai sample, one session, raw channels, speed >= 60 kph, limiter off; scratch script, not kept). Candidates against act: rear/front axle mean (Segers 4.13), rear/FL, rear/ecu_speed, rear/abs_vVeh_absRef, (rear - front)/rear (K&N Eq. 8.9 driving form).
- Straights (n 2,698): act p50 1.4 %; every front-referenced form gives slope 0.92-0.96, intercept 0.00-0.06 pp, R^2 0.92-0.94, median act - H -0.05 to -0.08 pp. act's zero is therefore NOT free rolling: it carries the +1.4 % rear rolling-radius offset uncorrected (WP-S1's +1.41 %), in the ECU's configured circumference frame. abs_vVeh_absRef fits worse (R^2 0.81).
- Braking (n 7,741): act exactly 0 on 89.3 % of samples, R^2 0.00 against every construction -- a braking-gated, traction-only channel.
- Traction (throttle > 20 %, n 25,100): slope 0.46-0.50, R^2 0.67-0.68 for the front-referenced forms; best lag +1 sample (20 ms), corr 0.85. On TC-active samples (n 71) act tracks nom (median act - nom 0.00) while the wheel-speed form reads 1.6-1.8 pp higher. Front axle, ecu_speed and ecu_speed_f* cannot be told apart as the reference; the traction-regime gain of about 0.5 is NOT explained by any construction tested.
- Floor vs effect (straight median removed): wheel-speed kappa straight robust sd 0.21 pp, combined traction (throttle > 50 %, |a_y| >= 0.8 g, n 7,018) median +2.15 / p90 +4.34 pp, TC-active +4.87 pp; act 0.15 pp vs +1.20 / +2.50 pp. Kappa carries usable signal on Dubai (about 10x its floor); on the serial-221 files TC is near-silent (~0.01 %).
- Reading: ecu_slip_act is a Segers-4.13-type drivetrain slip in the ECU's own (offset) circumference frame, braking-gated, with an unexplained compression under traction. Usable as an ordinal traction indicator and, with nom, as the TC margin; NOT validated as a kappa magnitude.

PROPOSAL (awaiting rulings; nothing run beyond the census and the probe):
- Option 1 (recommended, display/evidence tier): rear-axle force-demand occupancy. mu_used,r = sqrt(Fx_r^2 + Fy_r^2) / Fz_r (K&N Eq. 8.22, RCVD 2.7), read per corner-phase against the session's own measured envelope (RCVD 9.3/9.4: empirical, not an assumed circle). For the unsteered rear the resultant magnitude is invariant to the tyre-axis rotation, so it needs neither alpha nor beta nor kappa; the pure-lateral under-read is |F_r|/|Fy_r| - 1. Vehicle-level g-g occupancy is the zero-cost cross-check only (RCVD 9.1: it cannot attribute the limit to an axle). Kappa (route ii) and the TC flag enter as measured corroborators, not inputs. Scored only where Fz_r is Level 4 (4 files); Level-1 Fz without aero would inflate occupancy with speed.
- Option 2 (estimator-input tier if adopted): kappa-conditioned pure-lateral fit -- tests whether the combined-slip signature is visible in the rear fit residuals and whether excluding high-kappa samples cleans the fit. Cannot add beta information (Door 1, Option 3 reasoning); removing exit samples worsens the rear large-slip starvation.
- Option 3 (estimator-input tier): full combined fit Fy(alpha, kappa) (Rajamani 13.10 / Ch. 8 Dugoff now; combined MF once sourced). Needs C_sigma, mu, Fz_r, alpha (hence beta) and a kappa magnitude (route ii; act is not validated). Could represent the friction-budget loss on exits; could NOT rescue beta, and adds parameters to an already starved rear. Full re-derivation boundary.
Pre-registered criteria and costs: in the session report of this date, to be restated in PLAN.md (e) when ruled. [Restated in PLAN.md (e), 2026-10-01, with the rulings below.]

## Tyre-model architecture: the author's intent, recorded, and how it maps onto the built code [2026-10-01, author statement; records only]

INTENT (author, verbatim in substance): the tyre model is TRAINED ONCE ON ALL AVAILABLE DATA (the 18-session pool prior = "something reasonable"); each session TAILORS it. Variant 1 = free fit starting from the prior; Variant 2 = adaptation anchored to the prior, including the scale-only sub-variant. Variants 1 and 2 are the two candidate tailoring mechanisms of the ONE trained model -- there is no separate third model.
MAPPING onto the code as it stands (modules/tyre_fit_auto.py, config/parameters.json tyre_fit_auto; read this turn):
- Trained model: tyre_fit_prior (18 serial-221 sessions, n 1,075,186, "(d2) Part 1"). Built, config-held.
- Variant 2: tyre_fit_mode "prior_anchored" -- Powell started from the prior, curve-space penalty prior_weight (config 1.0). Built, EXPERIMENTAL, Tier A anchor pending.
- Variant 1: no mode of its own. _fit_axle_pacejka_anchored skips the penalty when the weight is 0 and still starts Powell from the prior, so "prior_anchored" with prior_weight 0 IS Variant 1 by construction; no test pins that case.
- Scale-only sub-variant: tested only as (d) step 0 Option B (diagnostics/inspect_tyre_prior.py, pooled prior with per-session scale, against the serial-221 SIX-session prior, not the 18-session one); failed its pre-registered exit; not built.
- Production default "per_session": a free fit started from the chair start guess PACEJKA_START_GUESS = (12.0, 1.9, 8000.0, 0.97), which does not use the trained model. Under the stated architecture this is outside both variants. Whether it differs in result from Variant 1 (same objective, different Powell start; the B/C/E ridge makes start-dependence plausible) is NOT checked.
Nothing in this entry changes a recorded verdict ((d) closure, (d2) convergence-by-suppression, Door 1/2); it records the intended frame they are read in.
MAPPING RULING (author, 2026-10-01): production per_session is a THIRD start point (chair guess) outside the architecture -- (a) now, (c) possibly later. Variant 1 = prior_anchored at prior_weight 0, confirmed. Whether starting from the trained prior changes the fit is tested only in the pending Phase-1/Option-A package; nothing replaces the default without its own boundary.

## Phase 1 anchoring [2026-10-01, author; documentation anchor package, records only]

WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS (methodology): the author's review chat was compacted twice. Standing rule from the author: nothing stays chat-anchored past the current work item; the repository is the project's memory. Every ruling, decision or queue change is written to PLAN.md or thesis_notes.md in the same turn it is made. The operational plan lives in PLAN.md "PHASE 1 PLAN, anchored 2026-10-01"; this entry mirrors its durable, thesis-relevant parts.

EVALUATION CRITERIA (method chapter). The only admissible criteria for the pending estimator and architecture comparisons are: (i) fit-internal mechanics -- residuals, convergence, start-point sensitivity; (ii) the measured NBR A->B rake-change resolution; (iii) the professional driver's NBR statements, phase-differentiated; (iv) CS physical-consistency bounds derived from tyre mechanics alone, never from any session's distribution; (v) internal cross-lap coherence (same corner, same session, similar reading). Retired as criteria on 2026-10-01: the survival battery, C4 (powerless tests), C3-via-LS (system output, never author-approved), gate health against production, and verdict-count comparisons; verdicts recorded under them stand as recorded and are cited with a scope line. Le Mans is banned from scoring (different tyres, author-confirmed); Dubai carries least-representative weight (different tyres and logger).
Rationale: production is a set of calibrated experiments, not ground truth, so a criterion built from the current system's output would make every comparison circular.

STANDING RULINGS. (a) Verdict thresholds are not formally re-derived; the method of record is the author's visual verification on rendered per-session CS traces, and every CS-touching package renders those traces and names its plot folder. (b) No criterion may be built from the current system's output. (c) A recorded negative is cited with a scope line: the data, the conditions, the reopen condition, and whether current data falls inside that scope.

TYRE-MODEL ARCHITECTURE (author, supervisor-aligned). One tyre model is trained once on all available data -- the 18-session pool prior held in config -- and each session tailors it. Two candidate tailoring mechanisms, both to be tested at full depth: Variant 1, prior-as-start (a free four-parameter fit started from the prior, i.e. prior_anchored at prior_weight 0); Variant 2, prior-as-model (the curve-penalised adaptation over a weight grid, plus the scale-only sub-variant with a fixed shape and a per-session scale lambda, so far tested only against the older six-session prior). Status of Variant 1, stated exactly: the same fit ran in (d2) Part 2/3 at w 0 and its start-point dependence is recorded there; (d) rejected it a priori ("Option A") without running it; it has never been tested as a tailoring mechanism against the criteria above. The production default (per_session, chair start guess) is a third path outside the architecture, kept as the recorded legacy baseline; it is replaced only through its own estimator-boundary package.

GPS CONTEXT (limitations/outlook). The project's logging is single-antenna 10 Hz course-over-ground (no independent heading, 0.32 s latency), unlike the RTK / dual-antenna setups of the supervisor's autonomous-racing background. Whether multi-lap averaging compensates is the subject of a pending census; a dual-antenna/RTK logging day remains the named sensor request from the Doors closure.

QUEUE (record of order, details in PLAN.md): Q1 labelled Dubai P2 read; Q2 NBR damper-offset feasibility (gates (e) adoption); Q3 Phase-1 experiments (Variant 1, Variant 2, GPS re-census); Q4 fair trial of the best prior variant against the per-session EKF; Q5 scope-narrowing pass on the (d2)/Doors conclusions after Q3; Q6 (e) adoption proposal after Q2.

## Q2c queued: track slope/bank feasibility -- where gravity enters the chain [2026-10-02, author order + ruling; records only]

QUESTION (read-only, proposal-first; after Q2b, with/before Q3, sharing the GPS-altitude machinery with Q3's GPS census): a per-position gradient map per track from cross-lap-averaged GPS altitude differentiated against distance -- noise floor against the 2-3 % gradient signal.
CONTEXT: slope and bank are measured absences in the chain. Door 1's N4 (p95 gradient 2.9-4.6 %) locked the longitudinal beta route; the roll check's yaw-leak residual groups by track, with gradient/bank the named untested hypothesis. The chain treats every track as flat and level.
LEAK-ROUTE PHYSICS (method; K&N 9.1.1 Eq. 9.2, 9.7.1 Eq. 9.82): the accelerometers measure specific force, a - g, and production uses them raw (prepare_vehicle_state: ax_mps2 = log_acc_x * 9.81, a_y likewise, no gravity term). Forces reconstructed from them -- Fx = m a_x, Fy = m a_y, the load transfers -- are therefore tyre (plus aero) forces with no grade or bank leakage. Gravity enters only where measured acceleration is equated with KINEMATIC acceleration: (i) speed-derivative comparisons such as d|v|/dt (Door 1, road grade); (ii) the beta kinematics beta_dot = a_y/v - r in the kinematic estimator and the EKF propagation, where a bank angle phi adds g sin(phi)/v and so reaches beta -> alpha -> fit -> CS.
PAYOFFS (author ruling, ranked): (1) partial softening of Door 1's N4 -- the N2 lock stands, no reopening claim; (2) bank/grade terms in the beta kinematics, if a bank estimate ever exists. (e) occupancy is not a target. Bank remains unmeasurable with the current channels (no independent bank sensor; the roll-gyro cross-coupling is that failure).
META (process): the review's chat-level claim that grade leaks about 0.3 m/s^2 into the occupancy Fx at 3 % grade was refuted by the session's physics check before it reached the records -- the anchoring rule working as intended.

## Q2b: fuel-channel content check -- one consumption source, an ECU remaining-fuel counter, level channels are plumbing [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, read-only]

Script diagnostics/inspect_fuel_channels.py (checks fixed in its header before the run); outputs diagnostics/plots/fuel_q2b/ (q2b.txt, q2b.json, one figure per file). 20 usable files, raw channels with their own header units, fuel density from the file (log_c_fueldensity 0.748 kg/l on all 20). Run correction: the first pass took the flow-meter total as the "used" reference, which is zero everywhere; the rerun takes the first used-channel that moves (ecu_fuelcons_kg). The used-family numbers are identical in both passes.
- FUEL USED -- ONE SOURCE, NOT THREE: Team_Fuel_Used [ltr] equals ecu_fuelcons [ltr] and Team_Fuel_Used_Stint [kg] equals ecu_fuelcons_kg [kg] on every file (identical consumed values); litres x density agree with kg to 0.995-0.998. The team channels mirror the ECU's consumption model, so the cross-family check is not independent. The flow meter (ffm_mass_total / ffm_mass_total.mass, DTM_ffm_mass_total) reads ZERO consumption on all 20 files. Burn per file 5.9-26.3 kg; per-lap steps median 1.9-2.3 kg (Le Mans 5.7). Lap-sum plausibility: Team_Fuel_Used_per_Lap step sums match the total within ~0.5 kg on most files and fall short on long-run files (e.g. US-v2 16.5 vs 25.4 kg, JDR 10 22.1 vs 26.3) -- consistent with laps whose value repeats or is not stepped (out/in laps), not checked further.
- vol_fuel_rem_telem (present on 4 usable files: NBR QP CDR, NBR QP MLA, PR US-v2, v3): remaining = set value - ECU fuel used, EXACTLY (slope -0.997 against used litres, rms 0.00 l). The set values are round: 102 l on the two NBR qualifying files and US-v2, 70 l on v3 -- an entered starting assumption at the last counter reset, not a measurement. File-start remaining: 102.0 / 79.3 / 51.6 / 61.4 l (76 / 59 / 39 / 46 kg); the second NBR qualifying file starts at the first one's end value (counter carried over, no reset between them).
- LEVEL-NAMED CHANNELS (premise: catch tank / plumbing -- confirmed in behaviour): log_fuellevel_catch flat at 10.0-10.19 l (near-full share 1.00) on 16 of 20 files; below full on the two Paul Ricard files (8.6-9.7 l) and dipping on the two NBR qualifying files (min 9.15-9.35 l, back to 10.0) -- including NBR QP CDR, whose computed remaining stays >= 79 l, so the dips are not explained by low total fuel alone; not pursued. lvlfuel_lvl_raw sits at 34-46 % with a 0.7-2.6 % range per file over 6-26 kg of burn, weakly negative against fuel used (rho -0.78 to +0.12); a main-cell level would move by tens of percent -- not a total-fuel level. The sensor voltage tracks lvlfuel_lvl_raw. Slosh (5 s detrended std) cornering vs straights near equal on every channel. No stationary >= 20 s plateau inside the analysed files except one (Le Mans: level change -0.014 %).
- READING (mass chain): the within-outing burn trace is logged (ECU consumption model; Level-3 shape, single source, flow meter dead). RULINGS AND CORRECTIONS [2026-10-02, author]:
1. ~~Counter start values (102 / 70 l, 4 files) used as a provisional starting load, labelled "team assumption (ECU-entered), unverified", Level 2.~~ [Struck 2026-10-02 by author correction: the counter start values are RELICS -- nobody types fuel values into this car (author, operational knowledge). 3. STANDS: the CUMULATIVE fuel-used channel (ecu_fuelcons_kg / Team_Fuel_Used_Stint) is authoritative for burn. The per-lap channel undercounts on long runs (US-v2 16.5 vs 25.4 kg) and must not be summed for totals -- standing note for any future mass work.
CHECK OF CORRECTION 2 ON THE FILES (2026-10-02, catch tank vs burn and speed over time, 4 candidate files): NO file dips near run end. NBR QP CDR: full (10.0 l) at every decile and no episode deeper than 0.05 l in this read; the Q2b summary minimum (9.346 l) did not reproduce (possibly a second channel block of the same name; not chased). Consequences: (a) no starting-load lower bound is derivable on any file -- the catch-tank route salvages nothing for the archive; (b) the "dip at 79 l remaining" that was to confirm the counter as a relic does not survive this read, so the relic verdict rests on the author's operational knowledge (correction 1) alone, which is sufficient on its own.
DESIGN FACT AND LIMITATION [2026-10-02, author]: fuel load was always designed as a SESSION INPUT to SetupTool (engineer-entered at session start) -- the intended forward path, unchanged; combined with the cumulative burn channel it gives Level-2/3 per-sample mass on future sessions (UI tier, whenever UI work resumes). For the 20 archive sessions it cannot be reconstructed: the values are not recoverable (author) and the channels cannot supply it (burn measured, start absent, counters relics, catch tank no bound). ARCHIVE STARTING MASS IS PERMANENTLY UNKNOWN -- a limitation with size, not an open question: about +/-40 kg of fuel, about +/-3 % of the 1356 kg config mass, propagating into fitted D, Fz-normalised quantities (mu, occupancy) and every force-per-mass comparison across sessions. The team question about archive fuel loads is STRUCK. (Limitations register item 14.)
