## Q2 proposal: NBR damper-offset feasibility + limitation-11 load-source check [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, proposal turn; code/record reads only]

SCOPE: read-only feasibility. Can the +60-65 kN additive offset on all four log_dms_dam_* gauges of the 16 NBR files be recovered per outing from in-file data, without a physical weighing? Success would unlock Level-4 (damper-measured) rear loads on up to 16 more files -- the adoption gate of (e).
FACTS FROM THE READS:
- Precedent (config channel_corrections.log_dms_dam_fr, v3): an additive decoding offset applied in csv_parser before the quality gate, guarded by a precondition on the file's raw mean; anchored with a HEALTHY AXLE MATE on the same file (FL) plus a per-outing weighing. On NBR all four corners carry the offset -- there is no healthy mate, so the anchor must be a static load reference instead.
- Static reference available: config vehicle.corner_weights 290 / 290 / 395 / 381 kg (Level 1, "measured on setup patch", event not stated). Its uncertainty for an NBR outing includes the permanently unknown fuel load (limitations item 14, ~+/-40 kg) and possible between-event base-weight differences.
- Record correction found: (d)'s EC3 line reports "Fz source measured" for every session including the six NBR files. In estimate_vertical_loads that label is the cascade PATH ("measured" whenever the damper cascade runs), not the per-corner TIER -- Dubai also reports "measured" with RR reconstructed. The existing record therefore does not show which tier the NBR loads behind limitation 11 came from.
PROPOSED PARTS (simplest first):
- Part A, limitation-11 check: per-sample tier census (vertical_load_source_per_sample) on the six (d) NBR sessions; then the PR sessions' rear mean Fz on the fit population recomputed on the STATIC path. SOURCE-EXPLAINED iff the NBR rear tiers are static fallback on >= 95 % of samples AND the PR static-path rear mean lies within +/-5 % of the NBR 7.6 kN; otherwise the track reading of item 11 stands.
- Part B, offset census (16 NBR files, one streaming pass): per corner raw mean and std; within-file stationarity as the drift of the straight-line raw mean (|a_x|, |a_y| < 0.1 g) between the first and last third of the run at matched speed bins; between-file constancy; inventory of stationary windows (speed < 3 kph, >= 1 s). Bars: stationary within a file iff matched-speed drift <= 100 N per corner (5 % of the healthy corners' dynamic std 1.9-2.1 kN, the precedent's own scale); a shared logger-family offset iff the per-file offsets agree within 100 N.
- Part C, anchor (Tier B: sensor zero calibration against a known static load; method anchor of the load decomposition Segers ch. 9/10): C1 stationary samples -> offset_c = raw_c - static pushrod force from the corner weights through the motion ratio; C2 straight-line v^2 extrapolation to v = 0 (aero absorbed in the slope, all straights usable); C3 one shared offset if Part B finds a logger-family constant. Pick by the selection principle.
- Validation (physics, offset-sensitive where possible): no corner load below -200 N outside kerb samples (p0.1); outer-wheel loading with a_y correctly signed, |corr| >= 0.85 per corner (offset-invariant -- a liveness/sign check only); total load rising with v^2 (downforce >= 0). Stated plainly: absolute accuracy is bounded by the static reference (Level-1 corner weights, fuel unknown) -- the result would be a Level-4 SHAPE on a Level-1 OFFSET.
- Exit (pre-registered): FEASIBLE iff Part B stationarity holds on >= 12 of 16 files, the chosen anchor's per-corner offset uncertainty is <= +/-300 N (about the +/-40 kg fuel spread over an axle), and validation passes on >= 12 of 16 files. NOT FEASIBLE iff the offset drifts beyond the bar on > 4 files or no usable reference exists on most files.
BOUNDARY: read-only diagnostic. Adoption would be a config channel_corrections entry (one per corner or one family) -- Fz is verdict-independent by the 2026-09-04 proof (CS / stability never take Fz), to be re-verified at adoption; consumers are fy_norm display, the diagnostic mu fit, and (e) occupancy.

## Q2 run: NBR damper offset NOT FEASIBLE per outing; limitation 11 explained by the load source [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, read-only]

RULINGS BEFORE THE RUN (author): proposal approved as written (A -> B -> C, bars and exit as pre-registered); corner-weight provenance unknown -- caveat "event unstated; between-event base-weight difference inherited on top of fuel uncertainty"; result label "L4-rel" (Level-4 shape on a Level-1 offset), not plain Level 4, upgradeable if the offset provenance improves.
SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_damper_offset_q2.py (header = pre-registration plus [impl] choices fixed before the run); outputs diagnostics/plots/damper_offset_q2/ (partA.json, partB_<key>.json, q2.txt, q2_summary.json, loads_<key>.png). Method fact used: the chain is linear in the gauge offset K, fz_c(K) = fz_c(0) - K MR_c(travel) (modules/wheel_loads.py), so one chain run per file gives every candidate.
IMPLEMENTATION FIXES FOUND BY THE ONE-FILE SMOKE TEST (nbr_o019_jst), before the 16-file run, disclosed: (1) the "on wheels" travel band for stationary windows was taken from straights > 60 kph, where downforce compresses the suspension, so every stationary sample fell outside it -- now taken from low-speed driving (5-80 kph, p0.5-p99.5); (2) a file with one analysis lap has no lap-spread SE for C2, and the first version then counted only the fuel term (u = 98 N, a spurious pass) -- an undefined statistical term now fails the leg (insufficient evidence); (3) an UNSCORED sensitivity row for the drift with |a_x| < 0.2 g was added, because the pre-registered |a_x| < 0.1 g straight filter leaves few NBR samples (47-497 per drift estimate). Also: the proposal said "six" (d) NBR sessions; (d) had four, used.
PART A (limitation 11) -- SOURCE-EXPLAINED: on the four (d) NBR sessions every corner is on the static fallback for 100 % of the fit population, so their "measured" path equals the static path (rear 7621-7631 N). Paul Ricard on the static path: 7626 N (v3), 7626 N (US-v2) -- ratio 1.0002 to the NBR mean 7624 N (bar +/-5 %). The 10.2-10.3 kN elsewhere are damper-measured and carry downforce; the Level-1 static model carries none. Limitation 11's track reading is withdrawn (dated correction there). Side finding, corrected in three records: Dubai's rear axle (RR reconstructed) is the SESSION-CORRECTED quasi-static axle total with a session-fitted aero term, not "Level 1 without aero" as recorded at Stage 0 and Q1; the N2 exclusion stands.
PART B (16 NBR files): within-file stationarity (burn-corrected matched-speed drift <= 100 N on all four corners) holds on 2 of 16 (o005 MLA, o054 CDR); drifts up to +667 N, mostly positive (later in the run the gauges read higher at the same speed and burn-corrected mass). Unscored sensitivity (|a_x| < 0.2 g, 3-5x the samples): 6 of 16 within the bar; the three short runs (JST problem, o018, o019) drift +150 to +570 N on nearly every corner either way -- a systematic early-run effect (tyre warm-up via ride height, or gauge thermal drift; not separated). Between files: per-corner C2 offsets spread 1.1-2.3 kN (bar 100 N) -- no shared logger-family offset, C3 not applicable. Stationary on-wheel windows: 1-2 per file, 1.5-5 s each, on all 16 files.
PART C: C1 and C2 disagree by up to ~1.2 kN in wheel units on some corners; per-corner uncertainty u 204-1212 N; u <= 300 N on all four corners on 0 of 16 files. VALIDATION with the chosen anchor: 8 of 16 pass; V2 (correctly signed lateral transfer, |corr| 0.85-0.90) and V3 (load rising with v^2) pass everywhere; failures are V1 (a corner's p0.1 below -200 N, down to -796 N) -- consistent with offsets wrong by a few hundred N.
P4 RENDERS (loads_<key>.png, inspected): recovered axle loads have a physically sensible, lap-repeatable shape (transfer, aero-loaded straights), while their absolute level differs between files of the same car and event (rear ~10-11 kN on JST solution vs ~9 kN on o046) -- the anchor spread made visible.
EXIT (pre-registered): NOT FEASIBLE -- drift beyond the bar on 14 of 16 files (> 4), uncertainty leg 0 of 16. Reading: the gauges carry a live, correctly signed load SHAPE (the "L4-rel" description is accurate), but the absolute offset is neither constant within a run at the 100 N level nor shared between files, and the only static references (1-2 windows of a few seconds against Level-1 corner weights of unstated event) cannot pin it to +/-300 N. Consequences: NBR rear loads stay on the static fallback (limitation 13 unchanged); (e)'s adoption gate does NOT open on this route -- reach stays 2 of 20; limitation 11 is now a recorded source difference, not a track property.
[2026-10-02 NOTE, author input (operational knowledge): in the Porsche system, damper/load-sensor OFFSET values are specified INVERSELY to the usual convention and in unusual units. Any future gauge calibration or team-supplied offset must be interpreted in the Porsche convention before use. The NOT-FEASIBLE exit is unaffected: within-run drift and between-file spread are convention-independent.]

## Q2d: rear-curve bias diagnostic -- convergent read uninterpretable (fits 2/3 degenerate), Option-2 residual signature present but phase-confounded; the fit population is dominated by kinematic-alpha error [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, read-only]

HYPOTHESIS (author): the rear pure-lateral fit is biased low, most at large alpha, because combined-slip exit samples (Stage 0: ~37 % longitudinal share, under-read >= 8 %, 41 % at p90) carry less lateral force than the pure-lateral capability, plus one-sided sub-limit scatter.
SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_rear_curve_bias.py (rules in its header, fixed before the runs); sessions PR US-v2 and v3 on the (d2) production fit cache (kinematic alpha, Fy_filt, production base mask). Outputs diagnostics/plots/rear_curve_bias/: q2d.txt, q2d.json, curves_pr_us_v2_rear.png, curves_pr_us_v2_front.png, curves_v3_rear.png, curves_v3_front.png, residual_kappa_pr_us_v2.png, residual_kappa_v3.png, run_log.txt. Fits: (1) production, (2) low-kappa (|kappa - straight median| < 3 x straight robust sd), (3) q = 0.9 binned upper quantile (0.2 deg bins, >= 30 samples) with Pacejka through the bin points; all from the chair start guess. Bar 3.8 % of D (quadrature of the recorded GPS k / a_y scale / mass components; a common scale error largely cancels in fit-to-fit deltas, so a lap bootstrap B = 100 gives the statistical context). Pre-registered reads: READ-L (as ordered) and READ-C (construction-corrected for fit 3: an upper-quantile fit lies above a least-squares fit by construction, so only its alpha-dependence, upper minus lower region delta, is informative).
ENTRY CHECK: production fit reproduced exactly (max relative parameter difference 0.0 on all four session-axles).
RESULTS (rear US-v2 / v3; deltas as % of production D, 95 % lap-bootstrap CI):
- Fit 2 low-kappa: lower region -7.1 / -7.1 %, upper region +2.4 [-1.9, +5.9] / -10.2 [-14.3, -5.6] %; keeps 27 % of the population but only 9-10 % of the upper-alpha region.
- Fit 3 q90: lower +106 / +111 %, upper +57 / +58 %, excess (upper - lower) -49 / -53 %.
- READ-L: NOT SUPPORTED on both. READ-C: NOT SUPPORTED (US-v2), CONTRADICTED (v3). Front (control, no prediction): READ-C CONTRADICTED on both.
- Option-2 signature (pre-registered in the (e) proposal): rear production residual on high-kappa exit samples -2267 N [-2655, -1910] = -22.5 % of D (US-v2, n 25,526) and -2661 N [-3426, -1905] = -28.1 % of D (v3, n 7,318) -- PRESENT on both by its pre-registered statistic.
POST-HOC FIT HEALTH (labelled; recorded (d) K2 band, Rajamani Eq. 13.67: C in (1, 2], E <= 1): fit 2 is non-physical on every session-axle (rear C 0.84 / 2.32, E -145 / -284; front E -62 / -140); fit 3 is a step (rear B 381 / 328, E 1.03 > 1, "peak" at 0.23-0.26 deg). Production itself sits marginally above C = 2 on the rear (2.006 / 2.007), as (d) already recorded.
RENDER INSPECTION (before any reading): the folded fit population carries dense bands of +/-10-15 kN rear force at near-zero kinematic |alpha| (0-3 deg), in BOTH signs -- the kinematic-seed alpha error the production fit is built on, not a tyre property. The low-kappa population is the straights/coasting cloud (Fy near 0, |alpha| < 2 deg), so fit 2 is fitted on the wrong part of the cloud by construction; the q90 bin points at small alpha sit on the high-force bands, so fit 3 snaps to a step. The residual-vs-kappa curves are NON-MONOTONIC: exit-phase residual strongly negative at kappa excursions 0.5-4.5 pp (-20 to -55 % of D), positive below zero and again above ~4.7 pp; non-exit residual mostly positive.
READING: (1) The convergent-evidence test is UNINTERPRETABLE, not a refutation: both test fits fail the recorded plausibility band, for structural reasons visible in the renders (population starvation; quantile on alpha-corrupted bins). Neither READ-L nor READ-C carries a verdict about the hypothesis. (2) The Option-2 signature is present by its pre-registered statistic, but its kappa structure is phase-confounded and non-monotonic, so it cannot be attributed to combined slip alone; with kinematic alpha this wrong, a residual is as much an alpha error as a force deficit. (3) The dominant error in the production fit population is alpha quality (kinematic seed), which this diagnostic cannot separate from combined slip -- consistent with the recorded curve/beta circularity. Low-bias hypothesis: neither supported nor refuted on this data. For Q3: any variant scoring that rests on the fitted rear curve inherits this alpha-dominated population.
RULINGS (author, 2026-10-02, recorded below; the combined Q2c + Q3 proposal follows in "Q2c + Q3 combined proposal").
RULINGS DETAIL: (1) READ-C accepted (pre-run, disclosed; moot by degeneracy). (2) Degenerate fits cannot testify: "uninterpretable, not refuted" stands, post-hoc label noted. The low-bias hypothesis remains OPEN -- unmeasurable at the current alpha quality. The Option-2 signature (-22 to -28 % of D, non-monotonic in kappa) is recorded as REAL BUT ENTANGLED. (3) Alpha quality is the first-order confound for curve-shape scoring; the Q3 courtroom narrows to alpha-robust criteria (PLAN.md PHASE 1 PLAN section 1, amended 2026-10-02); the render finding is an estimator-chapter exhibit (section 1, "The kinematic-seed alpha error made visible").

## Q2c + Q3 combined proposal: GPS census, track gradient map, corner anchor, Variant 1 and Variant 2 at full depth [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, proposal turn; header census only]

COURTROOM (PHASE 1 PLAN section 1, amended 2026-10-02): (i) fit-internal MECHANICS only (convergence, start-point sensitivity, no curve-truth claims); (ii) rake A->B resolution; (iii) driver statements; (v) cross-lap coherence; (iv) CS physical bounds = sanity screen only. Le Mans banned; Dubai least weight.
HEADER CENSUS THIS TURN (names only, 22 census files): GPS-related families -- log_gps_* (lat/lon/alt/course/speed/hdop/sats/quality/data_age, 22/22); NMEA RX RMC/VTG (course over ground, speed over ground, mode; 22/22 -- an external NMEA source received by the logger); gpsa_* (lat/long/alt/speed/time/track_condition, 20/22; never examined before); DTM_gps_sats/time (20/22); IMSA_GPS_* (2/22, logger 147). TO_VBOX_01..05 (22/22) reads as an output TO a VBOX, not a receiver. No heading, dual-antenna, RTK or slip-angle channel by name. Altitude: log_gps_alt (22/22), gpsa_alt (20/22). log_gps_gsep in [ft] on 5 files, [m] on 17 (per-file units).
PART G0 -- GPS census (all 20 usable files): per family liveness, rate, units, latency against the IMU (cross-correlation of GPS speed derivative vs a_x, as WP5b(d) did for 0.32 s), and INDEPENDENCE between families (identical position/speed traces = one receiver re-broadcast; distinct noise = two receivers). Output decides how many independent receivers G1/G2 can use.
PART G1 = Q2c -- gradient map per track: lap-averaged altitude per independent family against lap distance, gradient d(alt)/ds; noise = lap-to-lap sd of the per-position gradient / sqrt(N laps). USABLE iff the per-position gradient SE <= 1 % (one third of the 2-3 % signal) on >= 80 % of the lap length, and two independent families (if G0 finds two) agree within that SE. Payoffs as ruled: (1) Door 1 N4 softening -- the N2 lock stands, no reopening claim; (2) bank/grade terms in the beta kinematics if a bank estimate ever exists (bank stays unmeasurable). (e) occupancy is not a target (gravity-free by construction).
PART G2 -- corner anchor and yield: a beta reference from GPS course over ground minus a heading reference, cross-lap averaged at matched corner positions after latency alignment. Heading is not logged; the only route is integrated yaw rate re-zeroed per lap on straights (where beta ~ 0) -- stated as the method's own assumption. Anchor noise = lap-to-lap sd / sqrt(N) of (course - heading) per corner position. BAR (ruled: the anchor must resolve below what it discriminates): the recorded beta-candidate separation is median |dbeta| p1 vs p4 = 0.78 / 1.24 / 1.47 deg (Door 1 Stage 0, Dubai / v3 / US-v2) -> anchor SE <= 0.39 deg (half the smallest separation). Yield on the 12 new long NBR sessions: corner-laps with valid GPS (quality, sats, hdop, data_age) per session. G2 results are reported; whether a passing anchor may enter the courtroom is an author ruling (it is not on the approved list).
PART V1 -- Variant 1 (prior-as-start = prior_anchored at prior_weight 0) vs production (chair start), free 4-parameter fit, on the 18 pool sessions (+ Dubai at least weight; Le Mans not scored). Criterion (i): convergence (Powell success; K2 band as sanity screen), start-point sensitivity = curve RMS difference inside the visited range as % of D. MATERIALITY BAR (derived, provenance): input-error family = quadrature of the recorded scale components -- GPS speed k 0.5-1.2 % ((a2), eight sessions), a_y scale up to 4.5 % (log_acc_y pooled referee 0.996-1.045, (a2) Part 4), mass/fuel +/-3 % (limitations item 14) -> 5.5 % of D, a LOWER bound (between-event base weight unbounded). Stated with it: common scale errors cancel in fit-to-fit deltas on the same data, so a lap bootstrap of the delta is reported beside the bar (Q2d precedent). Sessions where the difference exceeds the bar are MATERIAL and get the full chain (EKF beta -> alpha -> CS) and the courtroom (ii), (iii), (v); immaterial sessions are recorded as "same answer".
PART V2 -- Variant 2 at full depth: prior_anchored at w = 0.1 / 1 / 10 and the scale-only sub-variant (prior shape frozen, per-session lambda by closed-form least squares, EKF run on the scaled prior) against the 18-session prior (scale-only was so far tested only against the 6-session prior). Same chain and courtroom.
Q4 FOLD-IN: production (per_session, chair start) is one contestant beside V1 and the V2 variants on the same courtroom; nothing is scored against production quality.
CRITERIA OPERATIONALISED (fixed here, before any run):
- (ii) rake A->B: NBR A = outing 21 (JST problem, 2 analysis laps) vs B = outing 29 (JST solution); measured rake change +2.5-3.7 mm at matched speed, damper clicks reported by the author but not logged (change partly unquantified). Per corner, apex-region CS_f and gap CS_r - CS_f medians; RESOLVED iff |change| > 2 x combined leave-one-lap-out SE (the recorded procedure); expected direction front up / gap narrower. Score = resolved-in-expected-direction minus resolved-opposite, over 14 matched corners; A's two laps cap the statistic (stated). [2026-10-02 CORRECTION (author): the change was rake + springs, no clicks; the pinned direction rested on the withdrawn understeer label -- see "AUTHOR CORRECTIONS 2026-10-02".]
- (iii) driver statements: scored only from statements recorded in the repo with corner/phase, phase-differentiated; the recorded NBR A label is "understeer" -- its phase content is not in the record (OPEN).
- (v) cross-lap coherence: per corner-phase lap-to-lap IQR of CS (lower = more coherent), read TOGETHER with (ii) -- a constant estimator is perfectly coherent and resolves nothing, so (v) alone never ranks a variant.
- (iv) sanity screen: a variant producing CS outside tyre-mechanics bounds on a session is flagged, not scored.
- Render rule: CS traces per session per variant (diagnostics/trace_render.py), folder named in the report; inspected before any exit.
DECISION RULE (proposed, needs the author's ruling): a variant earns an adoption proposal only if (i) passes (converges; start-insensitive within the bar or the material difference is explained), (ii) score >= production + 2 with zero opposite-direction resolutions, (v) not worse than production by more than the lap-bootstrap spread, and (iii) not contradicted; comparable evidence -> the simpler candidate (production / Variant 1 are equally simple; Variant 2 adds a weight and a prior).
[2026-10-02: the driver statement for criterion (iii) is anchored below, "Driver statement (iii), NBR outing A".]
ORDER AND COST: G0 (one streaming pass, ~30 min) -> G1 (cheap, cached altitude) -> G2 -> V1 fits (18 x 2, cached arrays, minutes) -> V1 full chain on material sessions (~5 min EKF each) -> V2 (w-grid x 18 + scale-only x 18 fits; chains on NBR A/B and the material sessions) -> Q4 synthesis. Several hours, overnight-able. BOUNDARY: read-only; adopting any variant is an ESTIMATOR-INPUT CHANGE with its own boundary package (threshold verification by rendered CS traces per rule 2a, goldens, full suite, schema bump if cached values change) and the pending Tier A anchor for a prior-plus-deviation fit.

## Driver statement (iii), NBR outing A [2026-10-02, author input; recorded verbatim]

SOURCE AND CONFIDENCE: the author's direct recollection of the pro driver's account, recorded 2026-10-02 (after the event, not a contemporaneous log). NBR outing A = outing 21 (JST "problem", nbr_jst_problem); B = outing 29 (JST "solution").
STATEMENT (verbatim, as given by the author): "the weekend's problem was getting the car INTO THE WINDOW. Behaviour: ENTRY snappy/unstable -> flips immediately to LAZY, poor rotation MID-CORNER -> ON THROTTLE twitchy, lacking grip again. Oscillates around the window, not one-sided."
SCORING CONSEQUENCE (author ruling, PLAN.md PHASE 1 PLAN Q3 ruling 2): criterion (iii) is matched PER PHASE -- entry: rear-instability signature; mid-corner: front-limitation signature; exit: rear-traction signature. An A -> B improvement may read as LESS EXTREME IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, not as a single-direction shift. This replaces the direction-only fallback.
NOTE: the earlier record calls outing A "labelled understeer"; the statement shows the problem was phase-alternating (entry and exit rear, mid-corner front), so a single understeer label describes only the mid-corner part.

Cause (checked read-only on Dubai and NBR A before any reading): the pre-registered straight gate (|a_y| < 0.1 g, |r| < 2 deg/s, v > 100 kph, run >= 1 s) is applied to the unfiltered 100 Hz state signals; a_y carries 0.15-0.23 g sample-to-sample vibration noise, above the 0.1 g gate, so the mask never stays true for 1 s (longest run 0.59 s Dubai, 0.31 s NBR A; 13 % of moving samples pass sample-wise). 3. SE vs apex speed: Spearman -0.29 (n 274) -- precision improves with speed.
4. Kerb: kerb minus clean corner-lap mean, median 0.02 deg over 97 corners -- no exclusion.
5. Lap count: median SE 0.21 deg at N = 2 down to 0.13 deg at N = 9, log-log slope -0.36 (flatter than sqrt-N); the bar is met at N = 2 -- lap count is not the limit.
6. Cross-session consistency FAILS: 276 of 1620 same-corner session pairs (17 %) agree within 1 x combined SE (bar 60 %).
GATE B: FAIL on checks 1, 2 and 6. CLOSURE (pre-registered wording): "anchor forms but fails validation on sign/phase straight leg, latency robustness and cross-session consistency, route closed at this logging". Part 3 not run (gated); Part 4 never in scope.
MECHANISM (labelled reading): the anchor is PRECISE BUT NOT ACCURATE. The construction makes beta_gps first-order sensitive to the course delay -- at apex yaw rates of 20-30 deg/s, 50 ms of course timing is ~1-1.5 deg of heading, exactly what check 2 measured. The 0.39 deg discrimination bar would need the delay known to < 10 ms per session, while the measured per-session delays already spread 0.21-0.33 s (G0, magnitudes) on a 10 Hz receiver. Small SEs (precision) with ~1 deg session-specific biases (check 6) and a small positive straight bias (check 1a) are the expected signature of that, plus the linear-in-time drift closure. The anchor's limiting term is latency, not noise or lap count.
CONSEQUENCE AND SCOPE LINE: the GPS corner-anchor route is CLOSED at this logging (single-antenna 10 Hz course over ground, ~0.2-0.33 s receiver delay, heading from integrated yaw with time-linear drift closure, 16 NBR + 2 Paul Ricard sessions). Reopen condition: a heading or sideslip reference without the course-delay sensitivity (dual-antenna / RTK GPS with a characterised low latency, or an optical slip sensor) -- the sensor request already named in the Doors closure and the PHASE 1 PLAN GPS context, now with a measured reason (delay sensitivity ~25 deg per second of delay error at apex yaw rates). The WP5b(c) negative (2026-07-26) is consistent with this, now on 18 sessions and on criteria not built from system output.
RULINGS (author, 2026-10-02, close-out): commit first (author runs it), Q5 scope-narrowing pass afterwards on the clean state, so the rewrite never shares a diff with the experiments it narrates; the scripts behind the G2 and A/B closures (inspect_phase1_q3.py, inspect_g2_anchor_validation.py, inspect_rake_ab_anchor.py -- three; the report's "four" was a miscount) stay keep-reproduces, each backing a thesis-citable closure.

## Q-RAW: raw-channel case file -- the sclu_* inertial channels are bus signals, the sclu accelerometers demonstrably filtered; the logger's own log_acc_* look unfiltered [2026-10-02, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: PLAN.md PHASE 1 PLAN Q-RAW (author); standing instruction "gates escalate, never cancel" (PROCESS RULES). Prepare the one team question with real upside: are the logged inertial channels raw body-axis sensor outputs or processed signals, and could raw versions be added to the logging configuration?
SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_raw_channels.py (rules frozen in its header before the run); native samples from the raw exports over the analysis laps of pr_us_v2, v3, nbr_jst_solution (serial 221) and Dubai (serial 147). Outputs diagnostics/plots/raw_channels/: raw_<key>.json, psd_<key>.png, raw_channels.txt.
CENSUS (from the file, v3 and Dubai channel lists): besides the sclu signals every file carries sclu_crc_tx1-3, sclu_msg_cnt_tx1-3, per-signal *_stat channels and sclu_HW_index; v3 also carries *_dash copies; a third accelerometer set ADR2_acc_x/y/z; computed channels a_yaw_velocity, v_yawrate, a_yaw_theo.
FINDINGS (same on all four files, both loggers):
- SPECTRUM: sclu rate channels fall 28-38 dB and sclu accelerometers 14-24 dB from their 2-8 Hz level to the top 20 % of the 50 Hz band; log_acc_x/y/z keep a flat floor (drop -2.7 to +3.1 dB). The paired read is the evidence (render psd_v3.png): log_acc_y and sclu_acc_y coincide below ~10 Hz and part above ~15 Hz, log_acc_y rising with vibration to 50 Hz, sclu_acc_y 15-20 dB below it. Reading: the sclu accelerometers carry on-board low-pass filtering; log_acc_* look unfiltered. The gyro roll-off is CONSISTENT with filtering but not separable from the natural decay of yaw/roll motion (no unfiltered gyro reference): not claimed.
- BUS FRAME: sclu_msg_cnt_tx1 is a 4-bit alive counter (0-15), logged at 10 Hz, stepping +10 mod 16 almost always -> a 100 Hz sensor frame with counter and CRC: the sclu values reach the logger as a bus message from a control unit. Status channels 0 throughout.
- QUANTISATION / HOLD: sclu rate step 0.001666 rpm (0.01 deg/s), sclu acc 0.000127 g, log_acc 0.000742 g; repeat share 0.1-2 % (effective update ~98-100 Hz) -- no stale frames.
- LIMITS: log_acc_y reaches about +/-5 g on US-v2 (rare samples); sclu_acc_y stays within about +/-2.9 g.
- LAGS (100 Hz grid): sclu_acc_y and ADR2_acc_y about 20 ms either side of log_acc_y; MRR_EgoYawRate 0.28-0.29 s behind sclu_yaw_rate (record 0.24-0.30 s), dead on Dubai.
- ADR2_acc_*: 10 Hz, step 0.0735 g, flat (aliased) spectrum -- too coarse for the chain.
CASE FILE: docs/team_questions_raw_channels.md (team-readable, no car data, tracks and loggers anonymised; reviewed by the author before sending). Evidence assembled from the records: roll-channel yaw leak 1.2-2.5 deg grouping by track on a body-fixed sensor ("Roll closure check ...", "Sensor tilt vs static attitude ..."), MRR yaw a delayed bus copy, sclu_acc_y 4-8.5 % below log_acc_y with the correct one undecidable ("Second IMU sources ..."), the serial-221 ay intercept, per-session gyro bias ("IMU offsets, Part 5"). Ask: bus channel list; definition of the sclu channels (raw vs filtered / compensated / axis-transformed, filter spec, body-axis roll rate); mounting; raw gyro/accel added to the logging configuration for one test day.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CHAIN (factual, no proposal): production integrates sclu_yaw_rate (a bus signal from the cluster, filtering not established) against log_acc_y (logger accelerometer, unfiltered) in beta_dot = a_y / v - r -- inputs from two different front ends. Any cluster roll-off sits mostly above the chain's 2 Hz low-pass, but the ~20 ms relative offset between the two inputs is not removed by it. Its effect on the integral is not quantified: a named, untested candidate contributor to the in-corner error, not a finding.

Prediction confirmed: bias-first does nothing useful under the washout. S1a and S1b differ by less than either differs from S0, so the ay-offset disagreement (S0-median vs referee intercept) does not matter to the seed at this stage.
- S2 / S3a / S3b (segment integration, beta = 0 on straights, linear closure): M1 shrink front 41-78 %, rear 34-47 %; M3 0.322 / 0.418 / 0.441 (S2) -- "degraded" on US-v2 and JST 29 under the pre-registered bound. Segment closing error |e| median 1.2-4.4 deg, p90 6-16 deg (the in-corner drift the ramp spreads over the segment). Refit: rear curve shape changes radically (rear D 9.5 -> 20 kN on v3, peak vanishes on Paul Ricard), near-zero slope far steeper.
- S4w_0.025 (slower washout): M1 worse (-22 to -3 %), M3 degraded on US-v2 / JST 29, straight-line beta larger.
- S4w_0.1 (faster washout): M1 shrink front 33-41 %, rear 5-7 %; M3 improves on all three (0.236 / 0.343 / 0.355).
- S4l_1 / S4l_4 (alpha/Fy low-pass 1 / 4 Hz): M1 within +-5 %, M3 identical (beta is untouched) -- the 2 Hz cutoff is not where the bands come from.
RENDER INSPECTION (assistant, before escalation; the author rules): S0 traces show slow +-2 deg beta ramps along straights (the washout's response to drift), the author's "unphysical" impression located. S2 removes the near-zero-alpha +-10-15 kN bands, moving those samples to |alpha| 1-3 deg, but adds a NEW dense near-vertical streak through the origin from about -10 to +6 kN inside the bin -- turn-in and exit samples with beta forced to 0, alpha pure steer/yaw geometry (the named gated-kinematic turn-in mechanism). The -7 to -9 deg spike near 5300 m on v3 is present in S0 too (not new). S4w_0.1: clouds show no new artefact; on JST 29 the rear +-10-12 kN bands are fully intact; its beta trace shows the mid-corner ripple more clearly, which is S0's own ripple with less low-frequency content on top.

On corner-bracket samples only (M1c): S2/S3 front 29-60 %, rear 27-34 % (the band removal is partly REAL); S4w_0.1 front 15-24 %, rear -0 to 6 % (mostly dilution); S1 and S4l ~0.

GATE (pre-registered, as computed): numeric legs PASS only for S4w_0.1 (M1 met 3/3, M3 not degraded 3/3); render leg passed -> PROMISING -> escalated. S2/S3 FAIL (M3 degraded 2/3 and the new origin streak). Under the post-hoc read S3a/S3b would pass numerically (S2 2/3), the render leg still fails; S4w_0.1 would fail M1c. Not escalated beyond the gate; the author rules.
ALL-18 (S0 + S4w_0.1, pool serial 221): M1 met on 6 of 18 (US-v2, v3, JST 29, o005, o020, o053); M3 not degraded on 17 of 17 assessable (nbr_o019_jst one analysis lap, M3 not assessable), S4w_0.1 M3 lower on all 17; M1c front 7-24 %, rear 0-6 % (o019: -12 / -6 %); all refits converge; rear curve RMS 13-32 % of D (visited range), front 8-17 %, dD outliers front +135 % (o059), +63 % (v3) on the B-C-D-E ridge.
SUPERVISOR QUESTION -- corner-switched integration (author input 2026-10-02, received AFTER the Tier-1 run, during the downstream escalation; recorded as received). The supervisor was surprised that corner-gated filter switching "did not work". Scope line: the clean version had never been tested before this sweep. (1) Gated-kinematic diagnostic (2026-09-29): |ay|-Otsu gate, hard reset, NO endpoint closure, scored on since-retired / banned criteria (CS bars, EKF sign agreement) -- a non-transferring negative. (2) PREMISE CORRECTION from the record ("(b) Part 1"): the (b) filters D1/E were NOT corner-gated; D1 low-passed the EKF beta at 1 Hz over the whole lap before alpha, E = C + D1. They failed on trace evidence under the old criteria, so (b) carries no evidence on corner switching. S2/S3 here are the clean implementation of the idea: free in-corner integration, beta = 0 anchors on straights, endpoint detrend. THEIR RESULT IS THE DIRECT ANSWER for the next supervisor meeting: the construction does move the near-zero-alpha force bands out of the bin (corner-only M1c front 29-60 %, rear 27-34 %, i.e. not only dilution). The cost is a new artefact at segment entry/exit: beta pinned to 0 makes alpha pure steer/yaw geometry, giving a near-vertical streak through the origin. Closing errors are large (median 1.2-4.4 deg, p90 6-16 deg) and get spread linearly across the corner. The refitted rear curve changes radically (no peak on Paul Ricard, far steeper near zero). It failed the pre-registered gate (M3 bound, itself biased low; render leg). The answer is "partly works, at a visible construction cost", not "does not work". Whether that cost is acceptable is the author's ruling on the renders.
DOWNSTREAM (escalated S4w_0.1 + fresh S0, Tier 1; production fit -> EKF -> gate -> CS; the chain was stopped once by the 30-min background limit after v3 and resumed for US-v2 / JST 29, nothing re-scored). Fresh S0 reproduces the recorded gate health (v3 0.098474, US-v2 0.093307). All six: gate PASS, no fallback. Health S0 -> S4w_0.1: v3 0.0985 -> 0.1074, US-v2 0.0933 -> 0.1094, JST 29 0.1155 -> 0.1082. Fitted B rises steeply under S4w_0.1 (rear 8.4 -> 24.0, 7.1 -> 25.5, 10.6 -> 16.4; v3 front lands at B 22.8, C 0.46, E -14.2 -- the ridge). CS renders (assistant read, the author rules): deepest front excursions shallower (v3 -2.0 -> -1.2, US-v2 -2.0 -> -1.3, JST 29 apex -2.7 -> -1.8), one new deeper front spike on JST 29 (-2.4 near 1750 m), visibly more NaN gaps in corner brackets (v3, JST 29 rear) -- partly the (b)-D1 signal-suppression route; corner-by-corner pattern unchanged, no new artefact class.
M3 BOUND DEFECT, confirmed by construction: S4l_1 / S4l_4 leave beta bit-for-bit unchanged yet read "M3 degraded" on JST 29 under the pre-registered bound (S0 itself above it).
SYNTHESIS (characterisation, no proposal; author rules): (1) Bias-first (S1) is inert under the washout, as predicted -- the measured offsets do not matter to the seed in this construction. (2) The bands are not set by the 2 Hz alpha/Fy low-pass (S4l inert). (3) Only constructions that pull beta toward zero move the bands: S2/S3 genuinely (corner-only M1c 27-60 %) at the cost of a turn-in/exit streak and large spread closing errors; S4w_0.1 mostly by diluting the bin with straights (M1c rear 0-6 %), with calmer CS traces and lower coverage. None removes the bands without imposing beta ~ 0 where beta is unknown -- consistent with the observability wall: seed construction relocates the seed error, it does not supply the missing information.
CLOSE-OUT RULINGS (author, 2026-10-02): Q-SEED CLOSED, nothing ships. S2/S3: no all-18 escalation, closed as characterised (entry/exit streak, closing errors spreading in-corner, collapsed rear refit; M1 gain substantially dilution per the post-hoc read). S4w_0.1: "marginal, mostly dilution, no adoption". The SYNTHESIS above stands as the finding, and the supervisor answer stands as written (clean corner switching partly works, at a visible construction cost). Record note (session): the ruling's cost list also names the v3 ~5300 m -8 deg spike; per the render inspection above that spike is present in S0 too, so it is not an S2 cost -- raised with the author; the closure does not rest on it. That framing is WITHDRAWN. The recurring deep dips are POSITION-LOCKED PHENOMENA OF UNPROVEN MAGNITUDE: the kerb arc eliminated four mechanisms but never proved the depths physical, and relaxation-length physics argues the depths are suspect (a force-built ratio cannot swing from the limit to three times the limit within metres). The FINDING is: fixed levers cannot separate noise from position-locked structure -- every lever that removes the non-recurring dips also flattens the recurring ones, and the one that keeps the recurring ones removes nothing. It is NOT a finding that the dips are real physics, and the dips are not quality anchors or evidence for or against any method. Read "known-real site" in the paragraph above as "position-locked site", "erases" as "flattens". The conflict between the report's framing and the author's same-period position was resolved in the report's favour at the time -- the process breach that rule 2b.4 now closes. ## Q-CHAIR-AUDIT: chair pipeline audit + CS foundation [2026-10-03, branch new-laps, read-only; written per part as the run proceeds]

WORK ORDER: PLAN.md PHASE 1 PLAN Q-CHAIR-AUDIT (author), governed by section 2b (GOVERNING FRAME), rulings 1-6 and EXECUTE. SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_chair_audit.py (rules frozen in its header before any run). Outputs diagnostics/plots/chair_audit/. Tier 1 = PR US-v2, v3, NBR JST 29. Framing per 2b: position-locked dips are of unproven magnitude; "vs production" numbers track change only.
PART A -- CHAIR PIPELINE AUDIT (reading only; enlarged copy of the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal) incl. its README and four new tool scripts; the earlier "no gap" expectation set aside, everything re-read).
- PIPELINE ORDER (README): read -> parser config (names, units) -> resample / interpolate to a uniform rate (data_handler: 100 Hz common time vector, time interpolation) -> DataFile.calc_signals() -> smoothing per filter_config (moving averages written as separate *_smoothed columns) -> lap slicing -> write. The pipeline driver (main.py) and config/filter_config.csv are NOT in the copy: the filter_config window lengths and the call position of the CS step relative to smoothing are not determinable from the reference.
- calc_signals(), line by line, the steps that feed CS: (1) vy from vx and beta only if vy is absent (vy is a logged channel on the chair's real car -- a measured lateral-velocity / sideslip state); (2) v, beta = atan2(vy, vx) if absent; (3) radius and curvature from v, a_y, beta; curvature_smoothed = 30-sample centred rolling mean -- used only for signs and derived metrics (alpha_diff, excess steer, yaw-rate comparisons), NOT by CS; (4) per-wheel slip angles from UNSMOOTHED vx, vy, yaw rate, steering (calc_slip_angles_vectorized), axle means alpha_f / alpha_r; (5) yaw_accel_radps2 = np.gradient(UNSMOOTHED yaw rate, median dt) -- DIFFERENTIATE FIRST; (6) Fy by the 2-DOF balance (static weight split + I_z yaw_accel / L) ONLY if no Fy channel exists; (7) quasi-static Fz model, efficiencies, weighted slip angles (alpha_f_weighted = Fz-weighted wheel mean) -- not CS inputs. calc_instantaneous_cornering_stiffness() is a separate method consuming alpha_f_rad, alpha_r_rad, fy_f_N, fy_r_N by name (unsmoothed columns); the estimator low-passes alpha and Fy itself (Butterworth order 4, 2 Hz, filtfilt) -- FILTER SECOND.
- SIMULATOR PATH (ACC shared-memory input): slip angles and axle lateral forces are read from simulator truth channels (physics.slip_angle_*, physics.wheel_tire_force_y_*); step (6) is skipped, so on simulator data no psi_dd term ever enters CS.
- TYRE-CURVE TOOLS (new files): tire_slip_observer_pajecejka_fit.py fits the Magic Formula on alpha_f_weighted_rad_SMOOTHED vs fy_f_N_SMOOTHED (filter_config moving averages), Fz-weighted slip angle, in FOUR SPEED BANDS with overlapping speed-proximity weights; slip_analyzer.py and tire_slip_observer_tuning_helper.py plot / peak-pick on the same smoothed columns. calc_metrics.py is a commented-out legacy metric set; cs_ratio_tire_obersver_tuning_helper.py is empty.
- COMPARISON PER SIGNAL (ours vs chair real-log path): slip source -- chair: measured vy (sensor state) + raw yaw rate + steering, unsmoothed; ours: EKF beta (estimated) + raw yaw rate + steering, unsmoothed -> SAME conditioning, DIFFERENT SOURCE (the recorded forced adaptation). Fy -- both: 2-DOF balance on raw a_y and raw-gradient psi_dd, static split, then 2 Hz order-4 zero-phase inside the CS step -> IDENTICAL order and filter. psi_dd term -- both differentiate then filter (raw gradient, no pre-smoothing) -> IDENTICAL. CS window inputs -- both the 2 Hz-filtered alpha / Fy -> IDENTICAL. Tyre-curve fit -- chair: smoothed (filter_config) inputs, Fz-weighted slip angle, speed-banded weighted fits; ours: 2 Hz chain inputs, axle-mean slip angle, one fit per session -> DIFFERENT.
- VERDICT: CS conditioning gap: NO -- the CS path (slip angle and Fy conditioning, psi_dd order, estimator filter) is lineage-identical to the chair's real-log path; the only CS-relevant difference is the slip SOURCE (measured vy vs EKF beta). Tyre-curve fitting conditioning gap: PARTIAL -- the chair fits its curve on additionally smoothed, load-weighted, speed-banded data; ours does not. Scope: filter_config contents unknown (moving-average lengths), so the size of the chair's extra smoothing cannot be reproduced exactly.
- LINEAGE-FAITHFUL SHORTLIST FOR Q-CAL: (1) keep the CS conditioning as is (it is the chair's); (2) chair-precedented options for the TYRE FIT, not the CS: speed-banded fits (chair: four bands, overlapping weights -- consistent with Q-STIFF-CS's speed-dependent K), Fz-weighted slip angle (needs per-wheel loads: Level 4 on Paul Ricard only), fitting on smoothed inputs (window lengths = a chair question, filter_config not in the copy); (3) the chair has NO grading, adaptive window or spike handling -- those are author constructions (governing frame 2b.3), not lineage.
PART B -- PHYSICS GROUNDS: B1 relaxation length WITHDRAWN as a filtering ground (ruling 1; Rajamani sec. 13.11 Eqs. 13.86-13.88: Fy bandwidth V / (2 pi sigma), no sourced sigma in the available references, of order 10-20 Hz at racing speed for any sub-metre sigma -- above the chain's 2 Hz, so the chain already honours it). Replaced by the CURVE-SHAPE BOUND (Part D4-new). B2 Segers sec. 2.6: filtering is standard practice but "use filtering as little as possible"; sec. 3: differentiation is itself filtering; p. 71: moving-average split of low / high-speed suspension movement. HONESTY NOTE (ruling 6): Segers bounds the constitution's "filter heavier" -- heavier WHERE grounded (grading, adaptive windows), never blanket; supervisor rule and Segers agree on precision over recall, not on indiscriminate smoothing. Load-cell jitter at standstill: author operational knowledge (practice tier).
PART E -- 4 s WELCH ROW (labelled POST-HOC; Q-STIFF-CS Part 1b rerun with 4 s windows, 0.25 Hz resolution, every other rule unchanged; outputs partE_welch4s_<key>.json, partE_welch4s_bode_<key>.png). The fits now run (5-10 coherent points per band). 1. DEFINITIONS (quantity -> formula -> inputs; per wheel unless stated; v_min = 3 m/s gates apply):
- whl_slip_* (longitudinal slip ratio) -> (a) from wheel angular speed via the external vehicle_handler (calc_long_slip_vectorized: vx, vy, yaw rate, steering, wheel speed) or (b) (v_wheel_over_ground - vx) / vx, clipped to [-1, 1].
- whl_slip_combined_* -> sqrt( tan(whl_slip)^2 + alpha^2 ) -> slip ratio and slip angle: a SLIP-based Euclidean norm (as written the tan acts on the slip RATIO, not on alpha -- recorded as found, not interpreted).
- long_slip_velocity_* -> whl_slip x v_mps; lat_slip_velocity_* -> v_mps x tan(alpha); combined_slip_velocity_* -> whl_slip_combined x v_mps (velocity form of the combined slip, NOT the vector norm of the two slip velocities).
- fz_* -> quasi-static model (static split + aero -0.5 rho v^2 A Cl distributed by CoP + longitudinal transfer m a_x h / L + lateral transfer m a_y h / track); fy_*_norm_N -> axle Fy / axle Fz.
- mue_effective (VEHICLE level) -> m x a_total / (Fz_f + Fz_r), a_total = sqrt(a_x^2 + a_y^2) -> measured accelerations and the quasi-static loads (aero included): the utilised friction coefficient of the whole car, combined (longitudinal + lateral), referenced to the modelled total vertical load.
- alpha_*_weighted -> Fz-weighted mean of the left / right wheel slip angles; whl_slip_weighted_* the same for slip ratio.
- lateral_slip_efficiency_front / _rear -> Fy_axle / alpha_axle_weighted (0 where |alpha_weighted| < 0.01 rad) -> a SECANT cornering stiffness (N/rad), force per slip; _vehicle -> Fz-weighted mean of front and rear where both are non-zero; lateral_slip_efficiency_norm_* -> the same divided by Fz (1/rad), README / code comment "lateral mue efficiency".
- wheel_slip_efficiency_* -> Fy_axle / whl_slip_weighted (LATERAL force over LONGITUDINAL slip ratio -- recorded as found).
2. CONSUMERS: only whl_slip_weighted_front / _rear are consumed downstream (calc_instantaneous_longitudinal_stiffness -> the longitudinal-stiffness / LS-ratio estimator). Every other quantity above is COMPUTED AND EXPORTED only (unified CSV, PlotJuggler viewing); slip_analyzer.py carries lat_slip_velocity_fl_smoothed and mue_effective_smoothed as commented-out plot alternatives. NOTHING verdict-like reads them; no metric, threshold or KPI in the copy uses them (kpi_report / plotting_methods / corner_characterisation: none).
3. RELATION TO (e) -- SURFACED (rule 2b.4), not resolved: the order's condition was "is lateral_slip_efficiency a chair version of combined utilisation / occupancy". It is NOT: it is a secant stiffness (Fy / alpha), slip-side, not a demand / capability ratio. The chair quantity that IS the precedent is mue_effective: demand-side, combined (sqrt(a_x^2 + a_y^2)), normalised by vertical load -- the vehicle-level form of (e)'s rear-axle mu_used,r = sqrt(Fx_r^2 + Fy_r^2) / Fz_r (K&N Eq. 8.22, RCVD 2.7), which (e) then reads against the session's empirical envelope (RCVD 9.3 / 9.4). Proposed lineage wording, pending the author: "chair-PRECEDENTED CONCEPT (vehicle-level mue_effective = m a_total / sum Fz), our adaptation: per AXLE (rear, unsteered, rotation-invariant), measured / session-corrected Fz, and normalised to an empirical envelope (friction-circle occupancy)" -- stronger than "extension into a chair gap", but via mue_effective, not via lateral_slip_efficiency. Note: the chair computes but never consumes mue_effective (display only).
4. FILTERING CLOSURE: every quantity above appears in filter_config.csv with a 0.15 s centred moving average (written as a separate *_smoothed column; the raw columns stay unsmoothed). parser_config.csv is still 0 bytes; by the README it maps raw log channel names to the unified names and applies unit conversions per log format -- none of the formulas above depends on it (they act on the unified names; units would change absolute values, not definitions).
SUMMARY (thesis-citable): the chair's combined-slip family is a set of per-wheel and per-axle KINEMATIC and FORCE-PER-SLIP quantities -- slip ratio, a slip-norm combined slip and its velocity forms, Fz-weighted axle slip, secant cornering stiffness ("lateral slip efficiency") raw and load-normalised -- plus ONE demand-side utilisation, mue_effective = m a_total / sum Fz at vehicle level. All are computed from unsmoothed inputs in calc_signals(), exported with 0.15 s moving-average copies, and consumed nowhere except the Fz-weighted wheel slip, which feeds the longitudinal-stiffness estimator. Fast-dynamics signals (all slips, forces, accelerations, yaw rate) share the 0.15 s smoothing; slow quantities 0.3-3.0 s; the CS and LS estimators apply their own Butterworth filters (2 Hz and 8 Hz, order 4, zero-phase) to unsmoothed inputs.

- VERDICTS AS COMPUTED (22 sites): B 6, C+B 9, C 3, A+B 1, A 1, C+A+B 1, unexplained 1 (v3 front 747 m, lag +150 ms, no B, small gap). Flag totals: B 17, C 13, A 3.

DataFile.resample_and_interpolate (data_handler ~2286) linearly interpolates every column onto a uniform 100 Hz grid, with one optional global time offset for the whole frame. RECORD: the chair applies uniform resampling (grid alignment) and NO sensor-latency correction -- the lineage-gap hypothesis on timing is CLOSED (no gap; neither pipeline corrects latency). C stays "not shown, not chair-practised". The stray smoothing_window = 40 constant is defined and never used -- noted, not a setting. ## Q-RECOVER-2: NBR wheel loads recovered on all four corners through the raw-voltage reference [2026-10-03, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: PLAN.md PHASE 1 PLAN Q-RECOVER-2 (author RE-ORDER + EXECUTE with R3 IN, 2026-10-03). SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_recover_rr.py (rules frozen in header before compute; [impl] notes and one pre-compute amendment dated in it). Outputs diagnostics/plots/recover_rr/: recover.json, voltage_reference.png, gap_correction.png, drift_patterns.png, run.txt, run_render.txt. Tier B throughout (calibration offset of a logged sensor, standard statics); no Tier A method involved.
- METHOD (R3, the main event): the NBR processed gauge equals gain x V + offset_NBR, the Paul Ricard gauge of the SAME car (serial 221) gain x V + offset_PR, both maps fitted in Q-CHANNEL-INVENTORY. The NBR gauge offset is therefore K_V = offset_NBR - offset_PR, per file and corner (PR FR including production's existing channel correction); one constant per corner = the median over the 16 files. It is pinned to a reference (the same car's other event), not fitted to the NBR config target. Uncertainty u_V = sqrt((MR_s x sqrt(SD_f(K_V)^2 + e_PR^2))^2 + 98^2), e_PR = how far PR's own standing loads sit from config.
- RESULT R3: offsets FL 58.64, FR 59.47, RL 58.42, RR 58.91 kN (gauge units); file-to-file SD only 45 / 46 / 95 / 76 gauge-N -- the zero entry is CONSTANT across all 16 NBR outings. u_V FL 177, FR 332, RL 389, RR 140 N (102-123 N without the config-referenced e_PR term). V1 (min p0.1 -198 FL -- marginal, 2 N inside the -200 N floor; -116 FR, +52 RL, +682 RR), V2 (min |r| 0.854-0.886), V3 (min b 1.40), V4 (max 576 / 394 / 335 / 475 N) pass on all 16 files. EXIT: ALL FOUR CORNERS RECOVERED VIA REFERENCE.
- R1 (RR cross-check, leave-one-out): with one characterised standing-rolling correction per corner (FL +298, FR +269, RL -171, RR -602 N) every corner is RECOVERED WITH CORRECTION (LOO max 611 / 444 / 416 / 526 N, u_stand 237-298 N); RR in both variants (LOO max 526 / 482 N). - T3(a) PR ZERO vs config: PR standing loads sit -125..-415 N from config on FL / FR / RL and -107 / +40 N on RR -- valid on all corners (within 700 N); consistent with rule 0 (config is a guideline).
- T3(b) WHICH OFFSET THE VOLTAGE PATH MATCHES: FL, RL, RR match the AT-REST offsets (median +23, -78, +37 N) rather than the rolling fit (+359, -204, -563 N); FR matches the rolling fit slightly better (-185 vs +108 N; FR's PR reference rests on the 2026-09-18 axle-mate correction). - T3(c) CONFIG CHECK: voltage-path standing loads vs config median -2.4 / +18.9 / +8.0 / -3.8 kg (FL / FR / RL / RR), max per file 626 / 386 / 285 / 473 N -> CONFIG CONSISTENT at rest (within the guideline uncertainty of rule 0).

The rolling fit that carried the RR gap and the drift is the DIAGNOSTIC estimator of Q-SHARED-OFFSET (diagnostics/inspect_shared_offset.py: shared aero term per corner, config target), never production. The ~0.6 kN RR standing-vs-rolling gap and the season drift of the rolling offset are a LIMITATION of the diagnostic rolling estimator of Q-SHARED-OFFSET (diagnostics/inspect_shared_offset.py: one shared aero term per corner, offset fitted against the config target on > 60 km/h straights). The voltage reference (Q-RECOVER-2) does not show them: its per-corner offset is flat over the 16 NBR outings (SD 45-95 gauge-N) and matches the at-rest offsets on FL / RL / RR. No production code has a rolling offset fit (modules/wheel_loads.py reads a fixed config offset), so there is no production defect and no production-consequence line. Thesis use: (1) methods evidence for the voltage path -- a reference-pinned offset avoids the confounding a target-referenced rolling fit picks up (unmodelled per-outing weight, aero split); (2) estimator-limits content -- a fit that absorbs offset into its own model terms can produce an apparent sensor symptom (gap, drift) that the sensor does not have. No fix owed; recorded in PLAN.md BACKLOG -- PERMANENT as a methods limitation.

## Q-CAL-1 measurement: kerb strikes leak past the mask edge through the 2 Hz filter [2026-10-03, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: PLAN.md Q-CAL item 1 (kerb-mask edge fix), re-scoped by the author 2026-10-03 to the FILTER-SMEAR path; raw-envelope mask extensions (options 1 / 2) stay closed per "Kerb-detection variant rulings" (2026-10-01). Tier B preprocessing measurement, no anchor claimed. SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py (rules frozen in its header before the first run; entry check amended once after the smoke run, rounding only, author ruling). Outputs diagnostics/plots/kerb_filter_decay/.
PREMISE (from the code): production low-passes Fy and alpha (2 Hz, 4th-order Butterworth, zero-phase filtfilt; chair-identical lineage) over the whole series WITH the strike samples, and applies the kerb mask afterwards as an endpoint exclusion only (estimate_cornering_stiffness; the window [start, i) still holds masked samples). The filter alone spreads one sample over +/-0.19 s at 20 % of peak and +/-0.40 s at 10 % (impulse response at 100 Hz). The 2026-10-01 variants measured only RAW ay / yaw envelopes (p75 80-100 ms); the filtered force path that CS regresses was never measured. Side finding: kerb_dilation_samples = 5 is a sample count calibrated as 100 ms on the old 50 Hz grid and runs as +/-50 ms on the 100 Hz grid (known limit in the config's grid-rate comment, never repaired).
METHOD: event = production-mask run touching a moving analysis-lap sample. Smear d = filt(x_raw) - filt(x_raw with every mask run bridged by a straight line between its neighbouring samples), x in Fy_f, Fy_r, alpha_f, alpha_r. Noise band = p95 of |d| 0-1 s beyond the edges of null-control pseudo-runs (same length, random in-corner positions >= 2 s from any mask sample, seed 20261003). Decay = connected exceedances of the band past the mask edge (0.10 s gap bridge for the filter's ringing), stopped at the next mask run (censored) or 1.5 s; pre side mirrored. Entry check: cached production CS reproduced, identical finite set, max |diff| <= 1e-6.
SESSIONS: 15 of 16 NBR (nbr_o020_jst stopped at the entry check, see below) + Paul Ricard pr_us_v2 and v3.
RESULTS (uncensored events; p50 / p75 / p90):
- Fy_filt, NBR (1,422 events): front 140 / 270 / 360 ms (6 / 9 / 15 m), rear 140 / 235 / 360 ms (6 / 9 / 14 m); pre side about the same (140 / 205-300 / 360-370 ms). Null control 30 / 90 / 130 ms. Share of events with any post-edge smear 0.79-0.98 per session vs 0.48-0.64 null.
- Fy_filt, Paul Ricard (391 events): front 150 / 338 / 370 ms, rear 150 / 320 / 380 ms (7 / 11 / 16 m).
- alpha_filt, NBR: front 90 / 160 / 340 ms, rear 90 / 170 / 360 ms; Paul Ricard 40-70 / 130 / 216-289 ms; null 0 / 80-90 / 140 ms. Alpha smears less than Fy -- consistent with Q-PAIRING (the strike disturbs the force path more than the slip path).
- No material front / rear difference in Fy: one shared mask is consistent with the force data (the axle split is a fixed fraction).
- p90 sits at 340-390 ms in nearly every session: the tail is set by the filter's own reach.
- CS windows touched (zone = that axle's Fy or alpha zone, pre or post): NBR in-corner, windows holding a zone sample 13.5 % front / 15.0 % rear vs 7.7 / 8.9 % holding a masked sample; endpoint inside a zone 7.9 / 8.6 %. Paul Ricard in-corner 20.1 / 20.9 % vs 9.7 / 10.4 %; endpoint 13.0 / 13.0 %. Per session in-corner zone share 6-7 % (o010) to 24-28 % (v3, o019).
CAVEATS (stated with the result, author rulings 1 and 2):
- CENSORING: ~40 % of events (NBR Fy 575 / 579 of 1,422) reach the next mask run while the smear is still active -- kerb sites are runs in a row. The percentiles above are over uncensored events and are LOWER BOUNDS of the true spread; no merge of consecutive runs (ruled).
- ANCHOR ARTEFACT: the line bridge is anchored on the first unmasked raw sample each side, itself often still strike-disturbed. On hard strikes the bridged counterfactual is then the wrong one, so the measured tail values are UPPER BOUNDS (ruled: no anchor sensitivity re-run). Both worst-case exhibits (Paul Ricard pr_us_v2 lap 48, mask end 4181 m) show it: production Fy stays smooth near -9 / -12 kN while the bridged version swings to 0 kN.
OPTION 3 EVIDENCE AND REJECTION (author ruling 4): "remove the strike before the filter" (bridge or NaN-fill the masked samples, then filter) is exactly the counterfactual this measurement builds. Its worst-case output INVENTS force through the strike (swing to 0 kN where production stays smooth), i.e. it replaces a bounded, filter-limited smear with a fabricated force excursion anchored on disturbed edge samples. REJECTED. Shipping next package: option 4 (grade near-strike CS windows, no deletion, no coverage loss) + option 0 (dilation unit repair, kerb_dilation_s = 0.10 replacing the sample count; neutral engineering).
SPIKE COINCIDENCE (author ruling 5; read-only from decay_records.json + the cached production CS, `coincidence` mode; NBR pooled, 15 files, in-corner CS on analysis laps). Cutoffs CS < 0 (impossible on a monotone tyre curve) and CS < -1 (deep tail).
- Endpoint inside a smear zone: base rate 7.9 % front / 8.6 % rear; CS < 0 10.4 / 9.8 % (x1.3 / x1.1); CS < -1 18.0 / 26.8 % (x2.3 / x3.1; n 3,880 / 564).
- Endpoint within X ms of a mask sample, deep tail vs base, front: 140 ms 11.9 vs 5.2 %, 250 ms 18.7 vs 8.2 %, 360 ms 23.1 vs 10.8 %, 400 ms 24.2 vs 11.7 %. Rear: 140 ms 19.0 vs 5.5 %, 250 ms 26.2 vs 8.7 %, 360 ms 28.5 vs 11.5 %, 400 ms 28.5 vs 12.5 %.
- Marginal enrichment per band (deep-tail gain / base gain): front 0-140 ms x2.3, 140-250 ms x2.3, 250-360 ms x1.7; rear 0-140 ms x3.5, 140-250 ms x2.3, 250-360 ms x0.8 (no enrichment). The coincidence is collected by ~250 ms (Fy p75) on the rear; the front gains a weaker extra 4.4 points to 360 ms.
- Zone vs mask contribution (window contents BOUNDED only -- production alpha is not cached, so windows are bounded by the 0.1 s minimum window below and the 53 m cap above): minimum window, deep tail, holds zone only 16.0 / 16.7 %, mask only 0.6 / 1.2 %, both 4.4 / 9.0 % (front / rear); base rate zone only 6.9 / 7.4 %. Near the endpoint the smear zone, not the mask, carries the coincidence. The 53 m upper bound is uninformative (almost every window near a kerb reaches the mask: "both" 22-25 %).
- READING: the smear zone is a real but MINOR contributor to negative CS: 73-82 % of the deep tail and ~90 % of CS < 0 lie outside every zone. Grading catches the strike-related part only; most negative CS has other causes (apex physics / short windows, see "Kerb-edge association: closed as characterised").
nbr_o020_jst REAR ENTRY FAILURE (author ruling 3, one probe, nothing fixed): one single sample of 39,546 differs (t = 987.16 s, s = 1721 m; CS 0.4920 recomputed vs 0.4974 cached, 1.1 %); all other samples match to <= 1e-6, Fy_filt identical, time base identical. Not a stale cache (would differ widely) and not denominator amplification (linear reference 224 kN/rad, 71st percentile of |ref|). Third reading, not verified further (timebox): a discrete decision flip at one sample (window growth / span floor or monotonic-section boundary) from the float32-rounded cached beta. The session stays out of the pool (frozen rule); impact nil.
RULINGS ON Q-CAL-1 OPEN 1-3 (author, 2026-10-03): (1) grade-zone width kerb_smear_grade_s = 0.25 s (Fy p75), one value, both axles; derived_from = the coincidence count above (rear enrichment ends ~250 ms; the front 250-360 ms band adds only x1.7). Enters config with the options 4 + 0 package. (2) Acceptance of BACKLOG item 1 confirmed: "CS windows inside the smear zone carry a grade mark". (3) diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py kept (reproduces; derives the grade width).
RULING 4 (author, 2026-10-03), RECEIVED: reconcile with frame 2b rule 1 (position-locked dips = characterised-real, unproven magnitude, protected), do not duplicate it. Recorded as binding on the next package: the grade mark flags smear proximity ONLY and must not erase or down-rank the position-locked sites. HELD (premise conflict surfaced per frame rule 2b.4, session): the ruling's statement that the position-locked sites lie outside any smear zone is not shown by this count (it never separated those sites) and conflicts with Q-PAIRING ruling 1 (strike disturbance of the force path, B, at 17 of 22 sites; 621 m exhibit window straddles the mask edge). SITE CHECK (author ruling option (b), EXECUTE 2026-10-03; records only, diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py mode sites; output site_check.txt). Do the 22 position-locked dip sites (Q-PAIRING, Tier 1) lie inside the 0.25 s grade zone? Dip sample per site and lap rebuilt by Q-PAIRING's own rule on the cached production CS (entry: matches the recorded per-lap CS to 1.0e-7 on all 134 site-laps). ## Q-CAL-3 premise check: chair fit-conditioning maps onto one element [2026-10-03, branch new-laps, read-only]

FINDINGS (from the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal), read-only, and our code):
- The chair's 0.15 s centred moving average is written to separate *_smoothed columns of the whole fast-dynamics family and feeds ONLY its tyre-curve fitting / plotting tools. Its cornering-stiffness step consumes the unsmoothed slip angle and axle force and applies its own 2 Hz order-4 zero-phase Butterworth -- our CS path exactly (ruled lineage-identical, Q-CHAIR-AUDIT).
- The chair's speed-banded fit: four reference speeds evenly spaced 18-44 m/s, per-band weight clip(1 - k (v - v_ref)^2, 0, 1) with the weight reaching zero 9.1 m/s from the reference (band spacing + 5 % overlap), samples with weight > 0.05, weighted least squares of the reduced Magic Formula on folded (|alpha|, |Fy|) front-axle data pooled over files; the four curves are plotted and annotated -- nothing downstream consumes them.
- There is no understeer-gradient constraint anywhere in the chair reference.
- Our tyre fit (tyre_fit_auto) fits one curve per axle per session on the kinematic-seed slip angle and axle Fy through the 2 Hz chain low-pass, signed, both axles; that curve is the EKF Pacejka observer's tyre model, so it feeds beta, the slip angles and CS.
RULINGS (author, 2026-10-03):
1. SPEED BANDS -- NOT TRANSPLANTABLE. The chair's banded curves are a display product; our fit is an observer input taking one curve per axle. Adopting bands would be a Tier A tyre-model change with no consumer need, and Q-CHAIR-AUDIT Part F(d) documented their degeneration on our population (step-shaped curves from the near-zero-slip band of the kinematic seed). One curve per axle stands.
2. K2-CONSTRAINED VARIANT -- re-filed as an author construction anchored on Rajamani ch. 3 (the steady-state cornering relation used by Q-PUSH P1), not chair conditioning. Calibration pass authorised later in Q-CAL-3: three Tier-1 sessions, diagnostic K2 (+1.27 to +1.41 deg/g), labelled variant beside the unconstrained fit. Production decision deferred to Q-K2 (production K2 readout). No verdict against the concept from the calibration pass alone (concept-vs-instance rule).
3. 0.15 s MOVING AVERAGE -- the single chair conditioning element to pursue. Chair-exact mechanism: the moving average on the RAW slip angle and Fy REPLACES the 2 Hz-filtered inputs of the tyre fit only; the CS path stays untouched. A calibration pass is REQUIRED before any production proposal and is judged on outcomes (fit quality, beta, CS cleanliness), not on chair-conformity alone. ASYMMETRY (recorded): the chair's fit feeds plots, ours feeds an observer -- conformity alone cannot justify the change. The pass also reports the fit's strike sensitivity under both conditionings: the moving average has finite support (+/-75 ms) where the 2 Hz filtfilt reaches about +/-400 ms, but its sidelobes pass 10-22 % up to about 12 Hz, so the Q-CAL-1 smear numbers (measured for the 2 Hz filtfilt) do not describe moving-average fit inputs. The CS smear zones and the near_strike mark are unaffected (CS conditioning unchanged; the tyre fit does not read the mark).
4. Full pytest suite before any code change (owed boundary).

P = production (2 Hz Butterworth fit inputs); M = chair-exact centred 0.15 s moving average on the raw slip angle and raw Fy, tyre fit only; everything else identical. Tier 1: Paul Ricard US-v2, v3, Nurburgring JST 29. Stated before the run: the M3 tie rule uses a two-sided bootstrap band from P's 2.5 / 97.5 % edges; the entry reference is a direct production call made now (the cached CS predates Q-CAL-1's mask change).
ENTRY: the harness reproduces the direct production call exactly on all three sessions (beta and CS max diff 0.0). The MA fitter was called once per axle on every session.
RESULTS (P -> M)
- Fit: the curves barely move -- B, C, D within about 1 %, E by up to 0.29 (JST 29 front -5.31 -> -5.61); F2 (residual vs the 2 Hz view) changes by under 0.15 N in every cell. F1 curve stability: median change +2.4 % (worse, within noise).
- Beta: gate passes for both, no fallback; straight-line |beta| and chatter unchanged to 0.004 deg. M3: US-v2 0.882 -> 0.861, v3 0.870 -> 0.715, JST 29 0.453 -> 0.459 -- all inside P's bootstrap band (v3's band is wide, 0.32-1.19, three laps), so TIES, no credit.
- CS < 0 share (in-corner): US-v2 front 19.23 -> 19.01 %, rear 14.91 -> 14.39 %; v3 front 16.50 -> 18.99 %, rear 17.47 -> 18.01 %; JST 29 front 19.87 -> 20.89 %, rear 9.06 -> 9.21 %. Pooled +1.5 % relative.
- CS < -1 share: US-v2 rear 0.116 -> 0.023 %, JST 29 rear 0.055 -> 0.010 %, JST 29 front 0.885 -> 0.767 %, but v3 rear 0.218 -> 0.479 %; pooled -7.9 % relative (below the -10 % bar).
- Strike sensitivity S: median +20 % (worse, as predicted for the leakier moving average; below the harm bar of 1.5 x).
- Coverage unchanged to within 0.8 point.
VERDICT (pre-registered): HARM -- CS < 0 share rises by >= 0.5 point on v3 front (+2.48), v3 rear (+0.54) and JST 29 front (+1.02). No EARNS candidate met (0 of 5). M REJECTED; production keeps its 2 Hz fit inputs.
READING (labelled; the author rules): (1) the chair's moving average and our 2 Hz chain give nearly the same tyre curve on our data -- the conditioning difference recorded in Q-CHAIR-AUDIT Part F(b) is real in the frequency domain but immaterial to the fit. (2) The CS < 0 share reacts to these tiny curve changes by up to 2.5 points per session -- the share's own sensitivity to small beta changes is of the size of the 0.5-point harm bar, so the harm items are not evidence that the moving average is physically worse; they show that there is nothing to gain. (3) The moving average makes the fit slightly more strike-sensitive, as its sidelobes predicted. Concept-vs-instance: this rejects the chair-exact instance on our observer chain; it says nothing against input conditioning as such.

## Q-CAL-3 K2-constrained calibration pass: balance pinned to the measured understeer gradient -- HARM (informational for Q-K2) [2026-10-03/04, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: overnight package step 2 (author EXECUTE; Q-CAL-3 premise-check ruling 2). Frame = the MA pass frame with ONE amendment (CS < 0 harm bar 2.5 points, the measured sensitivity, replacing 0.5), frozen in the header of diagnostics/inspect_fit_k2_calibration.py before any number. Purpose: informational for Q-K2 -- no production adoption from this pass regardless of outcome. Verdict vocabulary HARM / PROMISING / NEUTRAL.
METHOD (Tier A, author construction, Rajamani ch. 3, steady-state cornering relation): variant K = joint front/rear Pacejka fit on the production inputs (kinematic-seed alpha, 2 Hz Fy, base mask), minimising SSE_front + SSE_rear subject to m_f / (B_f C_f D_f) - m_r / (B_r C_r D_r) = K2 (Q-PUSH P1's diagnostic K2, read from p1_<key>.json: +1.407 / +1.356 / +1.272 deg/g, Level 2; mass and CoG Level 1). Unconstrained, the objective separates into the two production fits, so K differs from P by the constraint alone. B_r eliminated through the constraint, Powell (production optimiser) from P's fit projected onto the constraint.
ENTRY: harness reproduces the direct production call exactly (beta, CS max diff 0.0) on all three sessions; K's fitter called once per axle.
FIT LEVEL: the constrained fit converged on all three sessions, constraint met to 1e-16 -- the pre-registered degeneracy exit did NOT trigger. Balance implied by the production curves now: -0.94 / -0.32 / +0.37 deg/g (Q-PUSH recorded -0.93 / -0.31 / +0.38 before the kerb-mask change). The constraint is met mainly by SOFTENING THE FRONT origin slope (US-v2 153 -> 65, v3 132 -> 81, JST 29 138 -> 108 kN/rad) rather than stiffening the rear (142 -> 122, 157 -> 162, 219 -> 247): the front curve takes an S-kink at the origin, the rear goes nearly linear. US-v2 rear lands at B ~ 0, C ~ 4e6, E ~ -2e13 -- a near-straight line in a pathological Magic-Formula parameterisation (B C D finite and held by the constraint); JST 29 rear C 103. Not caught by the frozen degeneracy rule (B > 0, D > 0, converged), reported here as a labelled observation. Fit cost small: F2 rises by 0-41 N RMS (of 3-7 kN).
CHAIN: gate passes for both on every session, no fallback.
VERDICT (pre-registered): HARM -- coverage -15.8 / -28.3 points (US-v2 front / rear), S 0.006 -> 0.062 and 0.011 -> 0.042 (US-v2 front / rear), CS < 0 +8.57 points (v3 front), M3 above P's band (JST 29, 0.553 > 0.530), coverage -2.9 points (JST 29 front), CS < 0 +3.20 points (JST 29 rear). PROMISING candidates 1 of 5 (pooled CS < 0 -10.8 % rel, driven by US-v2 rear 14.9 -> 3.1 % together with its 28-point coverage loss); F1 median +122 % (worse); M3 credit on US-v2 only (0.88 -> 0.47).
READING (labelled; the author rules): (1) the production fit population (kinematic-seed alpha) cannot carry the measured balance -- imposing it costs little SSE but distorts the curve shape near the origin, which is where CS reads. This is the curve/beta circularity again from the constraint side: the balance information is real (beta-free, Level 2), the alpha it would have to reshape is not. (2) Concept-vs-instance: this rejects pinning K2 onto THIS fit population as an observer input; it says nothing against K2 as a readout (Q-K2 display candidate) or against a balance constraint on a better alpha. (3) Q-K2 input: the per-session K2 stands as the one estimator-free balance number; the tyre fit should not be forced to it.
Figures: diagnostics/plots/fit_k2_calibration/ (fit_<key>.png, beta_<key>.png, metrics.png, summary.txt, results.json, run_log.txt).
