## Q-FIT-CHAIR-DATA: what data enters the chair's tyre fit vs ours [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: author, read-only investigation after the standing ruling (comparability includes what data enters the fit). Source: the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal), read-only; nothing run.
(a) CHAIR CHAIN, raw log to fit call:
1. Lateral velocity comes from a logged source -- the car's state estimator, a GNSS/INS (vy, slip angle) or a Kistler optical speed/angle sensor, per the parser mapping; beta = atan2(vy, vx) only if beta is not logged. Never an integrated kinematic seed.
2. Below 3 m/s longitudinal speed, beta and the per-wheel slip angles are set to zero.
3. Per-wheel slip angles from vx, vy, yaw rate and ONE front steer angle, through a vehicle-handler function outside the reference set (relation not visible).
4. Axle Fy from the 2-DOF balance (static weight fraction + yaw-inertia term) -- the same construction as ours.
5. Per-wheel Fz from a MODEL (static + aero + longitudinal transfer, split left/right by lateral transfer); the axle slip angle for the fit = Fz-weighted mean of left and right. With model loads the weights depend on lateral acceleration only.
6. Centred 0.15 s moving average on the weighted slip angle and on Fy (the caller of the smoothing step is outside the reference set).
7. Lap slicing writes the full log plus per-lap files (first and last sample dropped); the fit reads every file in a folder the user picks -- no programmatic lap-validity, outlap or pit selection.
8. Fit: all files pooled (multi-session), FOLDED to |alpha|, |Fy|, FRONT axle only; four speed bands (reference speeds 18-44 m/s), per-sample weight clip(1 - k (v - v_ref)^2), samples with weight > 0.05 enter a weighted least-squares fit per band -> four curves. The band union is an effective speed window of about 9.1-52.9 m/s; everything outside gets weight zero.
9. No kerb mask, no cornering / steady-state / lateral-dominance selection, no a_x or slip-ratio gate anywhere in the chain.
(b) WHAT IT PRODUCES: not laterally dominant or quasi-steady by construction. Braking and traction samples inside the speed window enter at full weight. Implicit restrictions only: the speed window (drops the slowest and the fastest stretches -- for the chair's car that removes top-speed straights), band weighting (down-weights samples far from a band centre), folding (opposite-sign transient samples land in the first quadrant instead of standing as off-curve residuals), the 0.15 s moving average. The decisive property is not selection but PROVENANCE: the slip angle is built on a measured or estimator lateral velocity.
(c) OURS AGAINST IT, step by step: (1) lateral velocity: REPLACED, forced -- kinematic-seed beta (Level 1), no lateral-velocity sensor on the GT3R; the EKF then refines beta with the fitted curve (the recorded curve/beta circularity). (2) Low-speed cut: REPLACED, moving mask 5 m/s instead of 3. (3)+(5) per-wheel slip with Fz weighting: DROPPED, single-track axle slip angle; with a common steer angle the weighting moves alpha only through the track term (estimate <= ~0.1 deg). (4) Fy split: SAME. (6) Smoothing: REPLACED by the 2 Hz Butterworth; tested -- immaterial to the fit (Q-CAL-3 MA pass). (7) File choice: REPLACED, per-session fit on analysis laps only (per-session fitting experimentally vindicated, (d)). (8) Folding and front-only: DROPPED, signed fit on both axles (the EKF needs both signed curves); speed bands DROPPED (ruled not transplantable), and with them the implicit speed window -- we have no equivalent. (9) Kerb mask: ADDED by us (domain improvement). Our population contains what theirs cannot: kinematic-seed alpha error, the rear axle, signed opposite-sign samples, speeds 5-9 m/s, and every speed above the window (straights at our car's top speed). Theirs contains what ours does not: kerb strikes, possibly out/in laps, other sessions.
(d) MINIMAL CONVERGENCE SKETCH (no code): one selection change is chair-convergent -- a SPEED WINDOW on the fit population (the band union's implicit effect; window values = vehicle parameterisation, derived from our own speed distribution, not transplanted). Everything else either already matches (Fy split), was tested immaterial (smoothing), is forced by our consumer (signed, both axles, one curve) or by our car (no lateral-velocity sensor), or is negligible on our inputs (Fz weighting). A lateral-dominance gate (L) is NOT chair-convergent -- the chair has none; L would be our invention (Tier B). The dominant non-comparability is input provenance (measured vs kinematic-seed lateral velocity), which no data selection can close.

## Q-FIT-CHAIR-DATA (e)-(f): Pacejka physics check of our fit-data situation [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, read-only]

Source: Pacejka, Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics, 2nd ed. (on file 2026-10-04; sections verified on the rendered text, printed page = PDF page - 15).
(e1) PURE-SLIP VALIDITY. Sec. 4.3.1 (Eq. 4.49): the Magic Formula "holds for given values of vertical load and camber angle"; sec. 4.3 introduces it as a model of STEADY-STATE force generation; sec. 1.2.1 defines pure slip as lateral slip in isolation (kappa = 0). Sec. 1.2.2: effective AXLE characteristics (what our per-axle, per-session fit is) absorb steering compliance, roll steer, load transfer and (sec. 1.2 intro) moderate braking / driving, but only for (quasi) steady state -- under yaw / roll transients load transfer is no longer an algebraic function of the axle force. Implication: our pooled axle curve is legitimate as an effective quasi-steady characteristic; transients and large Fx are outside its validity.
(e2) COMBINED SLIP. Sec. 1.2.1 (Fig. 1.2, friction circle): adding the other slip component drops the force, because the total horizontal force cannot exceed the friction-circle radius. Sec. 4.3.1 (Eqs. 4.64-4.69): Fy = G_yk Fy0 + S_Vyk, with a hill-shaped weighting function equal to one at kappa = 0, slightly above one at moderate brake slip, then decaying. Sec. 1.3.4: at moderate braking / driving the influence on Fy is relatively small and may be neglected; longitudinal load transfer then acts through the axle loads. Mechanism of the bias, own words: samples with large Fx carry less Fy at the same slip angle, so in a pure-slip fit they pull the curve down at large alpha (lower peak D, shape E pushed towards early fall-off) and widen the residual band; samples with moderate Fx barely matter. Implication: a longitudinal gate is theory-consistent, and only a loose one is needed (large Fx only).
(e3) LOAD DEPENDENCE. Sec. 1.2.1 (Fig. 1.3, Eq. 1.6): cornering stiffness grows less than proportionally with load (C_Fa = c1 sin(2 arctan(Fz / c2))), peak normalised side force falls with load; sec. 4.3.2 (Eqs. 4.E1-4.E2) carries load through dfz. Our measured flat CS-vs-axle-Fz in the working range is CONSISTENT, not a test: CS is the ratio of the local stiffness to a session reference (position on the curve), so the degressive rise of the absolute stiffness largely cancels; theory does not predict a rising ratio. The rear rise above 11 kN (speed / throttle confounded, at the clip) is not interpretable against it. Implication: the pooled axle curve spans a load range (aero); narrowing that range moves the fit towards the "given Fz" condition of Eq. 4.49.
(e4) TRANSIENTS. Sec. 7.2.1 (Eqs. 7.6-7.7): side-slip relaxation length sigma_a = C_Fa / C_Fy; the carcass deflection follows the slip angle as a first-order lag with time constant sigma_a / |V_x|, i.e. corner frequency V_x / (2 pi sigma_a). The book gives no value for our tyre; with an assumed sigma_a of a few tenths of a metre (assumption, not from the book) the corner frequency at 20-60 m/s lies around 5-30 Hz, far above 2 Hz. Implication: on 2 Hz-filtered signals the tyre lag is negligible and the steady-state curve is the right model; faster content (the 0.15 s MA passes up to ~12 Hz) would carry relaxation hysteresis into the fit population.
(f) CROSS-LABELS for the d-sketch (chair / Pacejka):
- Low-pass conditioning of the fit inputs (our 2 Hz Butterworth; chair 0.15 s MA): chair-convergent (both condition) AND theory-required (steady-state model, sec. 4.3 / 1.2.2 / 7.2.1) -- UNASSAILABLE, already shipped.
- Low-speed cut (ours 5 m/s; chair 3 m/s): chair-convergent AND theory-required (slip defined as -V_y / V_x, sec. 1.2.1 Eq. 1.3, singular as V_x -> 0) -- UNASSAILABLE, already shipped.
- Speed window on the fit population: chair-convergent (implicit, band union) and theory-consistent (narrows the aero-load spread towards Eq. 4.49's given-Fz condition), not theory-required.
- Quasi-steady restriction beyond the low-pass: theory-required (sec. 1.2.2) but NOT chair-convergent (no such selection in the chair chain).
- Longitudinal gate (L): theory-consistent for LARGE Fx (sec. 4.3.1 / 1.3.4), theory-silent on the bound; not chair-convergent -- our invention.
- Kerb mask: theory-consistent (road unevenness is non-steady input, ch. 8 / 10); not chair (our domain improvement).
- Signed fit, both axles: theory-consistent (sec. 4.3.1: anti-symmetric curve with shifts S_H, S_V; folding forces symmetry and discards the shifts); not chair-convergent (chair folds, front only), forced by our observer.
- Axle-level slip without Fz weighting: theory-consistent (sec. 1.2.2 effective axle characteristics include load transfer); chair weights with model loads.
- Analysis-laps-only, per-session fit: theory-silent.
- Lateral-velocity provenance: theory-required in substance (the slip angle must be the true -V_y / V_x, Eq. 1.3); ours is the kinematic seed -- forced by our car, the inherent limit.

## Rulings after the Pacejka check; Q-FIT-DECISIVE received [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, records only]

1. Speed window: derived from our own speed distribution (vehicle parameterisation), not transplanted.
2. Quasi-steady condition: satisfied by the 2 Hz low-pass of the fit inputs -- the tyre's relaxation corner (5-30 Hz under a stated sigma_a assumption, Pacejka sec. 7.2.1) lies far above 2 Hz; no additional selection step.
3. Longitudinal gate: the tight version (|a_x| < 2 m/s^2) dies -- theory says moderate Fx leaves the side force nearly unchanged (weighting function G_yk ~ 1, Pacejka sec. 4.3.1 Eqs. 4.64-4.69; sec. 1.3.4), so removing 65-76 % of the fit population buys nothing. A loose large-Fx exclusion (LX) replaces it: bound derived from our a_x distribution, Tier B, theory-consistent, not chair practice.
4. Comparability with the chair = selection and conditioning; the provenance of the lateral velocity (logged at the chair, kinematic seed here) is the inherent limit and thesis content.
5. Chair pieces outside the reference set stay outside (per-wheel slip function, smoothing caller, fit file choice); recorded.
6. Thresholds parked behind Q-FIT-DECISIVE.

accuracy (Bechtloff 2018 VDI; Antonov et al. 2011 VSD; Wielitzka et al.
2014 IEEE CDC), but UKF requires more tuning (Antonov; Chindamo) and
positive-definite covariance / stability not guaranteed (Yang/Shi/Chen
2017, J. Navigation). Goblirsch 2024 states real-vehicle localization
uses EKF for computational stability and themselves run an EKF core with
UKF only as sideslip sub-estimator. Thesis stance: acknowledge UKF
accuracy edge, justify EKF by stability/tunability/real-vehicle practice;
own contribution is per-session Pacejka parametrization, not filter
family. One paragraph in ch. 2.4 or 3.4; todo marker set in draft.

Finding 3 - kinematic beta precedent: Goblirsch Eq. 8 (beta_kin =
atan(lr/l * tan(delta_f))) matches the SetupTool Level-1 kinematic beta;
Selmanaj et al. 2017 (Control Engineering Practice 67:1-12) is the
kinematic-approach anchor paper. Both citable precedent for the Level-1
route.

Finding 4 - TUM lineage anchor: their ref [5], Betz et al., "TUM
Autonomous Motorsport: An Autonomous Racing Software for the Indy
Autonomous Challenge", Journal of Field Robotics 2022, author list
includes F. Werner, L. Hermansdorfer and M. Lienkamp. Published backbone
for the ch. 2.6 lineage (Werner MA -> TUM published line -> chair
tooling -> this thesis). To retrieve; supervisor question (b) likely
answered by this.

Harvest queue from its reference list (verify each, open, then Citavi):
Kalman 1960 (J. Basic Engineering 82:35-45); Chindamo 2018; Jin 2019;
Selmanaj 2017; Wischnewski et al. 2019 (IFAC-PapersOnLine 52(8):154-161);
Betz et al. 2022 (J. Field Robotics); Yang 2017; optionally Antonov 2011,
Wielitzka 2014, Villano 2021, Bechtloff 2018. Thrun 2006: optional,
only if TUM library access works; not load-bearing.

## Front limit visited under combined braking; LT authorised; what "the fit works" means [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, records only]

FINDING (author ruling 2, from Q-FIT-DECISIVE's LX front degeneration): on this car's data the FRONT axle reaches its high-slip / limit region mainly while braking -- removing the heavy-braking tail (a_x < -1.29 g, JST 29) stripped the front fit of its high-slip support and left a curve with no peak (C 0.87, E -24.3). The pure-lateral front limit is therefore not directly observable in our track data; what the front fit sees near the limit is combined slip, where the side force at a given slip angle is reduced by the longitudinal force (Pacejka sec. 1.2.1 friction circle; sec. 4.3.1 Eqs. 4.64-4.69 weighting function G_yk). The fitted front curve near and beyond its peak is an effective combined-slip characteristic, not the pure-slip curve -- a stated limitation of track-data identification.
AUTHORISED: one further variant LT (traction tail only: exclude a_x above the per-session p95, keep heavy braking), new frame, same bars.
WHAT "THE FIT WORKS" MEANS (author ruling 3, design principle): method chair-comparable (achieved); fit population cleaned where physics supports it; absolute quality capped by the sensor set (no lateral-velocity / beta sensor) -- stated, not apologised. After LT the data-entry route is exhausted on this frame; what remains is provenance-side.
Q-FIT-DECISIVE result accepted as pre-registered (nothing ships); inspect_fit_decisive.py keep-reproduces confirmed.

## Literature digest written [2026-10-04, records only]

docs/literature_digest.md (local only, gitignored): one entry per work on disk (25 works + the chair reference code), with reading status, what each describes where it matters to the thesis and the application, and a closing synthesis. Headline findings beyond the claims register: (1) Bechtloff's dissertation (2018, VDI 809) estimates the UNDERSTEER GRADIENT as a filter state -- it converges fast from steady driving while axle stiffnesses need dynamic excitation (sec. 6.3): the strongest precedent for K2 as the robust balance readout; (2) published relaxation lengths 0.25-0.55 m (Bechtloff secs. 2.3.3, 4.6.3) back the 2 Hz conditioning argument; (3) Pacejka Fig. 1.7: load transfer can remove the axle peak -- a peakless fitted AXLE curve is not unphysical in itself (the C > 1 sanity screen is a fit-shape rule); (4) the chair's "logged" lateral velocity is, for at least one vehicle configuration, an estimator output of the Goblirsch / Bechtloff family (inference from the parser mapping); (5) per-wheel slip anchor found (Kiencke & Nielsen 8.3.2 Eq. 8.11); (6) no driver-feedback comparison methodology on disk (claim j stays open).

## Rulings after the literature digest; outlook item [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, records only]

1. SANITY SCREEN = FIT-SHAPE RULE, NOT PHYSICS (author). The calibration-frame screen (B >= 1, 1 < C <= 3, E <= 1, all finite) is kept as-is but labelled explicitly as a fit-shape rule. CAUTION (Pacejka sec. 1.2.2, Fig. 1.7): lateral load transfer leaves the axle curve's origin slope unchanged but lowers its slope at larger slip angles; the axle peak may diminish or disappear completely -- a peakless effective AXLE curve can be physical. The screen flags shapes the observer chain should not run on; it does not claim such curves are physically impossible. The running LT frame stays as frozen (no mid-run change); future frames carry the label.
2. Q-K2 LITERATURE ANCHOR (author): Bechtloff (2018, dissertation TU Darmstadt, VDI 809) sec. 6.3 is the main anchor of the Q-K2 proposal -- the understeer gradient, estimated as a filter state, converges fast from steady driving (2.2 % error), while the absolute axle stiffnesses need dynamic excitation. This also explains the K2-constrained pass's HARM: the stiffness magnitude there came from biased kinematic-seed slip angles.
3. CLAIM j -- DRIVER FEEDBACK vs DATA (author): the evaluation protocol states its OWN method explicitly, citing Segers (secs. 1.2.1, 7.4, 14.1) and Milliken (sec. 11.1) as practice precedent -- reading driver comments alongside logged data is documented practice; no formal comparison method exists in the literature on disk. No further source hunt. The thesis's explicit protocol is itself the method contribution -- modest and owned.
4. VARIANT W (dated note): the per-wheel slip-angle anchor gap is CLOSED by Kiencke & Nielsen sec. 8.3.2 Eq. 8.11. W stays dead on INPUTS: per-wheel steer absent (one steering ratio, no Ackermann / toe data), track width an unsourced placeholder, expected effect <= ~0.1 deg.
5. PROVENANCE LIMIT REWORDED (author): ~~"the chair's slip angle rests on a logged / measured lateral velocity, ours on a kinematic seed"~~ [reworded 2026-10-04] -> the chair's lateral velocity is REFERENCE-TUNED (estimator of the Goblirsch / Bechtloff family ~~tuned against a Correvit optical sensor~~ [SUPERSEDED 2026-10-07, read-only passes 1+2: Goblirsch et al. state the Correvit is used for evaluation only; the IFAC 2019 state-estimation paper uses the optical sensor as a filter input in one variant; no tuning-against claim is supported], or the optical sensor itself, depending on vehicle configuration); ours has NO reference. The contrast is REFERENCE AVAILABILITY, not estimator architecture (the architectures are of the same family).
OUTLOOK (author ruling; outlook chapter, concrete recommendation to the team; no work item, no BACKLOG entry): REFERENCE-TUNING DAY. One test day with an optical sideslip sensor (Correvit / Kistler class) would convert the estimator from shape-valid to reference-pinned: tune the EKF parameters and validate beta against measured lateral velocity, then run the tuned estimator on all regular telemetry (the tuning transfers within the car / tyre family). Literature precedent: every published estimator of this architecture was reference-tuned (Bechtloff 2016 / 2018, Goblirsch, Villano; 0.2-1.1 deg errors WITH a reference). The same day would pin a reference-grade slip-angle population for one tyre-fit upgrade.

## Steering-ratio premise check: L4 lookup exists, but it divides by a LOCAL ratio [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: session STEP 1 (author), read-only premise check: (a) how production converts the logged steering signal to road-wheel angle, (b) the front slip-angle error a fixed ratio implies, (c) whether a variable-ratio lookup is a clean input swap.
(a) LOGGED CHANNEL: log_asteer [deg], 100 Hz, STEERING-WHEEL angle (census of the three Tier-1 caches; not rack travel, not an already-converted wheel angle). PRODUCTION (modules/stability_analysis.py prepare_vehicle_state): delta_f = steer_sw / i_s(steer_sw); i_s = np.interp of the car_data.json steering_ratio_table (manufacturer table, Level 4) when accuracy resolution allows L4 (modules/accuracy_resolution.py; app default "Best available" = L4 when the local car_data.json exists; implemented WP-B 2026-07-26), else the constant 15.7 (L1). THE DIAGNOSTICS HARNESS (inspect_tyre_prior_d2._params, inherited by inspect_last_push / ma / k2 / fit_decisive -- every frozen-frame fit experiment) RUNS AT cap=1, i.e. the constant 15.7 (asserted on the live state). So the work order's premise "production uses a fixed ratio" is wrong for the app and right for the harness.
DISCOVERED DEFECT (definition mismatch): the table's steering_ratio column is the LOCAL ratio d(sw)/d(wheel), not the overall ratio sw / wheel. The table's own columns show it: at full stroke sw 291.5 deg, wheel 20.98 deg -> overall 13.89, column 11.93, numerical slope ~12.3; at sw 135.5 deg overall 15.33, column 14.02, slope 14.19. Production divides the TOTAL angle by the LOCAL ratio and therefore overestimates the wheel angle at large steer. The correct L4 conversion reads the wheel angle from the table directly (interpolate wheel_angle_deg over steering_wheel_angle_deg). [Definition inferred from the table's internal consistency; the author confirms against the setup sheet.]
(b) ERRORS vs the table's own wheel angle (mean of the +/- stroke branches, i.e. the two front wheels' Ackermann mean), front alpha error = delta error to first order: |sw| 113 deg (fit-population p99, Paul Ricard): L1 -0.12 deg, current L4 +0.42 deg; 152 deg (US-v2 fit max): L1 -0.42, L4 +1.07; 168 deg (JST 29 fit max): L1 -0.58, L4 +1.43; full lock 291 deg (not driven): L1 -2.70, L4 +3.16. Fit-population census (base mask): |sw| p99 113 / 114 / 127 deg, max 152 / 160 / 168 deg (US-v2 / v3 / JST 29); the current L4 departs from L1 by > 0.5 deg on 1.4-2.0 % of fit samples (2.3-3.3 % inside corner brackets), > 1 deg on 0.07-0.61 %. The fixed 15.7 is closer to the true wheel angle than the current L4 over the whole driven range (about 2.5x smaller error, opposite sign). The work order's "15.7 -> 11.9" span is the local-ratio span; the overall ratio only falls 15.7 -> 13.9 at full lock.
(c) INPUT SWAP: clean in structure (one line in prepare_vehicle_state, table already loaded and cache-identified by accuracy resolution, front-only kinematic input) but NOT effect-free under ekf_auto_pacejka: delta_f is an EKF input, so beta, the fit population's alpha and both axles' CS can move (the 2026-07 "front-only" scoping was measured on the kinematic beta).

## Steering conversion rulings: local ratio confirmed, fix gates the estimator [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, records only]

RULINGS (author) on the steering-ratio premise check: (1) the table's steering_ratio column is the LOCAL ratio d(sw)/d(wheel) -- confirmed (full lock 291.455 / 20.984 = 13.89 overall vs column 11.925; the manufacturer's ratio-curve plot shows the local slope). The correct conversion interpolates the table's wheel-angle column against its steering-wheel-angle column directly; no ratio division. (2) The fix comes first, before any further fit work (speed-window adoption, pooled fits, iteration): the steering angle feeds beta, alpha and CS, so every frozen-frame verdict so far ran on a wrong front steering input (harness: constant 15.7; app: total angle divided by the local ratio). This is the true "estimator final" gate. (3) The harness moves to the corrected conversion and becomes the same conversion as the app -- one source of truth.
ANCHOR for the two-wheel mean (verified, rendered text of the on-disk PDF): Rajamani, Vehicle Dynamics and Control, sec. 2.2, Ackermann turning geometry, Eq. 2.17 -- the bicycle model's single front steer angle is the average of the inner and outer front wheel angles (their difference grows with the square of the average angle, Eq. 2.18).
PREMISE CORRECTION (for the fix proposal): the Dubai goldens and test_stability.py run at accuracy cap 1 (the L1 constant, by design: reproducible on clones without the gitignored car_data.json) -- the fix does not move them.

## Steering fix: robustness rule frozen before the impact assessment [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, records only]

RULE (author, frozen before any (d) number): earlier frozen-frame verdicts (computed at the constant 15.7) count as robust to the steering-input error iff, for every Tier-1 session (US-v2, v3, JST 29) and axle, going from the constant 15.7 to the corrected table conversion moves the in-corner CS < 0 share by <= 1.0 point, the in-corner CS < -1 share by <= 20 % relative, the fitted origin slope by <= 5 %, and, per session, the median in-corner |delta-beta| is <= 0.2 deg. Rationale for the beta clause: beta is the propagating input to alpha; it can shift without the CS shares shifting, and a material beta shift means the earlier verdicts ran on materially different slip angles even if CS looks stable. Otherwise the Q-FIT-DECISIVE / LT verdicts are re-run on the corrected chain. The verdict itself is the author's ruling.

## Beta spikes between faulty and corrected steering: fallback-switch timing, not steering [2026-10-04, branch new-laps, read-only]

WORK ORDER: author ruling 3 -- locate the isolated 8-10 deg beta differences between the faulty and the corrected steering conversion before the robustness ruling; report, no fix. Script: diagnostics/inspect_steering_fix_impact.py mode spikes; output plots/steering_fix_impact/spikes.txt.
METHOD: each path's final EKF pass rebuilt from its manifest (Pacejka fit + chosen R); the rebuild reproduces the cached production beta to 4e-7 deg on all six runs, so its divergence mask is the production one. Events = |d beta| > 2 deg, runs closer than 0.2 s merged (reporting choices, Tier B).
COUNT AND PLACE: |d beta| > 2 deg on 2361 / 2163 / 527 samples (1.6 / 3.2 / 0.5 % of the file; US-v2 / v3 / JST 29), in 598 / 461 / 171 events; median event length 0.02-0.03 s (1-3 samples), longest 1.5 / 2.8 / 0.6 s; > 5 deg on 337 / 316 / 41 samples; events >= 8 deg: 7 / 2 / 1. Mostly in corners (76 / 51 / 71 % of events mainly in a corner bracket), rarely on kerbs (7 / 8 / 20 %), at moderate steering (median |sw| at the peak 30-42 deg, where the two conversions agree to < 0.01 deg) and ~39 m/s. The 15 deg hard bound never fires; divergence flags cover 1.4 / 1.4 / 0.7 % of samples in both runs.
MECHANISM: at the event peak one run is in the kinematic fallback and the other on the EKF in 98 / 97 / 88 % of events; a divergence flag differing between the runs lies within 5 s before or inside every event. The EKF's fallback is a per-sample switch: a flagged sample carries the kinematic beta and the state resets to it. The tiny upstream difference (front steering input plus the slightly different fit and chosen R it causes) moves the samples where the NIS-window flag trips, so the two runs differ there by the full EKF-minus-kinematic gap (several degrees) for a few samples. The spike size measures that gap, not the steering change (max |d delta| in the event window < 0.1 deg in 53-69 % of events). LIMITATION (thesis-worthy): production beta_with_fallback is discontinuous at fallback switches, and the switch timing is sensitive to small input changes.
DO THEY REACH CS: yes, through the 2 Hz CS chain. Share of in-corner samples within +/-0.5 s of a > 2 deg spike: 48 / 71 / 24 %. CS < 0 sign flips on common samples: 80 / 88 / 47 % of them lie near spikes. Decomposition faulty -> corrected, in-corner CS < 0:
- v3 front +1.74 pt = +2.48 pt near spikes, -0.05 pt away from them -> the shift is driven by fallback-switch timing.
- JST 29 rear +1.48 pt = +2.62 near, +1.13 away -> a systematic part remains away from spikes.
- JST 29 front +0.64 (near -1.16, away +1.14); US-v2 front +0.07 (near -0.21, away +0.31); US-v2 rear -0.61 (near -0.77, away -0.50); v3 rear +0.14 (near +0.59, away -0.87).
AMENDED RULE ON (i) -> (iii), as frozen + ruling 2 (CS < -1 relative bar only with >= 50 CS < -1 samples): beta median 0.033 / 0.094 / 0.026 deg -- within 0.2. Origin slope front +0.8 / 0.0 / +1.2 %, rear 0 -- within 5 %. CS < 0: OVER the 1.0 pt bar on v3 front (+1.74) and JST 29 rear (+1.48); all other cells within. ## Literature check before the iteration experiment (Step 4) [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, read-only]

Read on the rendered text of the PDFs in docs/literature (sections named are the ones verified):
1. Villano, Lenzo & Sakhnevych (2021), Meccanica 56, sec. 3.3: the cross-combination runs the kinematic filter and the dynamic UKF CONCURRENTLY and exchanges the common STATES at each time step (the kinematic filter's v_x feeds the dynamic filter, the dynamic filter's yaw rate feeds the kinematic filter), with a steady-state index (RMS of a_y over a 0.1 s buffer; 0.4 / 0.6 m/s^2 membership bounds) weighting kinematic (transients) vs dynamic (steady state) beta. Tyre parameters stay FIXED; validated against an optical sensor. PREMISE CORRECTION: our fit -> EKF -> refit iteration is not a batch version of this -- it re-identifies tyre parameters from estimated states, which their sec. 1 lists separately as the dual EKF (parameters estimated and fed to the state filter, recursively) and the two-stage structure (an EKF's states used to estimate tyre parameters). The source papers of those two schemes are not on disk; their convergence criteria are not verifiable here.
2. Bechtloff (2018), sec. 1.2 (state of the art): stiffness adaptation from estimated axle forces (RLS) "works well for dynamic manoeuvres; for stationary manoeuvres the estimation of the sideslip angle, and with it of the cornering stiffnesses, can diverge" (citing Bechtloff 2013); and "the stiffnesses can only be identified with a certain dynamic excitation" (citing Bechtloff et al. 2015). [Translated from German.]
3. Bechtloff (2018), sec. 6.3: convergence is judged on the parameter's estimated standard deviation settling ("the standard deviations of the cornering stiffnesses converge only after about 160 s") and against offline values identified with the reference sensor system; the understeer gradient converges after about 40 s.
4. Bechtloff (2018), sec. 6.2: with dynamic driving the sideslip needed to identify the lateral-force curves "can be determined even without reference sensors such as a Correvit" (max error 1.2 deg) -- but that estimator was itself parameterised with reference-identified axle models (ch. 4).
5. Sierra et al. (2006), sec. 3: under-determined stiffness methods need persistently exciting information "for the estimation results to converge to the true values".
6. Bechtloff, Koenig & Isermann (2016), sec. 1: kinematic integration must be stabilised by feedback; sensor bias is challenging.
7. Ortiz et al. (2006), sec. 1: regression-based Magic Formula fitting requires starting values; good starting values are hard to obtain -- start dependence of the fit, relevant to the two starting points of the experiment.
NO verbatim statement on disk that reference-free iteration AMPLIFIES bias. The closest warnings are (2) divergence of estimated-state-based stiffness adaptation in stationary driving and (5) convergence to the true values only under persistent excitation. Together with our own recorded circularity (a refit on a population whose slip angles were produced with a curve tends to return that curve -- PLAN (d2) P1 anchor note), they justify the pre-registered amplification exit and predict what iteration can do: steady track cornering supports the balance, not the absolute stiffness (Bechtloff 2018 sec. 6.3).

## Iteration experiment (Step 4): refitting on refined slip angles drifts, does not converge; both starting points HARM [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, read-only]

LITERATURE, as frozen in the header of diagnostics/inspect_iteration.py: the scheme belongs to the dual-EKF / two-stage family listed by Villano, Lenzo & Sakhnevych (2021, Meccanica 56) sec. 1 (their own cross-combination, sec. 3.3, exchanges states with fixed tyre parameters -- not this scheme); convergence judged on the parameter spread settling, after Bechtloff (2018, VDI 12/809) sec. 6.3; divergence warning behind the amplification exit: Bechtloff (2018) sec. 1.2 (stiffness adaptation from estimated axle forces "can diverge" in stationary manoeuvres) and Sierra, Tseng, Jain & Peng (2006, VSD 44 sup1) sec. 3 (convergence "to the true values" needs persistent excitation); start dependence of Magic Formula regression: Ortiz et al. (2006, VSD 44:9) sec. 1. No work on disk states verbatim that reference-free iteration amplifies bias.

READINGS (labelled, for the author):
1. NO REFERENCE-FREE FIXED POINT WITHIN THREE ROUNDS. After round 1 the steps settle at 1-6 % per round but never below the fit noise, and the rear peak force rises EVERY round (US-v2 own 10.1 -> 12.5 -> 14.0 -> 14.8 kN; v3 own 12.3 -> 13.6 -> 14.3 kN) with the peak moving to larger slip; the front step re-accelerates at round 3 in 5 of 6 branches (the frozen exit compares rounds 1 and 2 only, so it did not catch this). This is the persistent drift the literature warns of for estimated-state stiffness identification without excitation or reference (Bechtloff 2018 sec. 1.2; Sierra sec. 3).
2. THE "IMPROVEMENTS" ARE WHAT A SELF-REINFORCING LOOP PRODUCES. Every scored candidate improves, yet the in-corner CS < 0 share -- the disagreement signal between curve and data -- collapses (US-v2 rear 14.1 -> 1.4 %, v3 rear 16.0 -> 1.9 %) while finite-CS coverage falls. Curve and estimator converge toward mutual agreement; without a reference nothing distinguishes that from truth. The frame's no-harm bars (coverage) are what catches it.
3. START DEPENDENCE. Where the iteration ends after three rounds depends on where it started (Ortiz sec. 1), most strongly on Paul Ricard, where the pool curve is NBR-dominated.

## Rulings on the iteration experiment; agreement metrics vs data-anchored metrics [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, records only]

1. VERDICTS ACCEPTED (author): both starting points HARM; the one-pass production fit stands as the production fitting procedure. CONCLUSION (thesis material, with its evidence): without a reference sensor, refitting the tyre curve on refined slip angles has no fixed point within three rounds -- round-1 steps of 4-53 x the session's lap-to-lap fit noise, then a sustained 1-6 % drift per round with the rear peak force rising every round. This matches the published warnings: Bechtloff (2018, VDI 12/809) sec. 1.2 (stiffness adaptation from estimated states can diverge in stationary driving) and Sierra, Tseng, Jain & Peng (2006, VSD 44 sup1) sec. 3 (convergence to the true values needs persistent excitation). THE FAILED PREDICTION IS A FINDING: the loop is an open drift, not mere self-consistency (the predicted return to the starting curve did not happen).
2. AMPLIFICATION-EXIT LIMITATION (observation only, no re-run): the frozen exit compared rounds 1 and 2 only and missed the round-3 re-acceleration of the front step in 5 of 6 branches. The verdict is unaffected (HARM on coverage regardless). Future iteration frames, if any, compare consecutive rounds throughout.
3. FINDING -- AGREEMENT METRICS CANNOT TELL SELF-CONSISTENCY FROM TRUTH (methodological point, thesis material): in the iteration every internal-consistency metric improved (lap-to-lap fit stability, smear sensitivity, lap-to-lap beta coherence, straight-line beta, chatter, the CS < 0 and CS < -1 shares) while the data-grounded metric -- finite-CS coverage -- collapsed. In a reference-free chain, agreement between the estimator and its own curve can rise without the estimate getting closer to the truth; only data-anchored metrics can arbitrate. Recorded beside the two uncertainty sources of CS levels (fallback-switch timing, about +/-1-2 pt; curve choice, up to 4 pt) and cross-referenced to the verdict-validity frame: RELATIVE verdicts (variant vs production on identical inputs) remain valid; this finding concerns ABSOLUTE calibration only.
4. inspect_iteration.py keep-reproduces confirmed.
5. Kerb-display package authorised; rulings and caption recorded in PLAN.md STATUS (2026-10-05).

Exactly as pre-stated by construction (Milliken RCVD ch. 5, 2-DOF balance): with a Level-1 axle force split, mu_f / mu_r reports where the LOAD sits (aero balance, longitudinal transfer), not which axle saturates. LIMITS (stated): Fy is the Level-1 axle split estimate, Fz measured; mu is utilisation of the ESTIMATED lateral force against MEASURED load, not a friction measurement; banking / gradient and combined slip (Fx ignored) carry over; absolute level inherits the config mass and Iz (L1).
WHAT IT IS GOOD FOR (reading, for the author's ruling): a measured-load picture of how hard each axle is loaded laterally relative to its vertical load -- a load-aware g-g / occupancy input (BACKLOG item 10) and an independent check that the measured loads behave physically (front p99 1.8, rear 1.55, within slick-tyre range); not a balance metric.

## Rulings: gradient line ships; Werner read first, default chair-conform; damper loads consumed by one thesis g-g figure [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, records only]

The gradient is the car's steady-state balance over the quasi-steady population; a corner verdict is the local saturation of one axle in one phase of one corner, read from the cornering stiffness ratio. A car that understeers in steady state can still saturate its rear first at a given corner exit (traction, load transfer) -- the two are complementary, not contradictory.
2. WERNER SCOPE (author): read first whether Werner states a stability criterion or threshold form. If not, option (c): the stability measure stays chair-conform (inertial regressand, no damping term, no schema bump), Werner and Hoffman / Ono anchor the concept, stab_neg_thresh derives from the clean-population percentile run beside the CS thresholds, and the v2 damping term is recorded as considered-not-adopted (chair deviation, unmeasured benefit).
3. DAMPER LOADS (author, standing rule applied without sentiment): consumers after Q-MASS are c_session (insurance in the reconstruction cascade) and one thesis-script g-g figure (per-corner ay-ax, phase-coloured, kerb-graded, measured-Fz occupancy) built in the results phase -- no app view. ## Werner read: a sign criterion for stability, no threshold form; the measurement-side yaw-moment route abandoned by Werner himself [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, read-only; source verified in docs/literature/Werner_2021_MA.pdf text layer]

1. CRITERION FORM (sec. 2.2.3, printed p. 16, after Milliken RCVD): the stability moment derivative dMz/dbeta is "the measure of open-loop stability"; the car is stable when the rear's stabilising moment grows faster than the front's destabilising moment; if dMz/dbeta is NEGATIVE the sideslip grows unchecked without a counter-reaction; negative values occur mainly near the rear axle's lateral-force maximum. The criterion is the SIGN (zero as the physical boundary), not a value.
2. NOT A CRITICALITY THRESHOLD (same section, p. 16): skilled drivers operate in open-loop unstable states (Inagaki; Yi; Kegelmann), so "the region of negative stability is not to be interpreted as fundamentally critical"; temporary operation there may even be necessary for lap time. Sec. 4.3 (p. 48) and the measured-data plausibility check sec. 4.5.3 (pp. 57-58) read stability qualitatively against zero ("the first dip below zero seems small enough to have no noticeable effect; the second, somewhat larger one correlates with the rapid rise of sideslip") -- magnitude judged case by case, no numerical bound stated anywhere in sec. 2.2, 4.3 or 4.5.
3. EQ. 4.3 ROUTE (sec. 4.5.2, p. 57; discussion sec. 7.1, p. 86): the measurement-side yaw moment needs the yaw damping, which "behaves nonlinearly and would have to be derived with additional uncertainties"; "a correlation of the yaw moment could not be investigated successfully" and was dropped "owing to the small added value". Werner's own stability values come from SIMULATED yaw-moment diagrams (Milliken Moment Method), not from a measured regression.
4. CONSEQUENCE (per the author's ruling of the same day, no new decision taken here): the read yields no stated threshold form -> DEFAULT (c) applies unless the author rules otherwise on the text: the stability measure stays chair-conform (inertial regressand, no damping term, no schema bump); Werner (sec. 2.2.3, sign criterion and its non-criticality) and Milliken anchor the concept and the zero boundary; stab_neg_thresh derives from the clean-population percentile distribution beside the CS thresholds; the v2 damping term is recorded considered-not-adopted (chair deviation, unmeasured benefit, and the route Werner himself could not close). Anchor consequence for the derivation: a percentile-derived stab_neg_thresh must lie at or below zero to stay consistent with Werner's sign boundary.

## Pacejka anchor for the lateral-only, axle-level tyre fit [2026-10-05, read-only; verified in docs/literature (Pacejka, Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics, 2nd ed., 2006, text layer)]

a. PURE-SLIP BASE CURVE: sec. 4.3.1, Eq. (4.49) y = D sin[C arctan{Bx - E(Bx - arctan Bx)}] with Y = y + S_V, x = X + S_H (Eqs. 4.50-4.51), X = tan(alpha) for the side force (printed pp. 173-174); D = peak, BCD = origin slope, C shape, E curvature; Eqs. (4.52)-(4.53) assess C and E from the curve's peak, asymptote and peak location. Full model: Eq. (4.E19) F_yo = D_y sin[C_y arctan{B_y alpha_y - E_y(B_y alpha_y - arctan(B_y alpha_y))}] + S_Vy (p. 187), with D_y = mu_y F_z (4.E22) and B_y = K_ya / (C_y D_y) (4.E26). OUR REDUCED FORM = Eq. 4.49 with S_H = S_V = 0 (no ply-steer / conicity / camber offsets) and D free (not mu F_z), alpha for tan(alpha) (under 1 % apart below 8 deg). Fig. 4.10 caption (p. 175): "a value of curvature factor E > 1 does not produce realistic curves" -- the anchor of the sanity screen's E <= 1.
b. EFFECTIVE AXLE CHARACTERISTIC: sec. 1.2.2 (pp. 7-14): for (quasi) steady-state turning a two-wheel model with EFFECTIVE AXLE CHARACTERISTICS takes compliance, roll and load transfer into account (p. 7), restricted to quasi-steady motion; "Effective Non-Linear Axle Characteristics" with Fig. 1.7 (p. 14): under load transfer the origin slope is unaffected, at larger slip angles the derivative is lower, "the peak diminishes and may even disappear completely"; Exercise 1.1 (p. 15) constructs the axle curve from the tyre curves and the load transfer, with the Magic Formula Eq. (1.6). This is exactly the object we fit: Fy_axle(alpha_axle) from 2-DOF axle forces.
c. COMBINED SLIP AS AN EXTENSION OF THE BASE CURVE: sec. 4.3.1 (pp. 179-180): weighting functions G "multiplied with the original pure slip functions (4.49) produce the interaction effects"; they "take the value one in the special case of pure slip"; Eq. (4.65) F_y = G_yk F_yo + S_Vyk, Eq. (4.66) G_yk normalised to unity at kappa = 0, shape coefficients Eqs. (4.67)-(4.69). Ordering: the pure-lateral curve is the base object, combined slip modifies it, not the reverse; near kappa = 0 G_yk ~ 1 (a slight increase at moderate braking is part of the hill shape), so moderate Fx is theory-harmless; the large-Fx tails are the known bias (recorded: front limit visited mainly under braking, "Front limit visited under combined braking ..." 2026-10-04).
d. IDENTIFICATION FROM DATA: what exists -- sec. 1.2.1 (p. 7): the shape factors C and E, the stiffness parameters and the friction coefficient "may be estimated or determined through regression techniques"; Eqs. (4.52)-(4.53) give C and E from measured curve features; sec. 4.3 refers to parameters "assessed through the fitting process" (p. 200) of tyre measurements. What does NOT exist in the pages read: any guidance on identifying the curve from VEHICLE data (on-car axle forces and estimated slip angles) rather than from tyre-test-rig measurements -- the book assumes measured tyre input-output. Our route (vehicle data, estimated alpha) therefore rests on the chair tooling and Bechtloff (axle-force identification, sec. 4.4.1), not on Pacejka.
DOCSTRING (modules/tyre_fit_auto.py header, comment only, no behaviour change): "Lateral-only axle fit (Pacejka 2nd ed.): pure side slip is the base curve, Eq. 4.49 / 4.E19 with zero shifts and free D (sec. 4.3.1; regression per sec. 1.2.1); an effective axle curve absorbing load transfer is valid for quasi-steady turning, peak may vanish (sec. 1.2.2). Combined slip only scales it by G_yk = 1 at zero slip ratio (Eqs. 4.64-4.69): moderate Fx is harmless, the large-Fx tails (front limit seen under braking) are the known bias."

It catches the strikes that drive the deep CS tail (25 events, including all of the deepest dips); demonstrable misses at the 5 % chance level are 4 of 58 events (4 % of deep samples per axle), too few and too marginal to carry a detector change without tuning against noise. No recalibration, no new detector term, no config change.
2. WATCH ITEM: the C2 1044-1057 m left-wheel pair (F39, R01; FL / RL load transients, laps 108 / 103) -- reopens only if future files reproduce it.
3. LEDGER CLOSED as frozen: kerb-shown 25 + 4, car-on-track events 2, proven estimator artefacts 3 (lived with, pre-registered), and a residual of about 50 % (front) / 36 % (rear) of deep samples in which no specific mechanism is shown.
4. AUTHOR READING of the residual (interpretation, labelled as such): the known noise floor of a reference-free sideslip estimate; the classification already aggregates past it (phase medians, worst-phase aggregation, deep thresholds). The audit itself demonstrates no mechanism for these events -- the reading is an interpretation consistent with the recorded switch-timing sensitivity and the absence of a reference sensor, not a shown cause.
5. METHOD MATERIAL (thesis): a three-stage audit -- broad pre-registered classes, a specificity re-pass against matched random windows, one tightening to a union-5 % level -- with labels frozen after the single permitted tightening; every final criterion's base rate measured (2.5-6.0 %).

## Curve floor vs thresholds: STRONG lies beyond the quasi-steady characteristic on every pool session, both axles [2026-10-05, branch new-laps, read-only]

SCRIPT: diagnostics/inspect_curve_floor.py (rules frozen in its header; author EXECUTE). Production Pacejka curve per session and axle at best available (six from the 2026-10-05 production caches, Dubai fitted fresh). FLOOR = min over slip angle of (dFy/dalpha) / (B C D) -- the curve's own cornering-stiffness-ratio analogue -- on the visited range 0 .. p99 |alpha| of the production fit population; the 0-30 deg floor beside. Full suite at HEAD 9427b6a before the run: 585 passed, 9 skipped, 1 xfailed.
FRONT (STRONG -0.646, MODERATE -0.285), visited-range floor / 0-30 deg floor: Dubai +0.087 / -0.069 (peak 6.3 deg outside the visited 5.0 deg); Paul Ricard outing 25 -0.061 / -0.123; outing 32 +0.005 / -0.053 (peak outside); NBR JST 21 -0.235 / -0.248; JST 29 -0.305 / -0.320; NBR qualifying CDR -0.325 / -0.339; qualifying MLA -0.213 / -0.213. Pool (deepest session floor) -0.325.
REAR (STRONG -0.404, MODERATE -0.131): Dubai +0.165 / -0.210 (peak outside); Paul Ricard outing 25 +0.017 / -0.208 (peak outside); outing 32 +0.195 / -0.329 (peak outside); JST 21 -0.223 / -0.267; JST 29 -0.209 / -0.298; qualifying CDR -0.233 / -0.233; qualifying MLA -0.203 / -0.284. Pool -0.233.
OUTCOME (pre-stated case 2, both axles, every session, also against the 0-30 deg extension): STRONG lies BELOW the fitted characteristic's own floor. A corner value at the STRONG threshold cannot be produced by the session's quasi-steady tyre curve; the flag demonstrably marks beyond-characteristic events. WORDING (author, pre-stated): the STRONG verdict means "anomalous force loss beyond the quasi-steady characteristic (kerb-shown majority per audit; mechanism open otherwise)" -- the flag stays, its claim changes; it no longer reads "unusually deep for this car".
MODERATE (information, no pre-stated case): mixed -- front -0.285 lies below the floor on 5 of 7 sessions (above on JST 29 and qualifying CDR); rear -0.131 lies below the floor on the three sessions whose visited range ends before the peak (Dubai, both Paul Ricard) and above it on the four NBR sessions. On the Paul Ricard and Dubai rear, any negative CS lies beyond the visited part of the curve.
CAVEAT: the thresholds act on corner values (per-phase medians, worst lap, worst phase); the floor is a pointwise property of the fitted curve -- a corner value at STRONG means a sustained phase median deeper than anything the curve produces anywhere in the visited range.
RESIDUAL WORDING UPGRADE (author ruling; dated note to "Deep-tail ledger closed ..." and "Q-SPIKE-AUDIT FINAL LEDGER ...", entries not rewritten): the residual "no specific mechanism shown" reads from now on "incompatible with the session's quasi-steady tyre characteristic; specific mechanism not shown". Basis: the audit's events all lie below CS -0.5, and the curve floors lie at or above -0.34 (front) / -0.33 (rear) even to 30 deg -- every deep event is beyond what the session's fitted characteristic can produce.
[2026-10-05 ADDENDUM, author rulings: inspect_curve_floor.py keep-reproduces -- it re-runs with every threshold re-derivation, so the meaning check rides with the thresholds. UI wording (UI batch): card "anomalous force loss beyond the tyre's quasi-steady characteristic"; the full sentence with the kerb-shown-majority qualifier in tooltip / caption.]

## Event layer: anchor check -- Segers is the lineage for moment-level limit reading; Milliken gives the regime distinction; no source detects events against a fitted characteristic [2026-10-06, read-only; Segers text layer, Milliken RCVD rendered page images (scan, no text layer; PDF page = book page + 34)]

1. SEGERS (Analysis Techniques for Racecar Data Acquisition, 2nd ed.): ANCHOR FOUND for flagging handling moments from logged data. Sec. 7.4 reads oversteer and understeer as moments in the traces (steering corrections, "sudden losses in lateral acceleration" as the car loses and regains grip) and states a magnitude-and-duration rule separating them from surface noise (lateral-g variations smaller than 0.25 g and shorter than 0.3 s attributed to track-surface irregularities). Secs. 7.5-7.6: a balance math channel (understeer angle; attitude velocity r - G_lat / V) is read per moment ("points of interest", "a significant positive peak", located on a track-map overlay) AND, averaged per lap or gated by phase, as a trend statistic -- the moments-vs-tendencies split in practitioner form. Sec. 5.4: brake lock-up detected as a discrete event (spike in the wheel-speed trace and slip ratio). Ch. 17 (17.1-17.3): lap metrics and run charts are the trend side; time / distance during which a gated condition holds (Eqs. 17.4 / 17.5) is the duration measure; location-specific metrics exist.
2. MILLIKEN & MILLIKEN (Race Car Vehicle Dynamics): CONCEPT, no detection from data. Sec. 8.5 (pp. 313-318): under/oversteer belongs to the linear tyre range; limit behaviour is a different physical regime, best described in the driver's terms push (plow) / loose (spin); "sub-limit concepts of stability and control do not easily apply to limit operation" (stall / breakaway analogy). Sec. 11.1 (pp. 374-375): a disturbance is a force action moving the vehicle away from its momentary trim; the vehicle has occasions where it fails to facilitate the driver's intention. Sec. 9.4 (pp. 354-356): g-g envelopes of measured laps (overall usage), no discrete events.
3. DIGEST racing-practice entries (Segers, Milliken; docs/literature_digest.md): nothing on event detection beyond 1 and 2. Chair performance_analysis tooling (internal): no event detection (corner characterisation finds apexes only).
4. LINEAGE LINE (outcome "anchor found"): event flagging after Segers (secs. 7.4-7.6; 5.4 for a discrete-event precedent), event LINE from the session's own fitted characteristic (Pacejka secs. 1.2.2 / 4.3.1 derived), interpretation per Hoffman / Ono / Werner, limit-regime vocabulary per Milliken sec. 8.5. Stated adaptation: Segers flags moments on driver-input and acceleration channels by eye or simple thresholds; the event CHANNEL here (CS against the fitted floor) is SetupTool's own construction.

## Event layer rulings [2026-10-06, author rulings on the proposal OPEN 1-4; EXECUTE]

1. NO minimum duration: CS is already 0.1 s-windowed and 2 Hz filtered; a transferred Segers 0.3 s rule would be a second smoothing on a smoothed signal and an unanchored adaptation (his rule is for raw lateral g). The audit-frozen 0.5 s bridge gap is the only merge logic; min_duration_s exists in config (null) to be ruled again if a real session drowns in micro-events.
2. EVENT LINE = the 0-30 deg curve floor: the event claims "beyond what this tyre characteristic can produce ANYWHERE"; the visited-range floor would make every mild negative an event where the data never reaches the peak (Dubai, Paul Ricard). Caveat: the 0-30 deg floor extrapolates the fitted curve beyond the visited range; its value is the curve's own, not evidence the car visited it.
3. Promoted method AS IS: B C D normalisation is the curve's own scale and makes the floor conservative in CS terms (D4 record: the CS-scale floor sits deeper), so the line errs toward FEWER events -- right for a display-only flag; a per-session conversion would add a second normalisation for no verdict benefit. Mismatch documented in the module header.
4. Thesis consumer scoped to CORNER AND PHASE (the feedback form's resolution): events aggregate to "corner X, phase Y: N events across laps"; per-lap detail stays in card / record for narrative cases (JST 21 / 29). The feedback form gains no lap tags (team instrument, frozen).

## Event layer implemented: limit events as a display + record output class [2026-10-06, author EXECUTE on the rulings above]

- METHOD: per session and axle the event line is the 0-30 deg floor of the session's own Pacejka curve, min (dFy/dalpha) / (B C D) (modules/limit_events.curve_floor, promoted unchanged from inspect_curve_floor -- floors.json reproduced byte-identically through the module). Events = in-corner stretches (canonical brackets, analysis laps, full CS arrays) of CS below the line, merged across gaps < 0.5 s within one corner instance, no minimum duration. Labels from existing machinery only: kerb-affected (near-strike mark on an event sample, or a kerb-mask sample inside the span), recurring (same axle and corner, another analysis lap, minimum within +/-10 m), else single occurrence. ## Lap census: the double outlap is a leading pit-exit fragment on 7 of 24 exports [2026-10-06, read-only, author EXECUTE; diagnostics/inspect_lap_census.py, output diagnostics/lap_census/lap_census.txt]

- METHOD: every unique export's lap-related channels (lap_number, lap_time, lap_distance, ecu_B_speedlimit_en, ecu_speed) through the UNCHANGED production lap classifier (csv_parser._split_laps), beside the raw facts per lap (duration, pit limiter at start / end, lap-distance rise, speed at start / end).
- FINDING: 7 of 24 files carry two out laps -- four Paul Ricard exports (laps 4 + 5), both copies of NBR JST 29 (101 + 102), NBR JST 18 (57 + 58). In every case the FIRST lap is a 15.8-18.2 s fragment with the pit limiter ON AT ITS START AND ITS END, speed 0 -> 39.5 km/h (pit-lane limit), 6-323 m travelled; it is flagged out AND in at once. The real out lap follows (limiter on at start, off at end, full distance). The other 17 files start directly with the real out lap (limiter on at start, off at end) -- no fragment.
- MECHANISM: the lap counter ticks while the car is still in the pit lane (pit-box position before the start / finish or timing line); the parser already merges a TRAILING pit fragment into the in lap but has no leading-fragment rule.
- ANALYSIS IMPACT: none -- in all 7 files the fragment and the real out lap are both outside the analysis laps; the analysis-lap sets, corner detection (valid laps only), fit population, stability exclusion (out / in laps) and every summary are unchanged by a merge. A fix therefore changes the lap table and lap labels only.
- FIX SHAPE (proposed, not implemented, awaiting ruling): mirror of the trailing rule -- merge the FIRST lap into the next one when the pit limiter is on at the first lap's END (Level 3 signal; the fragment ends inside the pit lane), with the duration rule pit_fragment_max_duration_s = 20 s as the fallback without a limiter channel; the merged lap keeps the out flag. SCHEMA: no estimator input and no summary changes -> no bump expected; to be verified by re-running the lap census after the fix (analysis sets identical) and the pipeline goldens.

## Diagnostic 2: what the beta washout does to a held sideslip; input offsets and gain across six exports [2026-10-07, read-only, author work order; numbers only -- verdicts are the author's; Dubai and Le Mans out of scope]

- IMPLEMENTATION FACTS. (1) Kinematic beta: modules/stability_analysis.estimate_sideslip -- d beta/dt = ay / v - r on moving samples (0 otherwise), ONE cumulative sum over the whole file (no per-corner, per-phase or per-lap reset). (2) Drift handling: the same function applies _highpass_filter = Butterworth high-pass, order 4 (BUTTERWORTH_ORDER), run forward and backward (scipy filtfilt, zero phase), cutoff stability_estimation.beta_washout_cutoff_hz = 0.05 Hz (1 / (2 pi fc) = 3.18 s), then sets beta = 0 where not moving. (3) Consumers of the washed-out kinematic beta: tyre_fit_auto.fit_session_pacejka (slip angles of the per-session tyre-curve fit, the seed of the production chain); sideslip_ekf_pacejka (per-sample replacement and EKF re-initialisation whenever the EKF diverges); tyre_fit_auto.resolve_sideslip_beta (session-wide fallback on a degenerate fit or a failed NIS gate). The EKF's own beta (production default ekf_auto_pacejka) is model-based and passes through no washout. Downstream of the chosen beta: estimate_slip_angles -> alpha_f / alpha_r -> estimate_cornering_stiffness (CS) and the Pacejka curve views; estimate_yaw_moment_stability uses beta as the regression predictor; limit_events reads slip.
- WASHOUT ON A HELD BETA (production filter function, 100 Hz synthetic step held, then released): filtered / true at the end of the hold 0.707 (3 s), 0.510 (6 s), 0.432 (10 s); at mid-hold 0.693 / 0.417 / 0.127; mean over the hold 0.698 / 0.448 / 0.235; undershoot of -0.29 / -0.49 / -0.57 before and after the hold (zero-phase filter).
- ONE REAL CORNER (NBR-73-010-026-JDR, lap 27, stable corner C10 = corner number 7): longest run of |ay| >= 10 m/s^2 inside an analysis-lap corner, 5.10 s at mean |ay| 13.9 m/s^2 and mean vx 25.2 m/s. Integrated from the corner instance start (beta = 0 there) over 7.46 s to the end of the run: raw as logged +3.98 deg; raw with the session's straight-line offsets removed (yaw -0.214 deg/s, ay +0.515 m/s^2) -5.31 deg; production kinematic (washout) +0.18 deg; production path (ekf_auto_pacejka, no fallback) +2.02 deg. Ratios to the offset-removed raw: -0.03 (kinematic), -0.38 (production) -- opposite sign, so not a gain. Means over the run: -4.44 / -0.74 / +1.65 deg. The offset removal alone moves the integral by 9.3 deg over 7.46 s at 25 m/s.

## Lineage ruling: the kinematic beta's drift handling [2026-10-07, author ruling]

~~Whole-file integration followed by the 0.05 Hz washout is the chair-pattern drift handling of the kinematic sideslip (author ruling). The washout attenuation measured in diagnostic 2 -- a held sideslip keeps 0.71 / 0.51 / 0.43 of its value at the end of a 3 / 6 / 10 s hold, with opposite-sign dips before and after the hold (zero-phase filter) -- is the justification for evaluating adapted architectures.~~ [SUPERSEDED 2026-10-07, read-only passes 1+2: the chair code consumes beta -- measured, state-estimated or logged depending on the source format -- and skips every beta-dependent computation when it is absent; it contains no kinematic integration, no washout and no IMU compensation. TUM platforms obtain beta from EKF / UKF state estimation over GNSS, several IMUs and wheel speeds, with a Kistler Correvit optical sensor for evaluation (Goblirsch et al. p. 1, p. 3; ~~IFAC 2019 state-estimation paper p. 4;~~ [CORRECTED 2026-10-16, R1: IFAC 2019 struck from this clause -- single gyro platform, no multiple-IMU claim; the "several IMUs" part rests on Goblirsch et al. 2024 only] pages to verify on a full read). SetupTool's beta provision (kinematic seed + Pacejka EKF) is the adaptation forced by the GT3R's single production IMU; the integration and the washout within it are SetupTool-authored and carry their own literature anchors (to be assigned).]

## Beta architecture comparison A / B / B2 / C on two exports [2026-10-07, offline diagnostic, author work order; numbers only -- verdicts are the author's]

- SETUP: diagnostics/compare_beta_architectures.py. A = estimate_sideslip as-is (whole file + 0.05 Hz washout); B = per-session yaw / ay offsets removed, whole-file integration, no washout; B2 = B + 0.005 Hz washout (production filter function); C = B's correction, beta reset to 0 on every CALIBRATION straight and when not moving, no washout. Steering-defined straights split alternately in time: even = CALIBRATION (offsets, C's anchors), odd = VALIDATION (residuals). No metric uses a production beta as reference. ## Beta architectures, round 1 reading and the round-2 correction form [2026-10-07, author work order; records]

- ROUND 1 RESULTS (as recorded by the author's order): the ~4 % gain mismatch between ay / vx and yaw rate dominates the integration error (about 14 deg of sideslip per 360 deg of heading); the offsets alone are secondary. Metric 1 (residual on held-out straights) is a NECESSITY test, and the 0.05 Hz washout satisfies it by construction -- a high-pass drives every slowly varying error toward zero, so A's small straight residual does not by itself show that A is right in corners. A carries post-exit sideslip on Paul Ricard (about -2.8 to -3.4 deg in the 1 s after the C13 exits).
- ROUND 2 CORRECTION FORM (fixed by the author): beta_dot_corr = ay / v - c1 r - c0, with c1 and c0 from the M1 fit (ay / vx against yaw rate) on the CALIBRATION half of the quasi-steady cornering segments of the same export. DECLARED ASSUMPTION: the M1 mismatch is treated as measurement error; the transient response is scaled by c1 as a side effect. (Code comment in diagnostics/compare_beta_architectures.py.)

## Beta architectures, round 2: gain + offset correction and the app's estimator [2026-10-07, offline diagnostic; numbers only -- verdicts are the author's]

- CANDIDATES: A production kinematic (whole file + 0.05 Hz washout); B2 offsets only + 0.005 Hz (round 1); D gain + offset corrected, whole file, no washout; D2 = D + 0.005 Hz; CG gain + offset corrected, reset on calibration straights and at standstill; E = the app's beta (tyre_fit_auto.resolve_sideslip_beta, first return value = sideslip_ekf_pacejka beta_ekf_with_fallback; no session fallback on either export). ## Provenance classes of chair-related material [2026-10-07, author ruling]

(i) Chair internal code, CSVs and README (supplied by the author on 2026-10-03): cited only as "chair performance_analysis tooling (internal)", never committed, never named as files in tracked text. (ii) TUM chair-lineage publications -- Werner (2021, master's thesis), Goblirsch, Weinmann and Betz (IROS 2024, three-dimensional state estimation), the IFAC 2019 state-estimation and localization paper (Roborace), Betz et al. (2023, Journal of Field Robotics, TUM autonomous motorsport): cited normally. (iii) General literature: cited normally, no lineage claim.

## Read-only pass 2: what the chair-related material covers on sideslip and sensors [2026-10-07, read-only; pages marked to verify on a full read]

- Chair internal code (class i): no sideslip estimation, no integration of ay / v - r, no washout, no IMU bias / offset / gain compensation; beta enters as a source channel or as arctan2(vy, vx) from source velocities, and beta-dependent steps are skipped when it is absent (read-only pass 1).
- Sensor setups (class ii): Dallara AV-21 (Goblirsch et al., p. 1 to verify) -- three GNSS receivers with four antennas, three IMUs, four wheel-speed encoders, a Kistler SF-Motion Correvit for evaluation only; Roborace vehicle (IFAC 2019, p. 4 to verify) -- sensor table with a Kistler Correvit SF-II optical speed sensor and an OXTS 4002 GPS; IAC software (Betz et al. 2023, pp. 3 and 6 to verify) -- Novatel GNSS receivers with integrated IMU and dual antennas. Werner (2021, sec. 4.5, p. 70 to verify) lists beta among the logged measurement inputs of the recorded data without naming a sensor.
- Sideslip method (class ii): Goblirsch et al. -- EKF with a point-mass model plus a UKF with a single-track model and Pacejka tyres (pp. 3-4 to verify); a kinematic single-track variant from steering geometry (p. 4), not an integration of ay / v - r. IFAC 2019 -- Kalman-filter velocity estimation, one variant with the optical sensor as input (p. 7 to verify).
- IMU compensation practice: Goblirsch et al. (p. 3 to verify) FIR-filter the IMU signals and correct them by sensor biases identified in stationary tests. This is the concept the straight-based session offset calibration of the diagnostics adapts (straights as the quasi-stationary reference, since the archive holds no stationary test); the calibration exists in diagnostics only, not in production.
- Unreadable for keyword checks: Milliken & Milliken (RCVD PDF, no text layer) and Kiencke & Nielsen (text layer is a font-substitution cipher) -- targeted page checks only when a claim needs them.

## Estimator hardening D3 + D4, phase 1: divergence re-entry and tyre-curve plausibility gate [2026-10-07/08, author decision + implementation; phase 2 (re-derivation, goldens, schema) pending]

- AUTHOR DECISION (2026-10-07, after rounds 1-3 and the literature mining pass): the washed-out kinematic seed and the washout stay as they are -- a documented limitation, explained by Bechtloff's identifiability result (front / rear stiffness pairs with the same understeer gradient give the same low-frequency yaw and lateral-acceleration gains; stiffness fitted separately from an estimated sideslip is biased or diverges in steady state). Two defects are fixed: D3 (divergence resets wrote the kinematic beta into E's state) and D4 (no plausibility gate on the fitted tyre curve). The medium-cost literature options go to the thesis outlook: straight-driving forcing term with smooth scheduling (Selmanaj et al. 2017), roll / gravity compensation of ay (Selmanaj et al. 2017; Rajamani 2nd ed. sec. 15.2; Goblirsch et al. 2024), joint state + stiffness identification (Bechtloff), kinematic / dynamic blending by a steady-state index (Villano et al. 2021; Cheli et al. via Chindamo et al. 2018).
- D3 DESIGN (modules/sideslip_ekf_pacejka.estimate_sideslip_ekf_pacejka), two re-entry cases, the kinematic beta no longer read at all: NIS-window divergence (state in range, measurements disagree) keeps the state and resets P to P0 -- after Goblirsch et al. 2024 (IROS, sec. III-D, adaptive covariance after a signal dropout; p. 3375 to verify) and Rajamani 2nd ed. sec. 14.4.2 (covariance scaling on change detection; pp. 410-411 to verify); hard-bound divergence (|beta| > 15 deg) resets beta to 0, the yaw-rate state to the measurement and P to P0 -- reset to zero, never to another estimate, after Villano et al. 2021 (Meccanica, sec. 3.1 kinematic filter reset; p. 2659 to verify). Hard bound takes precedence. beta_with_fallback keeps its name and carries the post-re-entry state. The session-wide fallback in resolve_sideslip_beta is unchanged. The Dugoff EKF is unchanged.
- D3 FIRST VARIANT FAILED (recorded, not a ship candidate): keeping the state on every divergence, hard-bound ones included, runs away -- at large slip the Magic Formula slope is near zero or negative, the measurements carry no information on beta, and P0 (beta std about 1 deg) is no real widening. |E| reached 4244 deg (NBR-73-010-026-JDR) and 2531 deg (MLA-SE07_US-v2); validation-straight median 0.21 -> 2224 deg and 0.07 -> 627 deg. This is why the hard-bound case resets to zero.
- D4 DESIGN (modules/tyre_fit_auto.plausibility_gate, after the status verdict of fit_session_pacejka): per axle g1 excitation (p1..p99 span of the fit's slip-angle data >= 3.0 deg), g2 implied linear stiffness B*C*D in [30000, 600000] N/rad, g3 numerical argmax of the curve in [3.0, 15.0] deg (no peak in the grid fails). Any failure -> status 'degenerate' with the failed checks in degenerate_reason -> the existing kinematic fallback. The per-axle verdict stays in the in-memory manifest; resolve_sideslip_beta strips it, so the persisted payload shape is unchanged. Bands deliberately wide (garbage catch, not ridge adjudication); magnitudes after Bechtloff Fig. 7.2 (single-track reference stiffnesses 140 / 220 kN/rad passenger car, 230 / 630 kN/rad supersport car; p. 130 to verify) and a team rule of thumb (front peak about 8 deg, personal communication, Proton race engineer) -- both coarse bounds. Config: tyre_fit_auto.min_alpha_span_deg, stiffness_min_npr, stiffness_max_npr, peak_min_deg, peak_max_deg.
- REASON FIELD (ruling 2026-10-07): every degenerate status now carries degenerate_reason, including the sign-check / NIS-miscalibration branch of fit_session and fit_session_pacejka (field already in the payload).
- VALIDATION, D4 dry run on all round-3 fits (diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py; fits recomputed and identical to round 3): NBR A passes (front 149413 N/rad, peak 5.00 deg, span 11.9 deg; rear 253216 N/rad, peak 3.61 deg, span 7.0 deg); NBR D2 rejected (front peak 17.12 deg); NBR B2 rejected (front no peak); PR A passes (front 157269 N/rad, peak 7.45 deg; rear 142125 N/rad, peak 5.81 deg); PR D2 passes; PR B2 rejected (g2 and g3 both axles, 18728 / 12976 N/rad). PEAK-NEAR-BOUND NOTE: the NBR seed-A rear peak sits at 3.61 deg, 0.6 deg above peak_min_deg = 3.0.
- VALIDATION, D3 old vs new (seed A, production fit; fitted curves identical old vs new): NBR fit 'ok' / gate pass -> 'marginal' / gate pass (sweep out of band); diverged samples interim / sweep sum / final 6024 / 68448 / 996 -> 6243 / 81741 / 1666; hard-bound / NIS-window final 0 / 996 -> 5 / 1661; hard-bound re-entries at |ay| >= 5 m/s^2 (mid-corner zero resets) interim 200 -> 548, sweep sum 4 -> 130, final 0 -> 3; R chosen 0.1 / 16 both; max |E| 6.96 -> 14.93 deg; C10 signed means +1.65..+1.86 -> +1.61..+1.74 deg; validation straights 0.21 / 0.26 / 0.28 -> 0.21 / 0.26 / 0.28 deg. PR fit 'marginal' / gate pass -> 'degenerate' (reason: sign check, median gate racing fraction 0.333 < 0.5) / gate warn; diverged 4741 / 78866 / 1909 -> 4816 / 92677 / 3634; hard-bound / NIS-window final 0 / 1909 -> 3 / 3631; mid-corner zero resets interim 59 -> 52, sweep sum 19 -> 68, final 0 -> 2; R 0.1 / 16 -> 1 / 1; max |E| 12.27 -> 14.98 deg; C13 signed means +4.75..+4.98 -> +3.01..+4.96 deg (peaks up to +12.31); validation straights 0.07 / 0.19 / 0.24 -> 0.27 / 0.36 / 0.38 deg. Pre-registered expectation (straights sub-degree) holds on both exports.
- CONSEQUENCE, stated not tuned: under the new re-entry the PR session's fit turns 'degenerate' through the existing sign check, so production would ship the kinematic beta for MLA-SE07_US-v2. A mid-corner zero reset leaves E near zero for about 3 s before it climbs back (PR C13 lap 53 overlay) -- the price of resetting to a bias-free value.
- FULL SUITE after phase 1 (2026-10-08, goldens still old, nothing re-baselined): 3 failed, 605 passed, 9 skipped, 1 xfailed. Failures: test_auto_fit_wiring::test_ekf_auto_pacejka_reproduces_wp_n3_phase3_figures and ::test_forced_fallback_via_impossible_gate_thresholds (both expect Dubai fit status 'ok', now 'marginal'); test_golden_pipeline::test_pipeline_output_matches_golden (Dubai ekf_auto_pacejka, 2265 fields differ; corner 0 apex_3 cs_ratio_f median 0.518 -> -0.201, stability_observed median 387 -> 11 Nm/deg). The Dubai apex shift is large and belongs to the phase-2 review, not to a re-baseline by default.

## Phase 2 step 2, Part 1: the R-sweep band under the corrected re-entry, and the selection redesign [2026-10-11, diagnostics + author ruling]

- STEP 1b EXONERATION (PR, R pinned): sign-check fraction new@1/1 0.333, new@0.1/16 1.000, old@0.1/16 1.000, old@1/1 0.800 -- the PR collapse came from the sweep's pick (1/1), not from the re-entry.
- GRID FINDING (full 25-point grid, new estimator, diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py --step p2s2grid): the yaw NIS exceedance never comes near the band on any grid point. Floors: Dubai 0.263 (0.1/16), NBR-73-010-026-JDR 0.211 (0.3/16), MLA-SE07_US-v2 0.393 (1/4). The ay exceedance reaches [0.03, 0.15] on all three exports. On PR f_yaw is nearly flat in the yaw scale (0.39-0.44 over x1..x16). Sign check per grid point: 1.000 everywhere on Dubai and NBR; on PR below 1 only on rows ay x1 (1/1 0.333, 1/2 0.600, 1/4 0.800, 1/8 0.933) and ay x0.3 (0.800, 0.867, 0.867 at yaw x1, x2, x4).
- CAUSAL CHAIN (author's reading): the old re-entry wrote the kinematic beta into the state on every divergence, which flattered the NIS (yaw exceedance 0.11-0.22 at the old pick); with the honest re-entry the yaw exceedance is 0.21-0.52 everywhere, the joint band is dead, and the old rule then took the grid point "nearest overall" -- an arbitrary pick that inverted the physics on PR.
- RULING (author, 2026-10-11): select R on the ay exceedance only, in [0.03, 0.15], nearest the band centre; physics guard = the sign-check fraction of that grid point's own run >= 0.7 (sign_check_marginal_fraction), else the next-nearest in-band point; no guarded in-band point -> config default R (ay x0.1, yaw x16), status at most 'marginal' with marginal_reason r_sweep_no_in_band / r_sweep_guard_fail. f_yaw stays logged per point; the gross-miscalibration limit (0.5) stays a degenerate trigger. Reasoning: the yaw innovation is dominated by single-track model mismatch, not sensor noise, so a yaw NIS band cannot select R.
- UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS (recorded, not checked): PR's flat f_yaw may come from the NIS-window re-entry resetting P to P0 about 3000 times per run, which could keep the yaw innovation covariance dominated by P rather than R.
- VERIFY (production sweep with the new rule, --step p2s2verify): NBR picks 0.1/16 (f_ay 0.052, sign 16/16) -> status 'ok'; PR: nearest candidate 1/1 FAILS the guard (sign 0.333), next 0.1/1 passes (f_ay 0.071, f_yaw 0.443, sign 15/15) -> status 'ok'; Dubai picks 0.03/1 (f_ay 0.116, sign 11/11) as expected, but its f_yaw there is 0.521 > 0.5, so the retained gross-miscalibration limit makes the Dubai fit 'degenerate' -> production would ship the kinematic beta on Dubai. Package stopped here for a ruling.
- CONTRADICTION AT THE VERIFY (2026-10-11): f_yaw had been demoted from the R selection but was still a degenerate trigger through the gross-miscalibration limit (max of yaw and ay > 0.5). Dubai exposed it: its guarded ay-band pick 0.03/1 has f_yaw 0.521, so the fit turned 'degenerate' and production would have shipped the kinematic beta. RULING (author, 2026-10-11): the gross trigger reads f_ay only (reason text "NIS gross miscalibration (ay): exceedance X > 0.5"); f_yaw is logged per fit and a new SOFT ceiling yaw_mismatch_ceiling = 0.75 can only cap the status at 'marginal' (marginal_reason yaw_mismatch_high), never degenerate -- set well above the observed 0.21-0.52 so it flags only anomalous sessions. The Dugoff path is unchanged.
- VERIFY AFTER THE RULING (--step p2s2verify): Dubai 0.03/1, sign 11/11, f_yaw 0.521 logged, status 'ok'; NBR 0.1/16, 16/16, 'ok'; PR 0.1/1 (1/1 guard-failed at 0.333), 15/15, 'ok'. All as expected.
- PART 2 FRESH CHAIN (inspect_threshold_rederivation.py compute_fresh / counts_fresh, cache_clean_20261011; same eight sessions, seven-session pool, Le Mans information only; all eight through the fresh production chain, none fell back): front p10 -0.784 / p15 -0.548 / p30 -0.265 / p40 -0.184 (n 106); rear p10 -0.677 / p15 -0.571 / p30 -0.323 / p40 -0.213 (n 104). Clean and full populations are identical now -- summarise_corners has excluded kerb-affected CS samples itself since schema 14 (2026-10-07), so the separate clean step no longer changes anything (in the 2026-10-05 caches 14-19 corner-axis values differed per session).
- STABILITY SURGE (stop reason): worst-phase observed stability, pool of seven: negatives 9 -> 34 of 109, p10 +27 -> -389 Nm/deg. Per session negatives old -> new: Dubai 0 -> 10 of 14 (median 342 -> -360), PR outing 25 4 -> 8, PR outing 32 1 -> 4, NBR JST 21 1 -> 6, NBR JST 29 1 -> 2, NBR qualifying CDR 0 -> 2, NBR qualifying MLA 2 -> 2, Le Mans 1 -> 3. Dubai pinned check (scratch run): new estimator at 0.03/1 10 of 14 negative (median -360), at 0.1/16 6 of 14 (median +55) -- part of the surge comes with the re-entry, part with the R pick. Package stopped before any threshold, golden or schema change.

## Phase 2 step 2c: why worst-phase observed stability turns negative under the corrected estimator [2026-10-11, diagnostic, diagnostics/check_estimator_hardening.py --step p2s2c; numbers only, verdict the author's]

- REGRESSION (modules/yaw_stability.calculate_observed_stability): regressand mz_inertial_Nm (Iz x filtered yaw acceleration, beta-free); predictors beta_rad, delta_f_rad, v_mps, ax_mps2, az_mps2; Gaussian-weighted ridge over lap distance s +/- 55 m pooled across laps (sigma 22 m); stability = beta coefficient in Nm/deg. Only beta differs between estimator variants; every other input is identical.
- NOTE ON "OLD" IN THIS RUN: the old EKF ran through the current R selection, so on Dubai it also picked 0.03/1 (old EKF at 0.03/1: C4 -295, C8 -217 negative); the 2026-10-05 cache (old EKF, old pick 0.1/16) had no negative Dubai corner.
- DUBAI C5 (R-sensitive; apex_3): new@0.03/1 -912 +/- 131, new@0.1/16 +338 +/- 144, old +161 +/- 83 Nm/deg (n 1303). Beta mean/std over the window 2.75 / 0.32, 2.51 / 0.30, 2.75 / 0.49 deg; no re-entry inside the phase for new@0.03/1. Same span, no resets -> the slope sign follows a different beta trajectory (a), driven by the R pick.
- DUBAI C9 (negative at both picks; apex_3): new@0.03/1 -564 +/- 91, new@0.1/16 -201 +/- 140, old +348 +/- 100 Nm/deg (n 1815). Beta std 0.74 / 0.58 / 0.71 deg. New: 1 NIS-window reset in the phase, beta step at it 0.36 deg (elsewhere p99 0.92); old: 3 resets with steps 2.5-3.0 deg -- the kinematic injection drew downward spikes through the whole regression window (overlay). ## Class A estimator corrections, rebuild [2026-10-16, R2, author work order; rebuilt from reviewer spec after the laptop loss; goldens stale by design, re-derivation deferred to the final chain]

- STEP 0, chair CS section clipping (docs/literature/cornering_stiffness_estimator.py, read line by line): all recorded facts confirmed. Window [W(i), i] both ends inclusive (slices start:i+1), W(i) the smallest start with max-min of the slip angle strictly below min_slip_angle_interval = 0.02 rad (shrinks while span >= threshold). Sections = whole-signal labels from sign changes of np.diff (np.sign(0) = 0 is its own class, so a zero step starts a section), the turning-point sample keeps the label of the step into it, i.e. it ends the section. Inside each window the sections are clipped exactly to the window (first starts at W(i), last ends at i). Section slope = lstsq line with intercept over the clipped part, NaN below 3 samples (end - start > 1); weight = section weighting function (order 4, [0, 0.02]) of the clipped part's span; NaN slopes drop out of the weighted mean.
- FIXES (Pacejka production path only; Dugoff mirror untouched, removed in R3): (1) #26 CS sections clipped to our window [start, i), re-fitted on the in-window part, span weight from that part, minimum 3 samples (now also for whole sections; was 2). (2) Q scaled by q_reference_rate_hz / grid rate (50 Hz tuning basis; factor exactly 1 at 50 Hz, 0.5 at 100 Hz; first-order discretisation of white process noise, Tier B). (3) EKF NIS divergence window 20 samples -> nis_window_s 0.4 s at the session rate (40 samples at 100 Hz).
