## Dataflow registry rebuild [2026-10-17, R4, author work order; read-only on code, config and tests; registry docs/dataflow_registry.md]

- METHOD (design principle): per-stage auditing missed the CS reference bug (Fix 0) because it lived in a cross-stage seam -- a window carried a reference into later samples while the kerb rule tested the newest sample only. The registry therefore lists, per verdict-relevant quantity (14 quantities + shared sections time grid, moving mask, kerb mask and smear zone, analysis-lap mask, 2 Hz filter, caches), its carried state (where set, where read, lifetime) and, per exclusion rule, whether it acts at the input edge, the carried-state edge or both; every edge where a rule does not act is a numbered finding. Result: no quantity is fully protected; the CS reference edge is the one seam verified closed.

## Spike trace: large negative CS in the traces after R4b [2026-10-17, read-only, author work order; logs diagnostics/output/spike_trace/]

- PROVENANCE: the outing was not named in the work order; the only payload written after R4b is outing 7 "Joel Solution" (NBR JST 29), analysed 2026-10-17 16:01 (R4b commit 15:55), schema 15, sidecar schema 15, no "balance" key; under the current code the app serves it from cache (identity matches). The sidecar's CS and stability arrays equal a fresh current-code run bit for bit: the display was CURRENT, not stale.
- MECHANISM (dominant, all three sessions): SMALL CLEAN REFERENCE. A window with max |alpha| < 0.03 rad and no kerb / smear / off-analysis sample (so Fix 0 admits it) sets a linear reference far below the session's median reference; every CS until the next set divides by it. JST 29 lap 106 C10: references set at t 724.28-724.29 s, front 18046 N/rad (0.19 x median 93999), rear 8595 N/rad (0.05 x median 181382); about 4-5.5 s later, ordinary negative C_alpha (-0.4 to -0.8 x median) gives CS down to -4.3 front and -12.4 rear.

- VERDICT REACH: kerb-affected spikes are graded (display only, greyed), 0 verdict-read, move no median. R1: 0 spikes. Small-reference spikes are verdict-read (JST 29 112 / 130, NBR 10 / 0, PR 76 / 2) and move classifier-read medians (JST 29 4 front + 3 rear, NBR 3 front, PR 2 front + 1 rear). "Other" (strongly negative C_alpha against a normal reference, PR laps 51 / 57; JST 29 lap 105) moves JST 29 1 front, PR 3 front.
- CHAIR COMPARISON: the chair's calculate_cornering_stiffness_ratio (docs/literature/cornering_stiffness_estimator.py) sets the reference the same way (any window under the linear threshold, then a hold) with no plausibility bound on the value, so the small-reference mechanism is inherited from the chair method, not introduced by R3 / R4b. Candidate registry finding R26 (F3, method limitation inherited from the chair): the linear reference has no plausibility bound on its value. Not fixed (read-only cycle).

## R5: reference band rule (R26/R27) + Group 1 fixes [2026-10-17, rebuild, author work order; logs diagnostics/output/r5/]

- BAND RULE (Step A, author ruling 2026-10-17). A clean window may set the CS linear reference only if its stiffness lies inside tyre_fit_auto.stiffness_min_npr / stiffness_max_npr (30000 / 600000 N/rad; the same config keys, not duplicated); outside, the previous reference is held (the Fix 0 mechanism). Basis: the reference is the linear axle stiffness, the quantity the D4 plausibility gate bounds on the fitted curve (B*C*D, magnitudes after Bechtloff Fig. 7.2, D4 2026-10-07); with estimated beta a low-excitation window's slope is ill-determined (Bechtloff pp. 14-16, identifiability); the chair does not bound its reference because it uses measured beta. Deviation class DOMAIN IMPROVEMENT. The rule also removes zero and negative references (new registry finding R27).
- STEP A VALIDATED ALONE (HEAD 4ad2cc2 vs HEAD+StepA; JST 29, NBR-73-010-026-JDR, PR MLA-SE07_US-v2): every recorded spike-follow-up number reproduced; CS and reference arrays equal the recorded simulation bit for bit. ## Q-FIT-SIMPLE: frozen frame [2026-10-18, branch new-laps, read-only; author order, proposal confirmed with rulings 1-4 and EXECUTE]

QUESTION: can a simpler, better-identified Magic Formula parameterisation of the per-session axle fit (fixed E, fixed or bounded C, inverse-density weighting) bring EKF beta and CS into an analysable range, with the rest of the chain unchanged? Variants P (production), P13 (chair tyre-fit start), E0, E0C19, E0C13, E97C13, Pw, E0w; sessions NBR-73-010-026-JDR, MLA-SE07_US-v2 (Paul Ricard), NBR JST 29. Script diagnostics/inspect_fit_simplification.py (rules, predictions and the BEATS-P rule frozen in its header before any run); outputs diagnostics/plots/fit_simplification/. Rulings in PLAN.md queue entry Q-FIT-SIMPLE.

ANCHORS (full citations, pages verified by the author): Goblirsch et al. 2025, IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV), pp. 1115-1119 -- parameter correlation in the Magic Formula fit, E needs sliding data (fix E otherwise), C ~1.3 for lateral force quoted from their references, even data distribution over slip (p. 1117). Rajamani 2012, Vehicle Dynamics and Control, 2nd ed., sec. 13.9, p. 387 -- E changes neither the origin slope nor the peak value. Pacejka 2006, Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics, 2nd ed., pp. 173-174 -- D = peak value, B*C*D = origin slope. Chair performance_analysis tooling (internal): CS-estimator evaluation-plot fit and tyre-fit tool start guesses. Fit variants Tier A (on these anchors); inverse-density weighting Tier B preprocessing, motivated by Goblirsch et al.'s even-distribution remark, not their method.
[2026-10-18 citation precision (author, Q-FIT-LIT): Goblirsch et al. 2025 pages are REVIEWER-VERIFIED in the thesis repo copy (ba-thesis/Pdfs), not in this repo: Table I p. 1116 "To ensure physical behavior ... bound to the following values" B 5-40, C 1.0-3.0, D 0.1-2.0, E -1.0-1.0; p. 1116 C 1.3 for lateral force; p. 1117 shifts removed beforehand, even data distribution; p. 1118 D identifiable once the peak is covered; p. 1119 fixed E "according to the literature", standardized parameters "until sufficient data is acquired". Checked in this repo's Pacejka copy: C 1.3 / Ey -1 in Table 4.1 p. 161 and Table 4.2 p. 196 (hypothetical values), supported by the fitted set Table A3.1 (pCy1 1.193, pEy1 -1.003); Exercise 1.1 p. 15 for D = mu Fz only (it uses E = -3); E > 1 unrealistic, Fig. 4.10 caption p. 175; racing tyres mu 1.5-2, p. 6; axle peak may vanish, p. 14; D peak and BCD origin slope, pp. 173-174. Rajamani sec. 13.9 p. 387 confirmed. Milliken RCVD sec. 2.1 pp. 26-27: load normalisation (lateral force coefficient Fy/Fz). Peak-slip band: Milliken p. 24 (3-7 deg, tyre level) primary, Trzesniowski Bd. 4 (2019) p. 34 second (reviewer-verified).]

BACKGROUND CORRECTIONS (verified in code and records before the design):
- Production fit confirmed: modules/tyre_fit_auto._fit_axle_pacejka, Powell, B, C, D, E free and unbounded, start PACEJKA_START_GUESS = (12.0, 1.9, 8000.0, 0.97), unweighted SSE on fit_mask (base mask x speed window), kinematic alpha_*_filt vs Fy_*_filt. This start is the chair CS-estimator evaluation-plot fit (cornering_stiffness_estimator.create_evaluation_plot, x0 = [12, 1.9, 8000, 0.97], Powell).
- The chair TYRE-FIT tool (tire_slip_observer_pajecejka_fit.py) starts at (10, 1.3, max|Fy|, 0.97) but differs in PROCEDURE, not only in start: scipy least_squares (not Powell), folded |alpha| / |Fy|, smoothed Fz-weighted slip angle, speed-proximity weights in four bands. Variant P13 therefore tests the START only; the chair procedure itself stays closed (Q-CHAIR-AUDIT Part F(d): it degenerates on our population).
- "Fitted C stays 1.88-2.0 on every recorded fit" holds for CHAIR-START PRODUCTION fits only (Dubai 1.940 / 1.982, v3 1.888 / 2.007 -- v3 rear slightly above 2.0; the "(d)" PREMISE CORRECTION line, ~line 24931). Fits from other starts or populations do not stay there: LOSO pool fit front C = 1.26 (~24954); independent fits break C <= 2 on v3 rear, US-v2 rear, Le Mans (~24957); Le Mans rear C = 0.448 from the prior start ((d2) Part 2, START-POINT DEPENDENCE); C 1.05-2.0 under anchoring ((d2) Part 3). Start-point dependence is therefore already on record.
- "E floats about -3.6 .. +0.6": the lower end is the pooled (d2) Part 1 fit (front -3.626, rear -3.548); the highest recorded production E is +0.091 (Dubai front, ~24931). E near 0-0.6 is the Q-PUSH TRIMMED fit (~25409), not production; that reading (only an E near 0-0.6 calmed CS) is Paul Ricard-local and made JST 29 worse.
- Rajamani sec. 13.9 holds at FIXED B, C, D: E does not enter B*C*D or D, but E moves the peak LOCATION. With E fixed in a free fit, B, C and D can re-trade along the recorded B/C/E ridge, so "E0 keeps BCD and D" is a test, not a tautology.
- Asymptote check (E0C19 vs E0C13 prediction): Fy(alpha -> infinity) = D sin(C pi / 2) for any E < 1 -> 0.891 D at C = 1.3, 0.156 D at C = 1.9.

## Q-FIT-LIT: literature-bounded axle fit L -- rulings [2026-10-18, branch new-laps, author rulings and EXECUTE for records, census, Step 1]

PRINCIPLE (author): fit choices are decided by physical bounds and literature practice on measured data, never by comparing CS verdicts or proxies with production (DECISIONS "Production is the candidate, not the standard"). CS is reported for information only; thresholds re-derive afterwards per the standing rule.
METHOD L (Tier A; deviation class FORCED ADAPTATION -- the chair fits all four Magic Formula parameters on measured beta; with an estimated beta and no sliding data the curve shape is not identified, Q-FIT-SIMPLE WHAT STANDS 2-4): per axle f(alpha) = Fy_axle / Fz_axle (load-normalised; Milliken RCVD sec. 2.1 pp. 26-27; D = mu Fz, Pacejka Exercise 1.1 p. 15); ~~C = 1.3 fixed (Goblirsch et al. 2025 p. 1116; Pacejka Table 4.1 p. 161);~~ [2026-10-18, author ruling Q-OBS-REENTRY fix, post-result and mechanism-motivated: C = 1.0 in mode literature_bounded, see "Q-OBS-REENTRY fix".] E = -1 fixed (Goblirsch p. 1119 fixed E "according to the literature"; Pacejka Table 4.1 p. 161, Table 4.2 p. 196 hypothetical values, fitted MF-Tyre set Table A3.1 pCy1 1.193 / pEy1 -1.003; E > 1 unrealistic, Fig. 4.10 caption p. 175); B in [5, 40] and D = mu in [0.1, 2.0] (Goblirsch Table I p. 1116, "to ensure physical behavior"; racing tyres mu 1.5-2, Pacejka p. 6). Inverse-density weights on signed alpha (Tier B, implementing Goblirsch p. 1117 "even data distribution"; their method unspecified). Fz(t) from the existing measured cascade, 2 Hz order-4 zero-phase filtered like Fy and alpha (Tier B; quasi-steady effective axle curve, Pacejka sec. 1.2.2 p. 14). Front force in the tyre frame, Goblirsch Eq. 13, in the fit population and the EKF. Full Goblirsch citations: frozen-frame note of Q-FIT-SIMPLE (reviewer-verified in ba-thesis/Pdfs).
IMPLICATION (analytic, C = 1.3 and E = -1): the peak lies where 2 B alpha - arctan(B alpha) = tan(pi / 2.6), i.e. alpha_peak = 1.86 / B rad; B in [5, 40] spans 21.3-2.7 deg; the D4 peak band 3-15 deg needs B in [7.1, 35.5]. With K = 1.3 B mu the normalised origin slope, alpha_peak = 2.42 mu / K -- where the data do not reach the peak, mu is an extrapolation (Goblirsch p. 1118).
LIMITATIONS (recorded with the ruling): limited-slip differential torque not modelled; sideslip estimated, not measured; Goblirsch et al. smooth with a Savitzky-Golay filter, SetupTool keeps the chair's 2 Hz order-4 zero-phase Butterworth.

## Q-FIT-LIT: verification cycle -- rulings [2026-10-18, branch new-laps, author rulings and EXECUTE]

HYPOTHESES (enrichment = event share / base share on JDR and JST 29; US-v2 has no events): H-OBS CONFIRMED (event share 1.00 vs base 0.37 / 0.41, enrichment 2.74 / 2.46); H-KERB MIXED (0.90 / 1.76); H-LOWV MIXED (1.09 / 0.83); H-LOC MIXED (1.91 / 2.19; locked corners on JDR 10, on JST 29 6). OUTCOME (frozen): impact >= 1 % -> the mechanism with evidence; a literature-anchored fix proposal next turn, no fix this cycle. MECHANISM: once the observer's slip passes the curve peak, the curve's slope is near zero or negative, the lateral-acceleration measurement no longer constrains sideslip (loss of observability on the extrapolated branch; Farrelly & Wellstead 1996, Repka et al. 2025, Bertipaglia et al. 2024 as cited by the author), and the state drifts to the 15 deg bound; under L the flatter post-peak branch (C 1.3, E -1) and the peak beyond the data let this happen about 3.5-4x as often as under production on NBR. Base-rate caveat: the H-OBS test uses the kinematic p99 as visited range; the observer exceeds it in the 0.5 s window on 37-42 % of all base samples, so the enrichment (2.5-2.7) rather than the event share carries the evidence.

## Q-OBS-REENTRY fix: C = 1.0 in mode literature_bounded -- ruling [2026-10-18, branch new-laps, author ruling and EXECUTE; POST-RESULT, MECHANISM-MOTIVATED]

MECHANISM (recorded, H-OBS confirmed in "Q-OBS-REENTRY"): the observer's slip runs past the extrapolated peak; on the falling post-peak branch a_y no longer constrains beta and the single-track model is open-loop unstable (Guiggiani 2023 p. 308: instability only if N_beta < 0) -> drift to the hard bound; CS impact 16-24 % on NBR.
RULING: mode literature_bounded uses C = 1.0 (was 1.3). Anchors (reviewer-verified, ba-thesis/Pdfs): Voser et al. 2010 p. 322 (no peak evident -> no post-peak drop modelled); Pacejka 2006 p. 14 (axle peak may vanish through load transfer; checked in this repo) and p. 174 (D is the peak only for C >= 1; checked in this repo: "D represents the peak value (with respect to the central x-axis and for C >= 1)"); Rao et al. 2006 p. 42 (C = 1.0 where no post-peak drop is observed); Goblirsch et al. 2025 Table I (C lower bound 1.0). With C = 1.0 and E = -1 the curve is monotonic with asymptote D: the drop our data never show is not modelled. mu = asymptotic grip, still an extrapolation and flagged.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FINAL CHAIN (not acted on now): the limit-event curve floor and the STRONG meaning sentence refer to the curve's minimum slope; for a monotonic curve that floor is 0, so the meaning becomes "CS < 0" -- to be re-worded in the final chain.
PRODUCTION'S OWN RE-ENTRIES (CS impact 1.6-4.7 %, kerb-enriched 3.12 / 5.02) recorded; out of scope (production is being replaced).
CITATION SCOPE: Farrelly & Wellstead 1996 p. 552 is cited only for "the kinematic observer is parameter-free"; the reading "a physical-model observer is only reliable in the linear region" stays unverified and is not cited.
C / E SENSITIVITY BAND: named by the author as queued and to centre on C = 1.0; no definition of it is on record in PLAN.md, DECISIONS.md or thesis_notes.md (searched 2026-10-18) -- to be specified by the author.

## Sources read 2026-10-18 (reviewer-verified, ba-thesis/Pdfs) and the C / E sensitivity band [recorded 2026-10-19, author]

- Farroni 2016, T.R.I.C.K. (Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 72-73, 808-831): lateral velocity from an optical sensor (p. 811); no sensor-free drift remedy (p. 814); the offset / gain correction steps (pp. 816-819) are the family already tested in Q-SEED -> seed construction stays CLOSED (the open trigger of 2026-10-18 is resolved); roll / gravity effects neglected (p. 818).
- Farroni et al. 2018, TRIP-ID (Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 102, 1-22): the peak is bounded to the maximum acquired forces (p. 5); the abscissa of the peak is bounded from known models when the limit is not reached (p. 7).
- Alagappan et al. 2015 (Vehicle System Dynamics 53(2), 154-178): the peak must be covered if C is not fixed (p. 155); C-D-E interplay without a peak (p. 156).
- Rao et al. 2006 (Vehicle System Dynamics 44(1), 33-63): C fixed as practice (p. 41); C = 1.0 where no post-peak drop (p. 42). Goblirsch et al. 2025's attribution "fitting C improves" to this source is NOT supported by it.
- Voser et al. 2010 (Vehicle System Dynamics 48 S1, 317-336): no friction estimate from a curve without saturation (p. 322).
- Acosta Reche et al. 2018 (Proc. IMechE Part D 232(14), 1883-1930): 70-90 % excitation needed for +/-10 % friction accuracy (pp. 1905, 1916); conservative grip underestimate as practice (p. 1904); kinematic drift under sustained body slip (p. 1884).
C / E SENSITIVITY BAND (queue item, definition, author 2026-10-19): refits with C in {1.0, 1.3, 1.6} (Rao et al. 2006 p. 42 range) and E in {-1, 0, 1} (Goblirsch et al. 2025 Table I); per axle K, in-range curve change and mu; reported, not selected.
C = 1.0 RESULT stands as reported ("Q-OBS-REENTRY fix: C = 1.0 -- result"): residual events 14 on JDR on the flat asymptote, corners 3 / 14 / 18; US-v2 rear mu at the 2.0 bound -> fallback. SHAPE CHANGES STOP HERE: no further C / E variation as a fix (author, 2026-10-19).

## Q-NIS-RESET: does a NIS-window covariance reset change the CS slope? [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author order and EXECUTE]

QUESTION: a hard-bound reset sets beta to 0 (a state break; stays in the observer-reset mask regardless). A NIS-window reset keeps the state and resets P to P0 only; afterwards the gain is large and beta is pulled towards the measurements quickly. Does that move alpha inside a CS window enough to change the windowed OLS slope?
DECLARED CRITERION (written before the run, DECISIONS.md): run A = shipped EKF L, run B = the same final observer configuration (same fit, same R) with the NIS-window reset disabled, hard-bound reset active. Per verdict CS window marked only by NIS-window resets, per axle, |CS_A - CS_B| / |CS_A| with CS the windowed OLS slope over the same Fy and the same [start, i) window. p95 <= 0.10 on every axle of every session -> NIS-window resets do not materially change the CS and the mask scope becomes hard-bound re-entries only; otherwise the mask stays as ruled and the excluded share is a stated limitation. 0.10 is a declared Tier-B tolerance, not tuned. Windows in which run B hits a hard bound are counted as affected and reported separately.
RESULT (2026-10-19, diagnostics/inspect_nis_reset_effect.py, outputs diagnostics/plots/fit_lit/nis_reset/): tests/test_tyre_fit_literature.py 8 passed; production path BIT-IDENTICAL with the flag at its default (diagnostics/output/fit_lit/inactive_check_nisflag.log). Window reproduction against C_window exact (max rel dev 0). Relative slope difference |CS_A - CS_B| / |CS_A| on NIS-only windows (front / rear):
- JDR: n NIS-only 25,073 / 25,250; run B hard-bound in 56 / 27; p50 0.370 / 0.409, p95 3.49 / 3.67, p99 14.5 / 13.4. Run B gate pass 0.090, hard-bound re-entries 1 (run A 1).
- JST 29: n 8,633 / 9,492; run B hard-bound in 1,765 / 1,965; p50 0.682 / 0.691, p95 3.68 / 3.95, p99 9.85 / 20.1. Run B gate pass 0.078, re-entries 62 (run A 7).
- US-v2: n 20,301 / 20,367; run B hard-bound in 1,155 / 1,228; p50 0.410 / 0.454, p95 2.57 / 2.80, p99 8.36 / 11.2. Run B gate pass 0.058, re-entries 134 (run A 94).
BRANCH: p95 > 0.10 on every axle of every session -> the mask stays as ruled (hard-bound or NIS-window); the excluded share (28-47 % of verdict CS samples) is a stated limitation. Not applied to code in this step (nothing to change).
READING (labelled): run B differs from run A along the whole trajectory, not only inside the window, so the metric measures how strongly the CS slope depends on the reset policy, not the local effect of one reset; either way the slope in these windows is not robust to it. Without the NIS-window reset, hard-bound re-entries rise (JST 29 7 -> 62, US-v2 94 -> 134): the covariance reset also keeps the state off the bound.

## Q-OBS-DERIVE: rulings and anchor check for deriving the observer Q and reset trigger on fit L [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author rulings]

RULING: observer-reset mask scope = hard-bound re-entries only (Q-NIS-CONTROL rule (b): the CS sensitivity to observer policy is general, not reset-specific); implementation in a later step.
ANCHOR CHECK (read in docs/literature; recorded as found): the three sources cited for the re-entry rule in sideslip_ekf_pacejka do not cover a NIS window/fraction trigger or a P0 reset on divergence.
- Goblirsch et al. 2024 (IROS) sec. III-D p. 3375: filters "tuned individually to achieve their best performance" (no Q procedure); per-sample Mahalanobis-distance outlier rejection, measurement clamped beyond a limit; after a GNSS dropout the MEASUREMENT covariance decays linearly back to the reported GNSS standard deviation (Fig. 4). Related work p. 3372: adaptive Q/R, innovation-adaptive filter.
- Rajamani 2012 (2nd ed.) sec. 14.4.2 pp. 410-412, RLS friction estimation: forgetting factor (p. 410); CUSUM change detector a_t = max(a_{t-1} + |e_t| - d, 0), a_0 = 0, alarm a_t > h (Eqs. 14.24-14.25, p. 411), drift d high-passes small errors; on alarm the entries of P are increased by a constant factor until the error is small and a_t returns to 0; cites Gustafsson (2000) for the same scheme in parallel with a Kalman filter.
- Villano et al. 2021 (Meccanica 56) sec. 3.1 p. 2659: kinematic filter Q includes the sensor noise covariances; vy forced to zero when |r| is small (observability reset). Dynamic filter Q = diag(sigma_vy^2, sigma_r^2), R = diag(sigma_r,m^2, sigma_ay,m^2), Eqs. 28-29 p. 2661; tuning method not found.
- Bechtloff (dissertation) ch. 5: Q as diagonal of physically meaningful process-noise variances with a speed-dependent element, Eq. 5.16 p. 81; stationary Riccati analysis of Q/R, Eqs. 5.49-5.52 p. 92.
FROZEN FRAME (author rulings, before any number): Q derived physically per session from the fit-L model error (anchors Villano Eqs. 28-29, Bechtloff Eq. 5.16; whiteness / NIS reported only); trigger = Rajamani p. 411 change detector on NIS, d = 2 (E[NIS], df 2), only h derived (1-D grid on the derive split; objective fewest hard-bound re-entries; ~~constraint alarm time share on validation straights <= 0.05, declared Tier B~~ [2026-10-19 correction: ill-defined for one-shot alarms; replaced by mean time between alarms on validation straights >= 10 s, see 'h derivation for the change-detector trigger']); action on alarm P -> P0 (declared adaptation of Rajamani's constant-factor boost, removes one free parameter); acceptance = all existing gates on every check session and straight-line beta median < 1 deg (re-entries, whiteness reported only); derive split NBR 5, 20, 46, 54, 61, 69 + Le Castellet 25 (US-v1), check split NBR 10, 29, 53, 59, 63, 70 + Le Castellet 32 (US-v2), h only; new keys fit-L-only, production bit-identical. Literature to obtain: Bar-Shalom et al. 2001, Mehra 1970, Gustafsson 2000.
CORRECTION: Q-NIS-CONTROL item 4 compared the window span with the chair's linear-reference threshold (0.021 rad), a different quantity; span floor 0.020 rad in both codes (chair min_slip_angle_interval). Struck above with a dated note.
SESSION IDENTITY (file header, census rule): NBR-73-010-026-JDR-26.07.01.1029.txt is OutingNumber 10, driver JDR, session 1, track NBR -> NBR outing 10, in the analysis set (check split). All three sessions used so far (outings 10, 29, 32) are check sessions.
Q-PHYS RESULT (2026-10-19, diagnostics/inspect_q_phys.py, outputs diagnostics/plots/q_phys/; 14-session analysis set, fit L run up to both axle fits, no observer; B and mu_demo of outings 10, 29, 32 reproduce the earlier fit-L runs exactly). On the joint fit population:
- Force residual Fy - mu Fz f(alpha) at the KINEMATIC slip angle (the fit's own population): front SD 2123-3824 N (normalised 0.36-0.71), rear 5593-7638 N (normalised 0.56-0.78); mean negative on both axles (front -125 to -756 N). Correlation front / rear residual 0.79-0.92.
- Autocorrelation time (integral to the first zero crossing): front 1.50-1.91 s, rear 1.62-2.08 s; against 0.166 s for the 2 Hz zero-phase CS filter alone (filtered white noise). The residual is strongly time-correlated on corner time scales.
- Propagated sample-wise, jointly: e_beta_dot = (dFy_f + dFy_r) / (m Vx) SD 0.179-0.222 rad/s (p50 |e| 0.082-0.121), tau 1.52-1.97 s; e_r_dot = (a dFy_f - b dFy_r) / Iz SD 1.75-2.04 rad/s^2, tau 1.23-1.93 s; corr(e_beta_dot, e_r_dot) -0.62 to -0.86.
- Per-step Q in the config convention (50 Hz reference), current q_beta_var 9.632e-7 rad^2, q_yaw_rate_var 2.408e-7 (rad/s)^2: held over one step (sigma^2 dt^2) Q_beta 1.28e-5 to 1.98e-5 (x13-21), Q_r 1.23e-3 to 1.66e-3 (x5100-6900); equivalent white noise (2 sigma^2 tau dt) Q_beta 2.25e-3 to 3.89e-3 (x2300-4000), Q_r 0.173-0.253 (x7.2e5-1.05e6). Per-session values in the run log.
READING (labelled, not ruled): (1) the residual is measured at the kinematic slip angle, so it carries the kinematic beta error as well as the tyre-curve error; the high front / rear correlation and the corner-length correlation time fit a common slip-angle error (a beta error shifts both axle slip angles equally), so this Q is an upper estimate of the tyre-model error the observer sees. (2) With tau about 100 times the 0.02 s reference step the error is close to a bias over a corner: the held-over-step value is the exact one-step variance but makes the filter under-predict drift over several steps; the equivalent-white value is right only for horizons much longer than tau. (3) The same force error enters the ay measurement equation, so process and measurement noise are correlated, and R_ay is already derived from those innovations.

## Q-PHYS rulings and the change-detector trigger (fit L) [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author rulings and EXECUTE]

Q-PHYS OUTCOME: the fit-L residual at the kinematic slip angle is dominated by a common slip-angle error (front/rear correlation 0.79-0.92, corner-length correlation time 1.2-2.1 s, same-sign mean); the EKF slip angle is circular. Q is therefore not derivable from this data without a reference sideslip measurement (cf. Farroni et al. 2016 p. 811, Correvit; author citation, to verify). The held-over-step values of diagnostics/inspect_q_phys.py are recorded as a per-session UPPER BOUND for Q (q_beta 1.28e-5 to 1.98e-5 rad^2, q_r 1.23e-3 to 1.66e-3 (rad/s)^2 per step at 50 Hz); the equivalent-white values are dropped (they overstate over the filter's correction horizon).
RULING: Q stays at the current values as a documented Tier B parameter (fit-L keys l_q_beta_var 9.632e-7, l_q_yaw_rate_var 2.408e-7, copied). Provenance: hand-set base (0.1 deg)^2 and (0.05 deg/s)^2 per step, scaled by 0.3162 from the WP-S5b ratio sweep of the linear Kalman observer on the Dubai sample. Not claimed as derived. Diagonal form (Villano et al. 2021 Eq. 28); the off-diagonal is not estimable for the same reason.
~~RULING: Q is tested, not tuned. In the final chain, after the thresholds are re-derived on the baseline, Q is varied from /10 up to the per-session upper bound (grid declared then) and the verdict-class flip rate per corner phase is reported.~~ [2026-10-19: superseded -- declared post-result reopen of the Q policy, see 'Q-UPPER frame'.]
LIMITATIONS: (1) correlated process and measurement noise -- the force-model error enters both the beta_dot process equation and the ay measurement equation, and R_ay is derived from the same innovations; the Kalman filter assumes them independent. (2) The model error is slow and corner-correlated, so the white process-noise assumption is violated.
OUTLOOK (out of scope): model the slow error as extra filter states (Bechtloff ch. 5 Eqs. 5.15-5.16, random-walk stiffness term; Gelb 1974 to obtain).
IMPLEMENTED (fit L only): observer-reset mask = hard-bound re-entries (new EKF output hard_bound_mask); change-detector trigger after Rajamani 2012 sec. 14.4.2 (Eqs. 14.24-14.25, citing Gustafsson 2000): a_t = max(a_{t-1} + NIS_t - d, 0), alarm when a_t > h, action P -> P0 with the state kept, a_t back to 0 after every reset (the reset restarts P, so earlier evidence no longer describes the current covariance; without it every sample while a_t stays above h would reset P again -- the one-shot reset replaces Rajamani's boost that lasts while the alarm holds); d = 2 (E[NIS], df 2); h = placeholder 50, "to be derived"; fit-L default trigger stays the NIS window until h is derived. Docstring anchors corrected to what each source says.
RESULT (2026-10-19): tests/test_tyre_fit_literature.py 11 passed (new: change-detector step on a synthetic NIS sequence, mask hard-bound only, change-detector reset rule replayed on real data); production path BIT-IDENTICAL on three sessions (diagnostics/output/fit_lit/inactive_check_cd.log); test_stability.py exit 0. Context for h (JST 29, shipped L run, base mask): NIS mean 4.687, median 1.714 -- heavy-tailed, so against d = 2 the statistic drifts upward on average; the placeholder h = 50 gives 3911 alarms (24 hard-bound resets) against 654 NIS-window resets.

## h derivation for the change-detector trigger (fit L) [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author EXECUTE]

FRAME (written before any number): (1) CORRECTION -- the straight-line constraint "alarm time share on validation straights <= 0.05" of the frozen frame was ill-defined for one-shot alarms (one alarm is one sample, so 0.05 allowed an alarm every 20 samples; reviewer's spec defect). Replaced by: mean time between alarms on validation straights >= 10 s (declared Tier B; the average run length is the standard false-alarm measure of CUSUM detectors, Page 1954 as cited by Rajamani 2012 p. 411, to verify). The full curve over h is reported. Validation straights = the odd-indexed steering-defined straights (steering_straights in diagnostics/inspect_kinematic_inputs.py, split as in check_estimator_hardening.py). (2) Objective unchanged: fewest hard-bound re-entries summed over the derive split; tie -> fewer alarms. (3) R is held at the cached picks (made with the NIS-window trigger) during the grid -- declared simplification; the acceptance run re-derives R through the full chain. (4) The one-shot reset of a_t is part of the declared adaptation of Rajamani's detector. Grid h = 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200; derive split NBR 5, 20, 46, 54, 61, 69 and Le Castellet 25. ## Q-UPPER: observer process noise at the Q-PHYS upper bound, and the fit-L fallback of outings 59 / 70 [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author STEP]

READING OF THE h DERIVATION (author): no pick; evidence that the filter is overconfident -- the hard-bound objective falls monotonically with more covariance resets, and the mean NIS (about 4.7 on JST 29) lies well above E[NIS] = 2.
DECLARED POST-RESULT REOPEN OF THE Q POLICY: "Q is tested, not tuned" is superseded (struck in the Q-PHYS entry). Q now matters for observer health, not only for verdicts. Candidate: Q = the per-session held-over-step UPPER BOUND from Q-PHYS (Level 2, session measurement). Hypothesis (before any number): with this Q the hard-bound objective becomes flat over h and the trigger becomes a rare safety net. Literature context: Rajamani 2012 pp. 410-411, the trade-off between tracking ability and noise immunity.
FRAME (before any number): derive split, full chain per point (R re-derived); trigger points change detector h = 400, 800, 1600, 3200 and hard-bound only (no soft reset); NIS-window trigger at Q-UPPER as reference line only. Straight constraint corrected: all steering-defined straights (both halves), pooled over the derive split, mean time between alarms >= 10 s; the odd / even split remains for beta validation. Selection: among h meeting the constraint, re-entries within 10 % of the minimum count as tied, then fewest alarms; if the objective still falls monotonically to the smallest h -> report and wait.
RULING, CS ON LOAD-NORMALISED FORCE (implementation later): CS estimated on Fy / Fz of the axle. Basis: cornering stiffness is defined at constant vertical load; Milliken pp. 26-27 (load-normalised lateral force); consistent with fit L and the K gate. Declared adaptation beyond the chair estimator (Fy in N), enabled by measured axle loads. Intended reference band Pacejka 2006 p. 6, 6-30 per rad, to be checked against data before adoption. The dip reduction (Q-DIPS: 65-66 % fewer ratios below -1) is a consequence, not the reason.
RULING, PHYSICS FLOOR AS A LABEL (implementation in the final chain): a CS ratio below -0.53 (steepest post-peak slope of a pure-lateral Magic Formula at C = 3.0, the Goblirsch et al. 2025 Table I upper bound, E in [-1, 1], Pacejka 2006 p. 175) is labelled "not lateral saturation", never deleted.

## Observer finalisation for fit L (Q-UPPER in the chain, hard-bound only, R_ay noise floor) [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author EXECUTE]

RULINGS (before implementation):
1. Q-UPPER ADOPTED: Q per session = the held-over-step upper bound from the fit-L residual (Level 2 session measurement). Evidence: hard-bound re-entries 1-4 against 27-246 on the derive split, all gates pass. Stated property: NIS median 0.5-0.75 below the chi-square df-2 median 1.39 -- the filter is mildly conservative, consistent with Q being an upper bound.
2. TRIGGER "HARD-BOUND ONLY": admissible and selected under the frame tie rule (tied with h 1600 on re-entries, fewer alarms). With a realistic noise model no ad-hoc covariance reset is needed. The change-detector and NIS-window code paths become unused in fit L and are scheduled for removal in the cleanup round.
3. YAW STATE FOLLOWS THE GYRO (Q_r upper bound): accepted. The gyro is the most trusted signal (Level 3); yaw rate as an input is common in sideslip observers (Villano et al. 2021, kinematic filter, sec. 3.1). Stated loss: the yaw-moment equation no longer constrains the front/rear force balance. Tested in the final-chain robustness check (point: Q-UPPER beta, current Q_r).
4. R_ay NOISE FLOOR: the R_ay grid is extended downward; R_ay may not go below the measured ay sensor-noise variance of the session (Level 2): variance of ay minus its 2 Hz zero-phase low-pass on the steering-defined straights.
5. K BAND UNCHANGED at 30 per rad (no post-result move). Outings 59 and 70 fail D4-L g2 front by 1.1 % and ship the kinematic fallback; reported as "plausibility gate triggered" and excluded from the EKF-based verdict analysis (the thresholds encode one estimator's distribution). PENDING: author confirmation that no key driver feedback depends on them.

## R floor refinement and R_yaw from the measured noise (fit L) [2026-10-19, branch new-laps, author EXECUTE]

A5 CLOSED (author): the thesis analysis set comes from a separate clean data package (driver feedback, setup changes, at least 3-4 flying laps, driver and tyre age known); the current 14 sessions are the development set. No key driver feedback depends on outings 59 / 70; they stay "plausibility gate triggered" and out of the EKF-based verdict analysis. Physical reading (author context): 59 is likely a tyre run, 70 is qualifying -- fresh tyres give a high demonstrated mu and put K just above 30. Known edge case for the package: fresh-tyre sessions may sit at the upper K edge; that is decided then, with tyre age known.
NOISE-FLOOR DEFINITION (Tier B): signal content above 2 Hz on the steering-defined straights counts as measurement noise for the single-track model -- the model has no vertical or vibration dynamics, and R covers what the model cannot predict. 2 Hz is consistent with the chair CS filter and the Fz filter. The floor is computed on the exact signal the EKF consumes. The floor value itself is an R_ay candidate; a pick never lands on a grid point above the floor when the sweep prefers lower.
R_yaw: no longer swept in fit L; R_yaw = the session's yaw-rate noise floor (same method, Level 2). Reason: with Q_r at the upper bound the yaw state follows the gyro, and the sweep picks sat at grid ends on 11 of 14 sessions. Adopted only if all gates pass on every session.
LOAD CHAIN (facts from the read-only report): per wheel, Fz = strain-gauge damper force (log_dms_dam_*, logged in N; NBR event zero of about 58.4-59.5 kN per corner subtracted, Level 2) x motion ratio as a function of wheel travel (car_data table, Level 4) + ARB term (left-right travel difference x the car_data rate, damper motion ratio as proxy, blade position fallback 4) + unsprung lateral transfer + roll-centre (geometric) lateral transfer (Level 1 constants); axle Fz = sum of the wheels, 2 Hz zero-phase filtered. Spring rates, damper and bump-stop curves are not used (the force is measured). OPEN: the bump-rubber position relative to the gauge (to verify at the car); the ARB blade position from the setup sheet per session in the final package (Level 2) instead of fallback position 4.
SIGNALS: the measurement update reads state["ay_mps2"] = log_acc_y x 9.81 and state["yaw_rate_radps"] = sclu_yaw_rate x yaw_rate_to_radps, both linearly interpolated onto the common grid (100 Hz) by prepare_vehicle_state and otherwise unfiltered (no channel correction applies to them); both floors are computed on exactly these arrays.
IMPLEMENTED (fit L only, production bit-identical): tyre_fit_auto._measurement_noise_floors (ay and yaw rate, replaces _ay_noise_floor; manifest noise_floors); the ay floor value inserted into the R_ay grid (grid still continued below it), pick location floor / interior / top edge plus floor_binding (the sweep without the floor would pick lower); R_yaw = the yaw-rate floor, no R_yaw sweep in fit L; the no-in-band default never undercuts either floor.
CHECKS: tests/test_tyre_fit_literature.py 17 passed (new: floors equal an independent computation on the consumed arrays; the floor is on the R_ay grid and is the pick when the sweep prefers lower; R_yaw equals the yaw-rate floor at every grid point and in the final run); production path BIT-IDENTICAL (diagnostics/output/fit_lit/inactive_check_rfloor.log); test_stability.py exit 0.
